1.30.s:
sumantaruvāca
nimbamayamaṅguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kṛtvā nityadhūpagandhādibhirarcayitvā pracchannaṃ śirasi baddhvā gacchet . .
sarvajanapriyo bhavati . śvetārkamūlāṅguṣṭhamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kṛtvā dhūpādibhirarcayitvā sarvānvarṇānvaśamānayati ..
śvetacandanamaṅguṣṭhamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kṛtvā puṣpagandhādibhirarcayitvā śuklacaturthyāmaṣṭamyāṃ vā baliṃ kuryādaṣṭasahasraṃ juhuyāddadhnā pāyasena rājānaṃ vaśamānayati .
raktacandanamayaṃ gaṇapatimaṅguṣṭhamātraṃ kṛtvā bhautikaṃ baliṃ dadyāddadhimadhughṛtāhutīnāṃ gaṇapatimaṣṭasahasraṃ juhuyādātmaprāpikāṃ prajāṃ vaśamānayati . raktakaravīramūlāṅguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kārayet . .
raktapuṣpagandhopahārairbaliṃ dadyāt . tilalavaṇaghṛtenāṣṭasahasraṃ juhuyāt . daśagrāmānvaśamānayati . .
śvetakaravīrāṅguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kṛtvā tilapiṣṭadadhighṛtakṣīraharidrāmiśreṇāṣṭasahasraṃ
juhuyādveśyāṃ vaśamānayati . .
aśvatthamūlāṅguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kṛtvā gandhapuṣpadhūpabaliṃ dattvā śataṃ juhuyācchatruṃ vaśamānayati . .
arkamūlāṅguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kṛtvā gandhapuṣpadhūpabalīn dadyāt .
tindukāṣṭaśataṃ juhuyācchatruṃ vaśamānayati . .
bilvamūlamayamaṅguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kṛtvā gandhapuṣpadhūpārcitaṃ kṛtvā trimadhvaktānāmaṣṭasahasraṃ juhuyādrājāmātyānvaśamānayati . .
śirasi dhūpāndhṛtvā gacchedrājadvāraṃ vigrahe jayo bhavati .
hastidantamṛttikāmayamaṅguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kārayet . .
gandhapuṣpadhūpārcitaṃ kṛtvā. kṛṣṇacaturthyāṃ nagno bhūtvābhyarcayet .
sapta vārāñjapennityaṃ 1 nārīṇāṃ subhago bhavati . .
vṛṣabhaśṛṅgamṛttikāṅguṣṭhamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kārayet .
gandhapuṣpārcitaṃ kṛtvā gugguludhūpaṃ dadyādghoṣapatiṃ vaśamānayati . .
atha vā valmīkamṛttikāṃguṣṭhaparvamātraṃ gaṇapatiṃ kārayet .
kaṭukatailena pratimāṃ lepayet . .
unmattakakāṣṭhenāgniṃ prajvālyāhutīnāmaṣṭasahasraṃ juhuyāttilasarṣapamiśreṇa sarvadhūpaṃ dadyāttrikaṭukena lepayet . .
agarudhūpaṃ dadyādrājānaṃ vaśamānayati . pareṣāṃ ca vallabho bhavati . raktacandanenātmānaṃ dhūpayetsubhago bhavati . .
oṃ gaṇapataye vakratuṇḍāya gajadantāya gulaguletininādāya2 caturbhujāya trinetrāya muśalapāśavajrahastāya sarvabhūtadamanāya sarvalokavaśaṃkarāya sarvaduṣṭopaghātajananāya sarvaśatruvimardanāya sarvarājyasamīhanāya rājānamiha vaśamānaya hana hana paca paca vajrāṅkuśena gaṇeśa phaṭ svāhā .
oṃ gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaiṃ gauṃ gaḥ svāhā namaḥ hadayaṃ mūlamantrasya .
oṃ kaḥ śiraḥ, oṃ khaḥ śikhā, oṃ gaḥ hadayam, oṃ guḥ vaktraṃ, oṃ gaiṃ netram . oṃ ghaḥ kavacam, oṃ ṅa āvāhanaṃ hadayasya āvāhanāṅgāni bhavanti oṃ namaḥ hadayaṃ mūlamantrasya, oṃ gāḥ śiraḥ, oṃ gaiḥ namaḥ śikhā oṃ gauḥ namaḥ kavacam, oṃ gaṃ namaḥ netre, oṃ gaḥ phaṭ astram . .
oṃ aṅguṣṭholkāya svāhā āvāhanaṃ hadayasya svāhā visarjanaṃ hadayasya oṃ gandholkāya svāhā . .
gandhamantraḥ . . oṃ dharmabhūtolkāya svāhā . . puṣpamantraḥ . . durjayāya 1 pūrveṇa . oṃ dhūrjaṭaye dakṣiṇena .
oṃ lambodarāya paścimataḥ . oṃ gaṇapataye uttarataḥ . oṃ gaṇādhipataye aiśānyām . oṃ mahāgaṇapataye āgneyyām . oṃ kūśmāṇḍāya nairṛtyām .
oṃ ekadantatripuraghātine2 trinetrāya vāyavyām . oṃ mahāgaṇapataye vidmahe vakratuṇḍāya dhīmahi . .
tanno dantiḥ pracodayāt . . gāyatrī . .
padmadaṃṣṭrāmālāprakarṣaṇīparaśvaṃkuśapāśapaṭahamudrā aṣṭau mudrā darśayitvā tataḥ karmāṇi kārayet . .
kṛṣṇatilāhutīnāmaṣṭasahasraṃ juhuyāt . rājānaṃ vaśamānayet . .
āvāhanādyekādaśamudrā naivedyāntaṃ kramāddarśayet . .
ārādhayedyena vidhinā trinetraṃ śūlinaṃ haram .
tenaivārādhayeddevaṃ vighneśaṃ gaṇapaṃ nṛpa . . 1
1.30.d:
सुमन्तरुवाच
निम्बमयमङ्गुष्ठपर्वमात्रं गणपतिं कृत्वा नित्यधूपगन्धादिभिरर्चयित्वा प्रच्छन्नं शिरसि बद्ध्वा गच्छेत् ॥
सर्वजनप्रियो भवति । श्वेतार्कमूलाङ्गुष्ठमात्रं गणपतिं कृत्वा धूपादिभिरर्चयित्वा सर्वान्वर्णान्वशमानयति ॥
श्वेतचन्दनमङ्गुष्ठमात्रं गणपतिं कृत्वा पुष्पगन्धादिभिरर्चयित्वा शुक्लचतुर्थ्यामष्टम्यां वा बलिं कुर्यादष्टसहस्रं जुहुयाद्दध्ना पायसेन राजानं वशमानयति ।
रक्तचन्दनमयं गणपतिमङ्गुष्ठमात्रं कृत्वा भौतिकं बलिं दद्याद्दधिमधुघृताहुतीनां गणपतिमष्टसहस्रं जुहुयादात्मप्रापिकां प्रजां वशमानयति । रक्तकरवीरमूलाङ्गुष्ठपर्वमात्रं गणपतिं कारयेत् ॥
रक्तपुष्पगन्धोपहारैर्बलिं दद्यात् । तिललवणघृतेनाष्टसहस्रं जुहुयात् । दशग्रामान्वशमानयति ॥
श्वेतकरवीराङ्गुष्ठपर्वमात्रं गणपतिं कृत्वा तिलपिष्टदधिघृतक्षीरहरिद्रामिश्रेणाष्टसहस्रं
जुहुयाद्वेश्यां वशमानयति ॥
अश्वत्थमूलाङ्गुष्ठपर्वमात्रं गणपतिं कृत्वा गन्धपुष्पधूपबलिं दत्त्वा शतं जुहुयाच्छत्रुं वशमानयति ॥
अर्कमूलाङ्गुष्ठपर्वमात्रं गणपतिं कृत्वा गन्धपुष्पधूपबलीन् दद्यात् ।
तिन्दुकाष्टशतं जुहुयाच्छत्रुं वशमानयति ॥
बिल्वमूलमयमङ्गुष्ठपर्वमात्रं गणपतिं कृत्वा गन्धपुष्पधूपार्चितं कृत्वा त्रिमध्वक्तानामष्टसहस्रं जुहुयाद्राजामात्यान्वशमानयति ॥
शिरसि धूपान्धृत्वा गच्छेद्राजद्वारं विग्रहे जयो भवति ।
हस्तिदन्तमृत्तिकामयमङ्गुष्ठपर्वमात्रं गणपतिं कारयेत् ॥
गन्धपुष्पधूपार्चितं कृत्वा। कृष्णचतुर्थ्यां नग्नो भूत्वाभ्यर्चयेत् ।
सप्त वाराञ्जपेन्नित्यं 1 नारीणां सुभगो भवति ॥
वृषभशृङ्गमृत्तिकाङ्गुष्ठमात्रं गणपतिं कारयेत् ।
गन्धपुष्पार्चितं कृत्वा गुग्गुलुधूपं दद्याद्घोषपतिं वशमानयति ॥
अथ वा वल्मीकमृत्तिकांगुष्ठपर्वमात्रं गणपतिं कारयेत् ।
कटुकतैलेन प्रतिमां लेपयेत् ॥
उन्मत्तककाष्ठेनाग्निं प्रज्वाल्याहुतीनामष्टसहस्रं जुहुयात्तिलसर्षपमिश्रेण सर्वधूपं दद्यात्त्रिकटुकेन लेपयेत् ॥
अगरुधूपं दद्याद्राजानं वशमानयति । परेषां च वल्लभो भवति । रक्तचन्दनेनात्मानं धूपयेत्सुभगो भवति ॥
ओं गणपतये वक्रतुण्डाय गजदन्ताय गुलगुलेतिनिनादाय2 चतुर्भुजाय त्रिनेत्राय मुशलपाशवज्रहस्ताय सर्वभूतदमनाय सर्वलोकवशंकराय सर्वदुष्टोपघातजननाय सर्वशत्रुविमर्दनाय सर्वराज्यसमीहनाय राजानमिह वशमानय हन हन पच पच वज्राङ्कुशेन गणेश फट् स्वाहा ।
ओं गां गीं गूं गैं गौं गः स्वाहा नमः हदयं मूलमन्त्रस्य ।
ओं कः शिरः, ओं खः शिखा, ओं गः हदयम्, ओं गुः वक्त्रं, ओं गैं नेत्रम् । ओं घः कवचम्, ओं ङ आवाहनं हदयस्य आवाहनाङ्गानि भवन्ति ओं नमः हदयं मूलमन्त्रस्य, ओं गाः शिरः, ओं गैः नमः शिखा ओं गौः नमः कवचम्, ओं गं नमः नेत्रे, ओं गः फट् अस्त्रम् ॥
ओं अङ्गुष्ठोल्काय स्वाहा आवाहनं हदयस्य स्वाहा विसर्जनं हदयस्य ओं गन्धोल्काय स्वाहा ॥
गन्धमन्त्रः ॥ ओं धर्मभूतोल्काय स्वाहा ॥ पुष्पमन्त्रः ॥ दुर्जयाय 1 पूर्वेण । ओं धूर्जटये दक्षिणेन ।
ओं लम्बोदराय पश्चिमतः । ओं गणपतये उत्तरतः । ओं गणाधिपतये ऐशान्याम् । ओं महागणपतये आग्नेय्याम् । ओं कूश्माण्डाय नैरृत्याम् ।
ओं एकदन्तत्रिपुरघातिने2 त्रिनेत्राय वायव्याम् । ओं महागणपतये विद्महे वक्रतुण्डाय धीमहि ॥
तन्नो दन्तिः प्रचोदयात् ॥ गायत्री ॥
पद्मदंष्ट्रामालाप्रकर्षणीपरश्वंकुशपाशपटहमुद्रा अष्टौ मुद्रा दर्शयित्वा ततः कर्माणि कारयेत् ॥
कृष्णतिलाहुतीनामष्टसहस्रं जुहुयात् । राजानं वशमानयेत् ॥
आवाहनाद्येकादशमुद्रा नैवेद्यान्तं क्रमाद्दर्शयेत् ॥
आराधयेद्येन विधिना त्रिनेत्रं शूलिनं हरम् ।
तेनैवाराधयेद्देवं विघ्नेशं गणपं नृप ॥ 1
1.30.m:
Sumantu said:
Having fashioned a Gaṇapati made of neem wood the size of a thumb-joint, worshipped [him] daily with incense, perfume, and the like, and bound [him] concealed on one's head, one should go forth.
He becomes dear to all people. Having fashioned a Gaṇapati the size of a thumb from white arka root and worshipped [him] with incense and the like, he brings all castes under subjugation.
Having fashioned a Gaṇapati the size of a thumb from white sandalwood, worshipped [him] with flowers, perfume, and the like, and made an offering on the bright fourth or eighth [lunar day], he should offer eight thousand oblations with curd and milk-rice; he brings the king under subjugation.
Having fashioned a Gaṇapati the size of a thumb made of red sandalwood, he should give an offering to the ghosts; having made eight thousand oblations of curd, honey, and ghee to Gaṇapati, he brings the subjects born to himself under subjugation. One should have a Gaṇapati fashioned the size of a thumb-joint from the root of red oleander.
He should give an offering with red flowers, perfumes, and presents. He should offer eight thousand oblations with sesame, salt, and ghee; he brings ten villages under subjugation.
Having fashioned a Gaṇapati the size of a thumb-joint from white oleander, he should offer eight thousand oblations with sesame paste, curd, ghee, milk, and turmeric mixed together; he brings a courtesan under subjugation.
Having fashioned a Gaṇapati the size of a thumb-joint from the root of an aśvattha tree, given an offering of perfume, flowers, and incense, and offered one hundred oblations, he brings an enemy under subjugation.
Having fashioned a Gaṇapati the size of a thumb-joint from arka root, he should give offerings of perfume, flowers, and incense.
He should offer one hundred and eight [oblations] of tinduka; he brings an enemy under subjugation.
Having fashioned a Gaṇapati the size of a thumb-joint made of bilva root, worshipped [him] with perfume, flowers, and incense, and offered eight thousand oblations smeared with the three sweets, he brings royal ministers under subjugation.
Carrying the incense on one's head, one should go to the king's gate; victory occurs in battle.
One should have a Gaṇapati fashioned the size of a thumb-joint made of elephant-tusk earth.
Having worshipped [him] with perfume, flowers, and incense, he should worship [him] becoming naked on the dark fourth [tithi].
He should recite [the mantra] seven times daily; he becomes attractive to women.
One should have a Gaṇapati fashioned the size of a thumb from bull-horn earth.
Having worshipped [him] with perfume and flowers, he should give bdellium incense; he brings the lord of the cowherds' settlement under subjugation.
Or else one should have a Gaṇapati fashioned the size of a thumb-joint from anthill earth.
He should smear the image with pungent oil.
Having kindled a fire with datura wood, he should offer eight thousand oblations; he should give all kinds of incense mixed with sesame and mustard; he should smear [the image] with the three pungents.
He should give eaglewood incense; he brings the king under subjugation, and he becomes beloved to others. He should fumigate himself with red sandalwood; he becomes fortunate.
'Oṃ, to Gaṇapati, the crooked-trunked, elephant-tusked, who roars with a gurgling sound, the four-armed, three-eyed, who holds a pestle, noose, and thunderbolt in his hands, tamer of all beings, subjugator of all worlds, causer of injury to all the wicked, crusher of all enemies, desirer of all kingdoms: bring the king here under subjugation! Strike, strike! Cook, cook, with the thunderbolt-goad, Gaṇeśa! Phaṭ! Svāhā!'
'Oṃ gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaiṃ gauṃ gaḥ svāhā namaḥ' is the heart of the root mantra.
'Oṃ kaḥ' is the head, 'oṃ khaḥ' is the crest, 'oṃ gaḥ' is the heart, 'oṃ guḥ' is the mouth, 'oṃ gaiṃ' is the eye, 'oṃ ghaḥ' is the armour, 'oṃ ṅa' is the invocation of the heart. The limbs of invocation are: 'oṃ namaḥ' is the heart of the root mantra, 'oṃ gāḥ' is the head, 'oṃ gaiḥ namaḥ' is the crest, 'oṃ gauḥ namaḥ' is the armour, 'oṃ gaṃ namaḥ' is the two eyes, 'oṃ gaḥ phaṭ' is the weapon.
'Oṃ to the thumb-torch svāhā' is the invocation of the heart; 'svāhā' is the dismissal of the heart. 'Oṃ to the perfume-torch svāhā' is the perfume mantra. 'Oṃ to the righteous-being-torch svāhā' is the flower mantra. 'To the unconquerable' on the east; 'oṃ to Dhūrjaṭi' on the south;
'oṃ to the pot-bellied one' on the west; 'oṃ to Gaṇapati' on the north; 'oṃ to the lord of the gaṇas' in the north-east; 'oṃ to Mahāgaṇapati' in the south-east; 'oṃ to Kūśmāṇḍa' in the south-west;
'oṃ to the one-tusked destroyer of Tripura, the three-eyed one' in the north-west. 'Oṃ, we know Mahāgaṇapati, we meditate upon the crooked-trunked one;
may that tusked one impel us!' This is the Gāyatrī.
Having shown the eight hand-gestures—lotus, tusk, rosary, attractor, axe, goad, noose, and kettle-drum—he should then perform the rites.
He should offer eight thousand oblations of black sesame; he would bring a king under subjugation.
He should display in sequence the eleven hand-gestures from invocation up to the food offering.
By whatever procedure one should worship Hara, the three-eyed wielder of the trident,
by that very procedure one should worship the divine Vighneśa, the lord of the gaṇas, O king. 1

1.30.s:
tadeva maṇḍalaṃ cāsya aṅganyāsastathaiva ca .
ṛte mantrapadānīha samānaṃ sarvameva hi . . 2
1.30.d:
तदेव मण्डलं चास्य अङ्गन्यासस्तथैव च ।
ऋते मन्त्रपदानीह समानं सर्वमेव हि ॥ 2
1.30.m:
His diagram is the very same, and likewise the placement on the limbs;
except for the words of the mantra, everything indeed is the same here. 2

1.30.s:
pūjayedyastu vighneśamekadantamumāsutam .
naśyanti tasya vighnāni na cāriṣṭaṃ kadācana . . 3
1.30.d:
पूजयेद्यस्तु विघ्नेशमेकदन्तमुमासुतम् ।
नश्यन्ति तस्य विघ्नानि न चारिष्टं कदाचन ॥ 3
1.30.m:
Whoever worships Vighneśa, the one-tusked son of Umā,
his obstacles are destroyed, and no calamity ever befalls him. 3

1.30.s:
yaścopavāsaṃ kṛtvā tu caturthyāṃ pūjayennaraḥ .
sarve tasya samārambhāḥ sidhyeyurnātra saṃśayaḥ . .4
1.30.d:
यश्चोपवासं कृत्वा तु चतुर्थ्यां पूजयेन्नरः ।
सर्वे तस्य समारम्भाः सिध्येयुर्नात्र संशयः ॥4
1.30.m:
And whatever man worships on the fourth [tithi] having fasted,
all his undertakings succeed; there is no doubt about this. 4

1.30.s:
yasyānukūlo vighneśaḥ śivayoḥ kulanandana .
tasyānukūlaṃ sarvaṃ syājjagadvai sarvakarmasu . . 5
1.30.d:
यस्यानुकूलो विघ्नेशः शिवयोः कुलनन्दन ।
तस्यानुकूलं सर्वं स्याज्जगद्वै सर्वकर्मसु ॥ 5
1.30.m:
To whom Vighneśa is favorable, O delighter of the race of Śiva,
to him the entire world becomes favorable in all undertakings. 5

Therefore, one should worship him endowed with devotion and faith,
with saffron, eaglewood incense, and likewise with a garland of uṇḍīraka,
with sesame sweets and pastries, and likewise with jasmine and datura flowers. 6

1.30.s:
śuklapakṣe caturthyāṃ tu vidhinānena pūjayet .
tasya sidhyati nirvighnaṃ sarvakarma na saṃśayaḥ . .7
1.30.d:
शुक्लपक्षे चतुर्थ्यां तु विधिनानेन पूजयेत् ।
तस्य सिध्यति निर्विघ्नं सर्वकर्म न संशयः ॥7
1.30.m:
He should worship on the fourth [tithi] in the bright fortnight according to this procedure;
his every undertaking succeeds without obstacles; there is no doubt. 7

1.30.s:
ekadante jagannāthe gaṇeśe tuṣṭimāgate .
pitṛdevamanuṣyādyāḥ sarve tuṣyanti bhārata . . 8
1.30.d:
एकदन्ते जगन्नाथे गणेशे तुष्टिमागते ।
पितृदेवमनुष्याद्याः सर्वे तुष्यन्ति भारत ॥ 8
1.30.m:
When the one-tusked lord of the world, Gaṇeśa, is pleased,
ancestors, gods, humans, and others are all pleased, O descendant of Bharata. 8

1.30.s:
tasmādārādhayedenaṃ sadā bhaktipuraḥsaram .
karṇalepaistuṇḍikābhirmodakaiśca1 mahīpate . .
pūjayetsatataṃ devaṃ vighnavināśāya dantinam . . 9
1.30.d:
तस्मादाराधयेदेनं सदा भक्तिपुरःसरम् ।
कर्णलेपैस्तुण्डिकाभिर्मोदकैश्च1 महीपते ॥
पूजयेत्सततं देवं विघ्नविनाशाय दन्तिनम् ॥ 9

1.30.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi caturthīkalpe
vināyakapūjāvidhinirūpaṇaṃ nāma triṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 30 .
śivācaturthī pūjanam
1.30.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि चतुर्थीकल्पे
विनायकपूजाविधिनिरूपणं नाम त्रिंशोऽध्यायः । 30 ।
शिवाचतुर्थी पूजनम्
1.30.m:
Thus ends the thirtieth chapter, named 'Description of the Procedure for the Worship of Vināyaka', in the section on the fourth [tithi] in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty thousand [verses]. 30.
Worship on the Śivācaturthī

1.31.s:
sumanturuvāca
śivā śāntā sukhā rājaṃścaturthī trividhā smṛtā .
māsi bhādrapade śuklā śivā lokeṣu pūjitā . . 1
1.31.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
शिवा शान्ता सुखा राजंश्चतुर्थी त्रिविधा स्मृता ।
मासि भाद्रपदे शुक्ला शिवा लोकेषु पूजिता ॥ 1
1.31.m:
Sumantu said:
Śivā, Śāntā, and Sukhā: the fourth [tithi] is traditionally declared to be threefold, O king.
The bright [fourth] in the month of Bhādrapada, named Śivā, is worshipped in the worlds. 1

1.31.s:
tasyāṃ snānaṃ tathā dānamupavāso japastathā .
kriyamāṇaṃ śataguṇaṃ prasādāddantino nṛpa . . 2
1.31.d:
तस्यां स्नानं तथा दानमुपवासो जपस्तथा ।
क्रियमाणं शतगुणं प्रसादाद्दन्तिनो नृप ॥ 2
1.31.m: Bathing, giving gifts, fasting, and recitation of mantras performed on it, / O king, become a hundredfold [more fruitful] through the grace of the Tusked One.

1.31.s:
guḍalavaṇaghṛtānāṃ tu dānaṃ śubhakaraṃ smṛtam .
guḍāpūpaistathā vīra puṇyaṃ brāhmaṇabhojanam . . 3
1.31.d:
गुडलवणघृतानां तु दानं शुभकरं स्मृतम् ।
गुडापूपैस्तथा वीर पुण्यं ब्राह्मणभोजनम् ॥ 3
1.31.m: The gift of jaggery, salt, and clarified butter is considered auspicious; / likewise, O hero, feeding Brahmins with sweet jaggery cakes brings great merit.

1.31.s:
yāstasyāṃ naraśārdūla pūjayanti sadā striyaḥ .
guḍalavaṇapūpaiśca śvaśrūṃ śvasurameva ca . .4
1.31.d:
यास्तस्यां नरशार्दूल पूजयन्ति सदा स्त्रियः ।
गुडलवणपूपैश्च श्वश्रूं श्वसुरमेव च ॥4
1.31.m: The women who always worship on it, O tiger among men, / their mother-in-law and father-in-law with jaggery, salt, and cakes,

1.31.s:
tāḥ sarvāḥ subhagāḥ syurve1 vighreśasyānumodanāt .
kanyakā tu viśeṣeṇa vidhinānena pūjayet . . 5
1.31.d:
ताः सर्वाः सुभगाः स्युर्वे1 विघ्रेशस्यानुमोदनात् ।
कन्यका तु विशेषेण विधिनानेन पूजयेत् ॥ 5
1.31.m: all of them shall indeed be fortunate through the grace of the Lord of Obstacles. / An unmarried maiden especially should worship according to this procedure.

1.31.s:
( iti śivākalpaḥ)
sumanturuvāca
māghe māsi tathā śuklā yā caturthī mahīpate .
sā śāntā śāntidā nityaṃ śāntiṃ kuryātsadaiva hi . . 6
1.31.d:
( इति शिवाकल्पः)
सुमन्तुरुवाच
माघे मासि तथा शुक्ला या चतुर्थी महीपते ।
सा शान्ता शान्तिदा नित्यं शान्तिं कुर्यात्सदैव हि ॥ 6
1.31.m: (Thus ends the Śivā ritual.) / Sumantu said: / The fourth lunar day in the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha, O lord of the earth, / is the Śāntā, the peace-bestower; it always brings peace.

1.31.s:
snānadānādikaṃ karma sarvamasyāṃ kṛtaṃ vibho .
bhavetsahasraguṇitaṃ prasādāttasya2 dantinaḥ . . 7
1.31.d:
स्नानदानादिकं कर्म सर्वमस्यां कृतं विभो ।
भवेत्सहस्रगुणितं प्रसादात्तस्य2 दन्तिनः ॥ 7
1.31.m: Bathing, giving gifts, and all such rites performed on it, O lord, / become multiplied a thousandfold through the grace of that Tusked One.

1.31.s:
kṛtopavāso yastasyāṃ pūjayedvi ghnanāyakam .
tasya homādikaṃ karma bhavetsāhasrikaṃ nṛpa . . 8
1.31.d:
कृतोपवासो यस्तस्यां पूजयेद्वि घ्ननायकम् ।
तस्य होमादिकं कर्म भवेत्साहस्रिकं नृप ॥ 8
1.31.m: Whoever, having fasted, worships the Lord of Obstacles on it, / his rites of fire offerings and the like become a thousandfold [more fruitful], O king.

1.31.s:
lavaṇaṃ ca guḍaṃ śākaṃ guḍapūpāṃśca bhārata .
dattvā bhaktyā tu viprebhyaḥ phalaṃ sāhasrikaṃ bhajet3 . . 9
1.31.d:
लवणं च गुडं शाकं गुडपूपांश्च भारत ।
दत्त्वा भक्त्या तु विप्रेभ्यः फलं साहस्रिकं भजेत्3 ॥ 9
1.31.m: Offering salt, jaggery, vegetables, and sweet jaggery cakes / with devotion to Brahmins, O Bhārata, one obtains a thousandfold fruit.

1.31.s:
viśeṣataḥ striyo rājanpūjayanto guruṃ nṛpa .
guḍalavaṇaghṛtairvīra sadā syurbhāgyasaṃyutāḥ4 . . 1.31.10
1.31.d:
विशेषतः स्त्रियो राजन्पूजयन्तो गुरुं नृप ।
गुडलवणघृतैर्वीर सदा स्युर्भाग्यसंयुताः4 ॥ 1.31.10
1.31.m: Especially women, O king, who worship the elder / with jaggery, salt, and clarified butter, O hero, will always be endowed with good fortune.

1.31.s:
( iti śāntākalpaḥ)
sumanturuvāca
sukhāvahā ca susukhā saubhāgyakaraṇī param . . 11
1.31.d:
( इति शान्ताकल्पः)
सुमन्तुरुवाच
सुखावहा च सुसुखा सौभाग्यकरणी परम् ॥ 11
1.31.m: (Thus ends the Śāntā ritual.) / Sumantu said: / It brings happiness, is very pleasant, and is supreme in creating good fortune.

1.31.s:
caturthī kuruśārdūla rūpasaubhāgyadā śubhā .
sukhāvrataṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ rūpadaṃ bhāgyadaṃ tathā . . 12
1.31.d:
चतुर्थी कुरुशार्दूल रूपसौभाग्यदा शुभा ।
सुखाव्रतं महापुण्यं रूपदं भाग्यदं तथा ॥ 12
1.31.m: The fourth lunar day, O tiger of the Kurus, bestows beauty, good fortune, and auspiciousness. / The Sukhā observance brings great merit, conferring beauty and good fortune;

1.31.s:
susūkṣmaṃ sukaraṃ dhanyamiha puṇyasukhāvaham .
paratra phaladaṃ vīra divyarūpapradāyakam . . 13
1.31.d:
सुसूक्ष्मं सुकरं धन्यमिह पुण्यसुखावहम् ।
परत्र फलदं वीर दिव्यरूपप्रदायकम् ॥ 13
1.31.m: it is subtle, easy to perform, praiseworthy, bringing meritorious happiness here [in this world], / and granting fruit in the next world, O hero, bestowing a celestial form.

1.31.s:
hasitaṃ lalitaṃ coktaṃ ceṣṭitaṃ ca sukhāvaham .
savilāsabhujakṣepaścaṃkramaśceṣṭitaṃ śubham . . 14
1.31.d:
हसितं ललितं चोक्तं चेष्टितं च सुखावहम् ।
सविलासभुजक्षेपश्चंक्रमश्चेष्टितं शुभम् ॥ 14
1.31.m: Laughter, grace, and movements are said to bring happiness; / graceful swinging of the arms and elegant walking are auspicious movements.

1.31.s:
sukhāvratena sarveṣāṃ sukhaṃ kurukulodvaha .
kṛtyena pūjite ceśe vighreśe śivayoḥ sute . . 15
1.31.d:
सुखाव्रतेन सर्वेषां सुखं कुरुकुलोद्वह ।
कृत्येन पूजिते चेशे विघ्रेशे शिवयोः सुते ॥ 15
1.31.m: Through the Sukhā observance, happiness comes to all, O scion of the Kuru race, / when the Lord, the Lord of Obstacles, the son of Śiva and Pārvatī, is worshipped according to the rite.

1.31.s:
yadā śuklacaturthyāṃ tu vāro bhaumasya vai bhavet .
tadā sā sukhadā jñeyā caturthī vai sukheti ca . . 16
1.31.d:
यदा शुक्लचतुर्थ्यां तु वारो भौमस्य वै भवेत् ।
तदा सा सुखदा ज्ञेया चतुर्थी वै सुखेति च ॥ 16
1.31.m: When a Tuesday coincides with the fourth lunar day of the bright fortnight, / then that fourth lunar day is known as bestowing happiness, and indeed as Sukhā.

1.31.s:
purā maithunamāśritya sthitābhyāṃ tu himācale .
bhīmomābhyāṃ mahābāho raktabinduścyutaḥ kṣitau . . 17
1.31.d:
पुरा मैथुनमाश्रित्य स्थिताभ्यां तु हिमाचले ।
भीमोमाभ्यां महाबाहो रक्तबिन्दुश्च्युतः क्षितौ ॥ 17
1.31.m: Long ago, as Śiva and Umā were engaged in union upon the Himālayas, / O mighty-armed one, a drop of blood fell upon the earth.

1.31.s:
medinyāṃ sa prayatnena sukhe vidhṛto'nayā .
jātosyāḥ sa kujo vīra rakto raktasamudbhavaḥ . . 18
1.31.d:
मेदिन्यां स प्रयत्नेन सुखे विधृतोऽनया ।
जातोस्याः स कुजो वीर रक्तो रक्तसमुद्भवः ॥ 18
1.31.m: She carefully held it in comfort upon the earth; / from her Kuja was born, O hero, red, born from blood.

1.31.s:
mamāṅgato yathotpannastasmādaṅgārako hyayam .
aṅgadoṅgopakāraśca aṅgānāṃ tu prado nṛṇām . . 19
1.31.d:
ममाङ्गतो यथोत्पन्नस्तस्मादङ्गारको ह्ययम् ।
अङ्गदोङ्गोपकारश्च अङ्गानां तु प्रदो नृणाम् ॥ 19
1.31.m: Since he was born from my limb, he is indeed called Aṅgāraka. / He gives limbs, benefits the limbs, and bestows limbs upon men;

1.31.s:
saubhāgyādikaro yasmāttasmādaṅgārako mataḥ .
bhaktyā caturthyāṃ naktena yo vai śraddhāsamanvitaḥ . . 1.31.20
1.31.d:
सौभाग्यादिकरो यस्मात्तस्मादङ्गारको मतः ।
भक्त्या चतुर्थ्यां नक्तेन यो वै श्रद्धासमन्वितः ॥ 1.31.20
1.31.m: because he brings good fortune and other blessings, he is regarded as Aṅgāraka. / Whoever with devotion, fasting during the day and eating at night on the fourth lunar day, endowed with faith,

1.31.s:
upavatsyati nā rājannārī vā nānyamānasā .
pūjayecca kujaṃ bhaktayā raktapuṣpavilepanaiḥ . . 21
1.31.d:
उपवत्स्यति ना राजन्नारी वा नान्यमानसा ।
पूजयेच्च कुजं भक्तया रक्तपुष्पविलेपनैः ॥ 21
1.31.m: a man or a woman, O king, with an undistracted mind, / should worship Kuja with devotion, using red flowers and unguents.

1.31.s:
gaṇeśaṃ prathamaṃ bhaktyā yojayecchaddhayānvitaḥ .
yasya tuṣṭaḥ prayacchetsa saubhāgyaṃ rūpasampadam . . 22
1.31.d:
गणेशं प्रथमं भक्त्या योजयेच्छद्धयान्वितः ।
यस्य तुष्टः प्रयच्छेत्स सौभाग्यं रूपसम्पदम् ॥ 22
1.31.m: First, one endowed with faith should worship Gaṇeśa with devotion; / pleased with him, he will bestow good fortune and the wealth of beauty.

1.31.s:
pūrvaṃ ca kṛtasaṅkalpaḥ snānaṃ kṛtvā yathāvidhi .
gṛhītvā mṛttikāṃ vandenmantreṇānena bhārata . . 23
1.31.d:
पूर्वं च कृतसङ्कल्पः स्नानं कृत्वा यथाविधि ।
गृहीत्वा मृत्तिकां वन्देन्मन्त्रेणानेन भारत ॥ 23
1.31.m: Having first made the solemn vow and bathed according to rule, / taking up clay, one should salute it with this mantra, O Bhārata:

1.31.s:
iha tvaṃ vanditā pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇenoddharatā kila .
tasmānme daha pāpmānaṃ yanmayā pūrvasañcitam . . 24
1.31.d:
इह त्वं वन्दिता पूर्वं कृष्णेनोद्धरता किल ।
तस्मान्मे दह पाप्मानं यन्मया पूर्वसञ्चितम् ॥ 24
1.31.m: ‘Here you were praised long ago by Kṛṣṇa as he lifted you up; / therefore, burn away the sin accumulated by me in the past.’

1.31.s:
imaṃ mantraṃ paṭhanvīra ādityāya pradarśayet .
ādityaraśmisampūtāṃ gaṅgājalakaṇokṣitām . . 25
1.31.d:
इमं मन्त्रं पठन्वीर आदित्याय प्रदर्शयेत् ।
आदित्यरश्मिसम्पूतां गङ्गाजलकणोक्षिताम् ॥ 25
1.31.m: Reciting this mantra, O hero, one should show [the clay] to the Sun, / purified by the rays of the Sun and sprinkled with drops of Gaṅgā water.

1.31.s:
dattvā mṛdaṃ śirasi tāṃ sarvāṅgeṣu ca yojayet .
tataḥ snānaṃ prakurvīta mantrayeta jalaṃ punaḥ . . 26
1.31.d:
दत्त्वा मृदं शिरसि तां सर्वाङ्गेषु च योजयेत् ।
ततः स्नानं प्रकुर्वीत मन्त्रयेत जलं पुनः ॥ 26
1.31.m: Placing that clay on the head, one should apply it to all one's limbs. / Then one should bathe and again consecrate the water with mantras:

1.31.s:
tvamāpo yoniḥ sarveṣāṃ daityadānavadyaukasām .
svedāṇḍajodbhidāṃ caiva rasānāṃ pataye namaḥ . . 27
1.31.d:
त्वमापो योनिः सर्वेषां दैत्यदानवद्यौकसाम् ।
स्वेदाण्डजोद्भिदां चैव रसानां पतये नमः ॥ 27
1.31.m: ‘You, O waters, are the source of all—of Daityas, Dānavas, and celestials, / and of the sweat-born, egg-born, and sprouting beings. Homage to the Lord of juices!’

1.31.s:
snāto'haṃ sarvatīrtheṣu sarvaprasravaṇeṣu ca .
taḍāgeṣu ca sarveṣu mānasādisaraḥsu ca . . 28
1.31.d:
स्नातोऽहं सर्वतीर्थेषु सर्वप्रस्रवणेषु च ।
तडागेषु च सर्वेषु मानसादिसरःसु च ॥ 28
1.31.m: ‘I have bathed in all sacred water sites, in all waterfalls, / in all ponds, and in lakes such as Mānasa;

1.31.s:
nadīṣu devakhāteṣu sutīrtheṣu hradeṣu vai .
dhyāyanyaṭhannimaṃ mantraṃ tataḥ snānaṃ samācaret . . 29
1.31.d:
नदीषु देवखातेषु सुतीर्थेषु ह्रदेषु वै ।
ध्यायन्यठन्निमं मन्त्रं ततः स्नानं समाचरेत् ॥ 29
1.31.m: in rivers, in divine excavations, in sacred fords, and in deep pools.’ / Meditating and reciting this mantra, one should then perform the bath.

1.31.s:
tataḥ snātvā śucirbhūtvā gṛhamāgatya vai spṛśet .
dūrvāśvatthau śamīṃ spṛṣṭvā gāṃ ca mantreṇa mantravit . . 1.31.30
1.31.d:
ततः स्नात्वा शुचिर्भूत्वा गृहमागत्य वै स्पृशेत् ।
दूर्वाश्वत्थौ शमीं स्पृष्ट्वा गां च मन्त्रेण मन्त्रवित् ॥ 1.31.30
1.31.m: Then, having bathed and become pure, one should come home and touch; / having touched dūrvā grass, an aśvattha tree, and a śamī tree, the knower of mantras should touch a cow with the mantra.

1.31.s:
dūrvā namasya mantreṇa śucau bhūmau samutthitām .
tvaṃ dūrve'mṛtanāmāsi sarvadevaistu vanditā . . 31
1.31.d:
दूर्वा नमस्य मन्त्रेण शुचौ भूमौ समुत्थिताम् ।
त्वं दूर्वेऽमृतनामासि सर्वदेवैस्तु वन्दिता ॥ 31
1.31.m: One should salute the dūrvā grass growing on pure ground with the mantra: / ‘O dūrvā, you are named nectar, praised by all the gods;

1.31.s: vanditā daha tatsarvaṃ duritaṃ yanmayā1 kṛtam . . 32
1.31.d: वन्दिता दह तत्सर्वं दुरितं यन्मया1 कृतम् ॥ 32
1.31.m: praised [by me], burn away all that evil which was done by me.’

1.31.s:
śamīmantraṃ pravakṣyāmi tannibodha mahīpate .
pavitrāṇāṃ pavitrāṃ tvaṃ kāśyapī prathitā śrutau . .
śamī śamaya me pāpaṃ nūnaṃ vetsi dharādharān . . 33
1.31.d:
शमीमन्त्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि तन्निबोध महीपते ।
पवित्राणां पवित्रां त्वं काश्यपी प्रथिता श्रुतौ ॥
शमी शमय मे पापं नूनं वेत्सि धराधरान् ॥ 33
1.31.m: I shall state the śamī mantra; listen to it, O lord of the earth: / ‘You are the purest of pure things, renowned as Kāśyapī in sacred tradition; / O śamī, pacify my sin; surely you know the mountains.’

1.31.s:
aśvatthālambhane vīra mantrametaṃ nibodha me .
netraspandādijaṃ duḥkhaṃ duḥsvapnaṃ durvicintanam . .
śaktānāṃ ca samudyogamaśvattha tvaṃ kṣamasva me . . 34
1.31.d:
अश्वत्थालम्भने वीर मन्त्रमेतं निबोध मे ।
नेत्रस्पन्दादिजं दुःखं दुःस्वप्नं दुर्विचिन्तनम् ॥
शक्तानां च समुद्योगमश्वत्थ त्वं क्षमस्व मे ॥ 34
1.31.m: In touching the aśvattha tree, O hero, learn this mantra from me: / ‘The distress born from eye-twitching and the like, bad dreams, evil thoughts, / and the enterprise of powerful enemies—O aśvattha, forgive it for me.’

1.31.s:
imaṃ mantraṃ paṭhanvīra kuryādvai sparśanaṃ budhaḥ .
tato devyai tu gāṃ dadyādvīraṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇām . .
samālabhya tu hastena tato mantramudīrayet . . 35
1.31.d:
इमं मन्त्रं पठन्वीर कुर्याद्वै स्पर्शनं बुधः ।
ततो देव्यै तु गां दद्याद्वीरं कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणाम् ॥
समालभ्य तु हस्तेन ततो मन्त्रमुदीरयेत् ॥ 35
1.31.m: Reciting this mantra, O hero, the wise person should touch [it]. / Then, having circumambulated a white cow clockwise, / and touching it with the hand, one should recite the mantra:

1.31.s:
sarvadevamayī devi munibhistu supūjitā .
tasmātspṛśāmi vande tvāṃ vanditā pāpahā bhava . . 36
1.31.d:
सर्वदेवमयी देवि मुनिभिस्तु सुपूजिता ।
तस्मात्स्पृशामि वन्दे त्वां वन्दिता पापहा भव ॥ 36
1.31.m: ‘O goddess comprising all the gods, well worshipped by the sages, / therefore I touch you and salute you; praised, become the destroyer of sins.’

1.31.s:
imaṃ mantraṃ paṭhanvīra bhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ .
pradakṣiṇaṃ tu yaḥ kuryādarjunaṃ kurunandana . .
pradakṣiṇīkṛtā tena pṛthivī syānna saṃśayaḥ . . 37
1.31.d:
इमं मन्त्रं पठन्वीर भक्त्या श्रद्धासमन्वितः ।
प्रदक्षिणं तु यः कुर्यादर्जुनं कुरुनन्दन ॥
प्रदक्षिणीकृता तेन पृथिवी स्यान्न संशयः ॥ 37
1.31.m: Reciting this mantra, O hero, with devotion and faith, / whoever circumambulates the white cow, O joy of the Kurus, / the earth itself is circumambulated by him; of this there is no doubt.

1.31.s:
evaṃ maunena cāgatya tato vahnigṛhaṃ vrajet .
prakṣālya ca mṛdā pādāvācāntognigṛhaṃ viśet . .
homaṃ tatra prakurvīta ebhirmantrapadairvaraiḥ3 . . 38
1.31.d:
एवं मौनेन चागत्य ततो वह्निगृहं व्रजेत् ।
प्रक्षाल्य च मृदा पादावाचान्तोग्निगृहं विशेत् ॥
होमं तत्र प्रकुर्वीत एभिर्मन्त्रपदैर्वरैः3 ॥ 38
1.31.m: Thus coming in silence, he should then go to the fire chamber. / Having washed his feet with clay and sipped water, he should enter the fire chamber; / there he should perform fire offerings with these excellent mantra verses:

1.31.s:
śarvāya śarvaputrāya kṣoṇyutsaṅgabhavāya ca .
kujāya lalitāṅgāya lohitāṅgāya vai tathā . . 39
1.31.d:
शर्वाय शर्वपुत्राय क्षोण्युत्सङ्गभवाय च ।
कुजाय ललिताङ्गाय लोहिताङ्गाय वै तथा ॥ 39
1.31.m: ‘To Śarva, to the son of Śarva, to him born of the lap of the earth, / to Kuja, to him of lovely limbs, and to him of red limbs,’

1.31.s:
oṃkārapūrvakairmantraiḥ svāhākārasamanvitaiḥ .
aṣṭottaraśataṃ vīra ardhārdhamardhameva ca . . 1.31.40
1.31.d:
ओंकारपूर्वकैर्मन्त्रैः स्वाहाकारसमन्वितैः ।
अष्टोत्तरशतं वीर अर्धार्धमर्धमेव च ॥ 1.31.40
1.31.m: with mantras preceded by the syllable Om and accompanied by the exclamation Svāhā, / one hundred and eight times, O hero, or half of half of that, or half.

1.31.s:
etairmantrapadairbhaktyā śaktyā vā kāmato nṛpa .
khādiraiḥ susamidbhistu cājyadugdhairyavaistilaiḥ . . 41
1.31.d:
एतैर्मन्त्रपदैर्भक्त्या शक्त्या वा कामतो नृप ।
खादिरैः सुसमिद्भिस्तु चाज्यदुग्धैर्यवैस्तिलैः ॥ 41
1.31.m: With these mantra words, with devotion, or according to capacity or desire, O king, / with fine sacrificial sticks of khadira wood, clarified butter, milk, barley, and sesame,

1.31.s:
bhakṣyairnānāvidhaiścānyaiḥ śaktyā bhaktyā samanvitaḥ .
hutvāhutīstato4 vīra devaṃ saṃsthāpayetkṣitau . . 42
1.31.d:
भक्ष्यैर्नानाविधैश्चान्यैः शक्त्या भक्त्या समन्वितः ।
हुत्वाहुतीस्ततो4 वीर देवं संस्थापयेत्क्षितौ ॥ 42
1.31.m: and with other food offerings of various kinds, endowed with capacity and devotion, / having offered the oblations, O hero, one should then install the deity upon the ground;

1.31.s:
sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ vāpi śaktyā dārumayaṃ nṛpa .
devadārumayaṃ vāpi śrīkhaṇḍacandanairapi . . 43
1.31.d:
सौवर्णं राजतं वापि शक्त्या दारुमयं नृप ।
देवदारुमयं वापि श्रीखण्डचन्दनैरपि ॥ 43
1.31.m: made of gold or of silver, or according to one's means made of wood, O king, / or made of devadāru, or of śrīkhaṇḍa sandalwood.

1.31.s:
tāmre pātre raupyamaye cājyakuṅkumakesaraiḥ .
anyairvā lohitairvāpi puṣpaiḥ patraiḥ phalairapi . .
raktaiśca vividhairvīra atha vā śaktito'rcayet1 . . 44
1.31.d:
ताम्रे पात्रे रौप्यमये चाज्यकुङ्कुमकेसरैः ।
अन्यैर्वा लोहितैर्वापि पुष्पैः पत्रैः फलैरपि ॥
रक्तैश्च विविधैर्वीर अथ वा शक्तितोऽर्चयेत्1 ॥ 44
1.31.m: In a copper or silver vessel, with clarified butter and saffron stamens, / or with other red flowers, leaves, and fruits, / and with various red [offerings], O hero, or else worship according to one's means.

1.31.s:
yāvadvisṛjate vittaṃ vittavānvīra bhaktitaḥ .
tāvadvivardhate puṇyaṃ dātuṃ śatasahasrikam . . 45
1.31.d:
यावद्विसृजते वित्तं वित्तवान्वीर भक्तितः ।
तावद्विवर्धते पुण्यं दातुं शतसहस्रिकम् ॥ 45
1.31.m: As much wealth as a wealthy man gives out from devotion, O hero, / so much does the merit increase for the giver, a hundred-thousandfold.

1.31.s:
anye tāmramaye pātre vaṃśaje mṛnmaye'pi vā .
pūjayanti narāḥ śaktyā kṛtvā kuṅkumakeśaraiḥ . .
puruṣākṛtikṛtaṃ pātra imaṃ mantraiḥ samarcayet . . 46
1.31.d:
अन्ये ताम्रमये पात्रे वंशजे मृन्मयेऽपि वा ।
पूजयन्ति नराः शक्त्या कृत्वा कुङ्कुमकेशरैः ॥
पुरुषाकृतिकृतं पात्र इमं मन्त्रैः समर्चयेत् ॥ 46
1.31.m: Others, according to their means, worship in a copper vessel, / or one made of bamboo or clay, having made [an image] with saffron stamens; / one should worship this [image] made in human form in the vessel with mantras:

1.31.s:
agrirmūrdheti mantreṇa gandhapuṣpādibhistathā .
dhūpairabhyarcya vidhivadbrāhmaṇāya pradīyate . . 47
1.31.d:
अग्रिर्मूर्धेति मन्त्रेण गन्धपुष्पादिभिस्तथा ।
धूपैरभ्यर्च्य विधिवद्ब्राह्मणाय प्रदीयते ॥ 47
1.31.m: with the mantra 'Agni is the head,' and likewise with perfume, flowers, and the like, / having worshipped duly with incenses, it is given to a brāhmaṇa.

1.31.s:
guḍaudanaṃ ghṛtaṃ kṣīraṃ godhūmāñchālitaṇḍulān ...
avekṣya śaktiṃ dadyādvai daridro vittavāṃstathā . . 48
1.31.d:
गुडौदनं घृतं क्षीरं गोधूमाञ्छालितण्डुलान् ॥।
अवेक्ष्य शक्तिं दद्याद्वै दरिद्रो वित्तवांस्तथा ॥ 48
1.31.m: Boiled rice with jaggery, ghee, milk, wheat, and husked rice of winter rice... / having considered his means, both a poor and a wealthy man should indeed give.

1.31.s:
vittaśāṭhyaṃ na kartavyaṃ vidyamāne dhane nṛpa .
vittaśāṭhyaṃ hi kurvāṇo nāmutra balabhāgbhavet . .4 9
śatānīka uvāca
aṅgārakeṇa saṃyuktā caturthī naktabhojanaiḥ .
upoṣyā katimātrā tu utāho sakṛdeva tu2 . . 1.31.50
1.31.d:
वित्तशाठ्यं न कर्तव्यं विद्यमाने धने नृप ।
वित्तशाठ्यं हि कुर्वाणो नामुत्र बलभाग्भवेत् ॥4 9
शतानीक उवाच
अङ्गारकेण संयुक्ता चतुर्थी नक्तभोजनैः ।
उपोष्या कतिमात्रा तु उताहो सकृदेव तु2 ॥ 1.31.50
1.31.m:
Deceit regarding wealth should not be committed when money is present, O king; / for one who acts with deceit regarding wealth does not share in its fruit in the other world.
Śatānīka said:
The caturthī conjoined with Tuesday, observed by nocturnal meals: / how many [times] is it to be observed as a fast, or is it only once?

1.31.s:
sumanturuvāca
caturthī sā caturthī sā yadāṅgārakasaṃyutā .
upoṣyā tatra tatraiva pradeyo vidhivadguḍaḥ . . 51
1.31.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
चतुर्थी सा चतुर्थी सा यदाङ्गारकसंयुता ।
उपोष्या तत्र तत्रैव प्रदेयो विधिवद्गुडः ॥ 51
1.31.m:
Sumantu said:
Whenever that caturthī is joined with Tuesday, / on each and every such [day] one must fast, and jaggery must be given duly.

1.31.s:
upoṣya naktena vibho catasraḥ kujasaṃyutā .
caturthyāṃ ca caturthyāṃ ca vidhānaṃ śṛṇu yādṛśam . . 52
1.31.d:
उपोष्य नक्तेन विभो चतस्रः कुजसंयुता ।
चतुर्थ्यां च चतुर्थ्यां च विधानं शृणु यादृशम् ॥ 52
1.31.m: Having fasted with a nocturnal meal, O lord, on four [caturthīs] joined with Mars, / on each caturthī, hear what kind of rite [is performed].

1.31.s:
sauvarṇaṃ tu kujaṃ kṛtvā savināyakamādarāt .
daśasauvarṇikaṃ mukhyaṃ daśārdhamardhameva ca . .5 3
sauvarṇapātre raupye vā bhaktyā tāmramaye'pi vā .
viṃśatpalāni pātrāṇi viṃśatyardhapalāni vā . . 54
1.31.d:
सौवर्णं तु कुजं कृत्वा सविनायकमादरात् ।
दशसौवर्णिकं मुख्यं दशार्धमर्धमेव च ॥5 3
सौवर्णपात्रे रौप्ये वा भक्त्या ताम्रमयेऽपि वा ।
विंशत्पलानि पात्राणि विंशत्यर्धपलानि वा ॥ 54
1.31.m:
Having made a golden Mars together with Vināyaka with reverence, / ten suvarṇas [in weight] is the highest, or five [suvarṇas], or even half of that;
in a golden, silver, or out of devotion even a copper vessel, / vessels of twenty palas, or of ten palas,

1.31.s:
viṃśatkarṣāṇi vā vīra viṃśadardhārdhameva vā .
raupyasaṅkhyaṃ palaṃ kāryaṃ palārdhamardhameva ca . . 55
1.31.d:
विंशत्कर्षाणि वा वीर विंशदर्धार्धमेव वा ।
रौप्यसङ्ख्यं पलं कार्यं पलार्धमर्धमेव च ॥ 55
1.31.m: or twenty karṣas, O hero, or half of half of twenty; / in silver weight, a pala should be made, or half a pala, or even half of that.

1.31.s:
śaktyā vittaiśca bhaktyā ca pātre tāmramaye'pi tu .
pratiṣṭhāpya graheśaṃ vai vastraiḥ sampariveṣṭitam . .
vividhaiḥ sādhakai raktaiḥ puṣpai raktaiḥ samanvitam . . 56
1.31.d:
शक्त्या वित्तैश्च भक्त्या च पात्रे ताम्रमयेऽपि तु ।
प्रतिष्ठाप्य ग्रहेशं वै वस्त्रैः सम्परिवेष्टितम् ॥
विविधैः साधकै रक्तैः पुष्पै रक्तैः समन्वितम् ॥ 56
1.31.m: According to one's capacity, wealth, and devotion, in a copper vessel / having established the lord of the planet wrapped in clothes, / accompanied by various red items of accomplishment and red flowers,

1.31.s:
brāhmaṇāya sadā dadyāddakṣiṇāsahitaṃ nṛpa .
vācakāya mahābāho guṇine śreyase nṛpa . . 57
1.31.d:
ब्राह्मणाय सदा दद्याद्दक्षिणासहितं नृप ।
वाचकाय महाबाहो गुणिने श्रेयसे नृप ॥ 57
1.31.m: one should always give it to a brāhmaṇa together with a sacrificial fee, O king, / to a reciter, O mighty-armed one, endowed with virtue, for auspiciousness, O king.

1.31.s:
iti te kathitā puṇyā tithīnāmuttamā tithiḥ .
yāmupoṣya naro rūpaṃ divyamāpnoti bhārata . . 58
1.31.d:
इति ते कथिता पुण्या तिथीनामुत्तमा तिथिः ।
यामुपोष्य नरो रूपं दिव्यमाप्नोति भारत ॥ 58
1.31.m: Thus has been told to you the sacred, best lunar day among lunar days, / fasting upon which a man attains divine form, O Bhārata,

1.31.s:
kāntyātreyasamaṃ vīraṃ tejasā ravisannibham .
prabhayā ravikalpaṃ ca samīrabalasaṃśritam . . 59
1.31.d:
कान्त्यात्रेयसमं वीरं तेजसा रविसन्निभम् ।
प्रभया रविकल्पं च समीरबलसंश्रितम् ॥ 59
1.31.m: equal to Candra in radiance, heroic, resembling the sun in splendour, / like the sun in lustre, and endowed with the strength of the wind.

1.31.s:
īdṛgrūpaṃ samāpyeha yāti bhaumasado nṛpa .
prasādādvighnanāthasya tathā gaṇapaternṛpa . . 1.31.60
1.31.d:
ईदृग्रूपं समाप्येह याति भौमसदो नृप ।
प्रसादाद्विघ्ननाथस्य तथा गणपतेर्नृप ॥ 1.31.60
1.31.m: Attaining such a form here, he goes to the realm of Mars, O king, / through the grace of the Lord of Obstacles and likewise of Gaṇapati, O king.

1.31.s:
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ rājankurvatāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .
brahmahatyādipāpāni kṣīyante nātra saṃśayaḥ . .
ṛddhiṃ vṛddhiṃ tathā lakṣmīṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ . . . 61
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi caturthīkalpe
sukhāvahāṅgārakacaturthīvratanirūpaṇaṃ nāmaikatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 31 .
( samāptaścāyaṃ caturthīkalpaḥ)
nāgapañcamīpūjanam
1.31.d:
पठतां शृण्वतां राजन्कुर्वतां च विशेषतः ।
ब्रह्महत्यादिपापानि क्षीयन्ते नात्र संशयः ॥
ऋद्धिं वृद्धिं तथा लक्ष्मीं लभते नात्र संशयः ॥ । 61
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि चतुर्थीकल्पे
सुखावहाङ्गारकचतुर्थीव्रतनिरूपणं नामैकत्रिंशोऽध्यायः । 31 ।
( समाप्तश्चायं चतुर्थीकल्पः)
नागपञ्चमीपूजनम्
1.31.m:
For those who recite, hear, and especially perform this, O king, / sins such as the murder of a brāhmaṇa are destroyed; of this there is no doubt. / One obtains prosperity, increase, and fortune; of this there is no doubt.
Thus ends the thirty-first chapter, entitled 'Explanation of the Joy-Bestowing Aṅgārakacaturthī Vrata' in the Caturthīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty-five thousand verses.
(And this Caturthīkalpa is concluded.)
Worship on Nāgapañcamī

1.32.s:
sumanturuvāca
pañcamī dayitā rājannāgānāṃ nandivardhinī .
pañcamyāṃ kila nāgānāṃ bhavatītyutsavo mahān . . 1
1.32.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
पञ्चमी दयिता राजन्नागानां नन्दिवर्धिनी ।
पञ्चम्यां किल नागानां भवतीत्युत्सवो महान् ॥ 1
1.32.m:
Sumantu said:
The pañcamī is beloved of the serpents, O king, increasing joy; / on the pañcamī, indeed, a great festival of the serpents takes place.

1.32.s:
vāsukistakṣakaścaiva kāliyo maṇibhadrakaḥ .
airāvato dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ1 karkoṭakadhanañjayau . .
ete prayacchantyabhayaṃ prāṇināṃ prāṇajīvitām . . 2
1.32.d:
वासुकिस्तक्षकश्चैव कालियो मणिभद्रकः ।
ऐरावतो धृतराष्ट्रः1 कर्कोटकधनञ्जयौ ॥
एते प्रयच्छन्त्यभयं प्राणिनां प्राणजीविताम् ॥ 2
1.32.m: Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Kāliya, Maṇibhadraka, / Airāvata, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Karkoṭaka, and Dhanañjaya: / these grant safety to the lives of living beings.

1.32.s:
pañcamyāṃ snapayantīha nāgānkṣīreṇa ye narāḥ .
teṣāṃ kule prayacchanti te'bhayaprāṇadakṣiṇām . . 3
1.32.d:
पञ्चम्यां स्नपयन्तीह नागान्क्षीरेण ये नराः ।
तेषां कुले प्रयच्छन्ति तेऽभयप्राणदक्षिणाम् ॥ 3
1.32.m: Those men who bathe the serpents with milk here on the pañcamī, / in their family they grant the fee of fearlessness and life.

1.32.s:
śaptā nāgā yadā mātrā dahyamānā divāniśam .
nirvāpayanti snapanairgavāṃ3 kṣīreṇa miśritaiḥ . . 4
1.32.d:
शप्ता नागा यदा मात्रा दह्यमाना दिवानिशम् ।
निर्वापयन्ति स्नपनैर्गवां3 क्षीरेण मिश्रितैः ॥ 4
1.32.m: When the serpents were cursed by their mother, burning day and night, / they cool [them] with baths mixed with cow's milk.

1.32.s:
ye snapayanti vai nāgānbhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitā .
teṣāṃ kule sarpabhayaṃ na bhavediti niścayaḥ . . 5
1.32.d:
ये स्नपयन्ति वै नागान्भक्त्या श्रद्धासमन्विता ।
तेषां कुले सर्पभयं न भवेदिति निश्चयः ॥ 5
1.32.m: Those who bathe the serpents with devotion, endowed with faith, / in their family there will be no fear of snakes: this is certain.

1.32.s:
śatānīka uvāca
mātrā śaptāḥ kathaṃ nāgāḥ kiṃ samuddiśya kāraṇam .
kathaṃ cānandakaraṇaṃ kasya vā samprasādajam . . 6
1.32.d:
शतानीक उवाच
मात्रा शप्ताः कथं नागाः किं समुद्दिश्य कारणम् ।
कथं चानन्दकरणं कस्य वा सम्प्रसादजम् ॥ 6
1.32.m:
Śatānīka said:
How were the serpents cursed by their mother? What was the reason behind it? / And how did the bringing of joy arise, and born from whose favour?

1.32.s:
sumanturuvāca
uccaiḥśravā aśvaratnaṃ śveto jāto'mṛtodbhavaḥ .
taṃ dṛṣṭvā cābravītkadrūrnāgānāṃ jananī svasām . . 7
1.32.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
उच्चैःश्रवा अश्वरत्नं श्वेतो जातोऽमृतोद्भवः ।
तं दृष्ट्वा चाब्रवीत्कद्रूर्नागानां जननी स्वसाम् ॥ 7
1.32.m:
Sumantu said:
Uccaiḥśravas, the jewel among horses, was born white, arisen from the nectar [of churning]. / Seeing him, Kadrū, the mother of the serpents, said to her sister:

1.32.s:
aśvaratnamidaṃ śvetaṃ samprekṣe'mṛtasambhavam .
kṛṣṇāṃśca vīkṣase bālānsarvaṃ śvetamutāmbare . . 8
1.32.d:
अश्वरत्नमिदं श्वेतं सम्प्रेक्षेऽमृतसम्भवम् ।
कृष्णांश्च वीक्षसे बालान्सर्वं श्वेतमुताम्बरे ॥ 8
1.32.m: 'I see this jewel of a horse, white, born from the nectar. / Do you see black hairs, or all white, in the sky?'

1.32.s:
vinatovāca
sarvaśveto hayavaro nāsya kṛṣṇo na lohitaḥ .
kathaṃ paśyasi kṛṣṇaṃ tvaṃ vinatovāca tāṃ svasām4 . . 9
1.32.d:
विनतोवाच
सर्वश्वेतो हयवरो नास्य कृष्णो न लोहितः ।
कथं पश्यसि कृष्णं त्वं विनतोवाच तां स्वसाम्4 ॥ 9
1.32.m:
Vinatā said:
'The excellent horse is all white; he is neither black nor red. / How do you see black?' Vinatā said to that sister.

1.32.s:
kadrūruvāca
vīkṣe'hamekanayanā kṛṣṇabālasamanvitam .
dvinetrā tvaṃ tu vinate na paśyasi paṇaṃ kuru . . 1.32.10
1.32.d:
कद्रूरुवाच
वीक्षेऽहमेकनयना कृष्णबालसमन्वितम् ।
द्विनेत्रा त्वं तु विनते न पश्यसि पणं कुरु ॥ 1.32.10
1.32.m:
Kadrū said:
'I, having one eye, see him endowed with black hairs. / You, with two eyes, Vinatā, do not see; make a wager!'

1.32.s:
vinatovāca
ahaṃ dāsī bhavitrī te kṛṣṇe keśe pradarśite .
na ceddarśayase kadru mama dāsī bhaviṣyasi . . 11
1.32.d:
विनतोवाच
अहं दासी भवित्री ते कृष्णे केशे प्रदर्शिते ।
न चेद्दर्शयसे कद्रु मम दासी भविष्यसि ॥ 11
1.32.m:
Vinatā said:
'I will become your slave if a black hair is shown; / if you do not show it, Kadrū, you will become my slave.'

1.32.s:
evaṃ te vipaṇaṃ kṛtvā gate krodhasamanvite .
vinatā śayane suptā kadrūrjihmamacintayat . . 12
1.32.d:
एवं ते विपणं कृत्वा गते क्रोधसमन्विते ।
विनता शयने सुप्ता कद्रूर्जिह्ममचिन्तयत् ॥ 12
1.32.m: Having thus made the wager, both went away filled with anger. / Vinatā slept on her bed; Kadrū conceived deceit.

1.32.s:
āhūya putrānprovāca bālā bhūtvā hayottame .
tiṣṭhadhvaṃ vipaṇe jeṣye vinatāṃ jayagarddhinīm . . 13
1.32.d:
आहूय पुत्रान्प्रोवाच बाला भूत्वा हयोत्तमे ।
तिष्ठध्वं विपणे जेष्ये विनतां जयगर्द्धिनीम् ॥ 13
1.32.m: Calling her sons, she said: 'Becoming hairs on the excellent horse, / stay there! In the wager I will conquer Vinatā, who is greedy for victory.'

1.32.s:
procuste jihmabuddhiṃ tāṃ nāgā mātāṃ1 vigṛhya tu .
adharmyametanmātaste na kariṣyāma te vacaḥ . . 14
1.32.d:
प्रोचुस्ते जिह्मबुद्धिं तां नागा मातां1 विगृह्य तु ।
अधर्म्यमेतन्मातस्ते न करिष्याम ते वचः ॥ 14
1.32.m: The serpents, opposing their mother, spoke to her of crooked mind: / 'This is unrighteous, O mother; we will not carry out your word.'

1.32.s:
tāñśaśāpa ruṣā kadrūḥ pāvako vaḥ pradhakṣyati .
gate bahutithe kāle pāṇḍavo janamejayaḥ . . 15
1.32.d:
ताञ्शशाप रुषा कद्रूः पावको वः प्रधक्ष्यति ।
गते बहुतिथे काले पाण्डवो जनमेजयः ॥ 15
1.32.m: In wrath Kadrū cursed them: 'Fire will consume you! / When a long time has passed, Janamejaya, son of the Pāṇḍava,

1.32.s:
sarpasatraṃ sa kartā vai bhuvi hyanyaiḥ suduṣkaram .
tasminsatre sa tigmāṃśuḥ pāvako vaḥ pradhakṣyati . . 16
1.32.d:
सर्पसत्रं स कर्ता वै भुवि ह्यन्यैः सुदुष्करम् ।
तस्मिन्सत्रे स तिग्मांशुः पावको वः प्रधक्ष्यति ॥ 16
1.32.m: will indeed perform a snake sacrifice on earth, which is very hard for others to perform. / In that sacrifice, that hot-rayed fire will consume you.'

1.32.s:
evaṃ śaptvā ruṣā kadrūḥ kiñcinnoktavatī tu sā .
mātrā śaptāstathā nāgāḥ kartavyaṃ nānvapatsata . . 17
1.32.d:
एवं शप्त्वा रुषा कद्रूः किञ्चिन्नोक्तवती तु सा ।
मात्रा शप्तास्तथा नागाः कर्तव्यं नान्वपत्सत ॥ 17
1.32.m: Having cursed them thus in wrath, she said nothing more. / The serpents, thus cursed by their mother, did not know what was to be done.

1.32.s:
vāsukiṃ duḥkhitaṃ jñātvā brahmā provāca sāntvayan .
mā śuco vāsuke'tyarthaṃ śṛṇu madvacana param . . 18
1.32.d:
वासुकिं दुःखितं ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्मा प्रोवाच सान्त्वयन् ।
मा शुचो वासुकेऽत्यर्थं शृणु मद्वचन परम् ॥ 18
1.32.m: Knowing Vāsuki to be sorrowful, Brahmā spoke, consoling him: / 'Do not grieve excessively, O Vāsuki; hear my supreme word.

1.32.s:
yāyāvarakule jāto jaratkārūriti dvijaḥ .
bhaviṣyati mahātejāstasminkāle taponidhiḥ 1. ( 19
bhaginīṃ ca jaratkāruṃ tasmai tvaṃ pratidāsyasi .
bhavitā tasya putro'sāvāstīka iti viśrutaḥ . . 1.32.20
1.32.d:
यायावरकुले जातो जरत्कारूरिति द्विजः ।
भविष्यति महातेजास्तस्मिन्काले तपोनिधिः 1. ( 19
भगिनीं च जरत्कारुं तस्मै त्वं प्रतिदास्यसि ।
भविता तस्य पुत्रोऽसावास्तीक इति विश्रुतः ॥ 1.32.20
1.32.m: A twice-born named Jaratkāru, born in the family of the Yāyāvaras, / will be of great splendour at that time, a treasury of austerities. / And you will give your sister Jaratkāru to him; / his son will be known as Āstīka.

1.32.s:
sa tatsatraṃ pravṛddhaṃ vai nāgānāṃ bhayadaṃ mahat .
niṣedhetsumatirvāgbhiragryābhistaṃ naviṣyati . . 21
1.32.d:
स तत्सत्रं प्रवृद्धं वै नागानां भयदं महत् ।
निषेधेत्सुमतिर्वाग्भिरग्र्याभिस्तं नविष्यति ॥ 21
1.32.m: He will stop that extended, great sacrifice that causes fear to the serpents; / the wise one will praise him with foremost words.'

1.32.s:
tadimāṃ bhaginīṃ rājaṃstasya tvaṃ pratidāsyasi .
jaratkāruṃ jaratkāroḥ pradadyā avicārayan . . 22
1.32.d:
तदिमां भगिनीं राजंस्तस्य त्वं प्रतिदास्यसि ।
जरत्कारुं जरत्कारोः प्रदद्या अविचारयन् ॥ 22
1.32.m: "Therefore, O king, you must give this sister to him; / you should give Jaratkāru to Jaratkāru without hesitation.

1.32.s:
yadāsau prārthate'raṇye yatkiñciddhi vadiṣyati .
tatkartavyamaśaṅkena yadīccheḥ śreya ātmanaḥ . . 23
1.32.d:
यदासौ प्रार्थतेऽरण्ये यत्किञ्चिद्धि वदिष्यति ।
तत्कर्तव्यमशङ्केन यदीच्छेः श्रेय आत्मनः ॥ 23
1.32.m: Whenever he asks in the forest, and whatever he says, / that must be done without doubt, if you desire your own welfare."

1.32.s:
pitāmahavacaḥ śrutvā vāsukiḥ praṇipatya ca .
tathākarodyathā coktaṃ yatnaṃ ca paramāsthitaḥ . . 24
1.32.d:
पितामहवचः श्रुत्वा वासुकिः प्रणिपत्य च ।
तथाकरोद्यथा चोक्तं यत्नं च परमास्थितः ॥ 24
1.32.m: Having heard the Grandfather's words and bowed down, / Vāsuki did as had been said, making the utmost effort.

1.32.s:
tacchrutvā pannagāḥ sarve praharṣotphullalocanāḥ .
punarjātamivātmānaṃ menire bhujagottamāḥ . . 25
1.32.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा पन्नगाः सर्वे प्रहर्षोत्फुल्ललोचनाः ।
पुनर्जातमिवात्मानं मेनिरे भुजगोत्तमाः ॥ 25
1.32.m: Hearing that, all the serpents, their eyes blossoming with joy, / considered themselves to be as if born anew, best of snakes.

1.32.s:
tatra satraṃ mahābāho1 tava pitrā pravartitam .
ṛtvigbhiḥ sa hi teneha sarvalokeṣu duṣkaram . . 26
1.32.d:
तत्र सत्रं महाबाहो1 तव पित्रा प्रवर्तितम् ।
ऋत्विग्भिः स हि तेनेह सर्वलोकेषु दुष्करम् ॥ 26
1.32.m: There, O mighty-armed one, that sacrificial session was set in motion by your father; / for along with priests, he performed here what was difficult to do in all the worlds.

1.32.s:
proktaṃ ca viṣṇunā pūrvaṃ dharmaputrasya dhīmataḥ .
avaśyaṃ tasya bhavitā nāgānāṃ bhayakārakam3 . . 27
1.32.d:
प्रोक्तं च विष्णुना पूर्वं धर्मपुत्रस्य धीमतः ।
अवश्यं तस्य भविता नागानां भयकारकम्3 ॥ 27
1.32.m: And it was declared of old by Viṣṇu to the wise son of Dharma: / 'Inevitably it will happen, causing fear to the snakes.

1.32.s:
tasmātkālāntarādrājansāgre varṣaśate gate .
tatsatraṃ bhavitā ghoraṃ nāgānāṃ kṣayakārakam . . 28
1.32.d:
तस्मात्कालान्तराद्राजन्साग्रे वर्षशते गते ।
तत्सत्रं भविता घोरं नागानां क्षयकारकम् ॥ 28
1.32.m: From that lapse of time, O king, when a hundred years and more have passed, / that terrible sacrificial session will take place, causing the destruction of the snakes.

1.32.s:
yāsyantyadharmabharitā dandaśūkā viṣolbaṇāḥ .
koṭisaṅkhyā mahārāja nipatiṣyantyaharniśam . . 29
1.32.d:
यास्यन्त्यधर्मभरिता दन्दशूका विषोल्बणाः ।
कोटिसङ्ख्या महाराज निपतिष्यन्त्यहर्निशम् ॥ 29
1.32.m: Filled with unrighteousness, serpents terrible with venom will go; / numbered in tens of millions, O great king, they will fall day and night.

1.32.s:
apūrve tu nimagnānāṃ ghore raudrāgnisāgare .
āstīkastatra bhavitā teṣāṃ naurvahnisāgare . . 1.32.30
1.32.d:
अपूर्वे तु निमग्नानां घोरे रौद्राग्निसागरे ।
आस्तीकस्तत्र भविता तेषां नौर्वह्निसागरे ॥ 1.32.30
1.32.m: For those submerged in that unprecedented, terrible ocean of fearful fire, / Āstīka will become a boat in that ocean of fire.'

1.32.s:
śrutvā sa cāgniṃ rājānamṛtvijastadanantaram .
nivartayiṣyate yāgaṃ nāgānāṃ mohanaṃ param . . 31
1.32.d:
श्रुत्वा स चाग्निं राजानमृत्विजस्तदनन्तरम् ।
निवर्तयिष्यते यागं नागानां मोहनं परम् ॥ 31
1.32.m: Hearing him, the fire, the king, and the priests immediately thereafter / will cause to cease that sacrifice that utterly stuns the snakes.

1.32.s:
pañcamyāṃ tatra bhavitā brahmā provāca lelihān .
tasmādiyaṃ mahābāho pañcamī dayitā sadā . .
nāgānāmānandakarī dattā vai brahmaṇā purā . . 32
1.32.d:
पञ्चम्यां तत्र भविता ब्रह्मा प्रोवाच लेलिहान् ।
तस्मादियं महाबाहो पञ्चमी दयिता सदा ॥
नागानामानन्दकरी दत्ता वै ब्रह्मणा पुरा ॥ 32
1.32.m: "On the fifth [lunar day] it will happen there," Brahmā said to the serpents. / Therefore, O mighty-armed one, this fifth [lunar day] is ever beloved, / causing joy to the snakes, given indeed by Brahmā of old.

1.32.s:
kṛtvā tu bhojanaṃ pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ tu kāmataḥ .
visṛjya nāgāḥ prīyantāṃ ye kecitpṛthivītale . . 33
1.32.d:
कृत्वा तु भोजनं पूर्वं ब्राह्मणानां तु कामतः ।
विसृज्य नागाः प्रीयन्तां ये केचित्पृथिवीतले ॥ 33
1.32.m: Having first fed the brāhmaṇas according to desire, / having dismissed [them], [one should say]: 'May the snakes, whoever they may be on the surface of the earth, be pleased!

1.32.s:
ye ca helimarīcisthā ye'ntare divi saṃsthitāḥ .
ye nadīṣu mahānāgā ye sarasvatigāminaḥ . .
ye ca vāpītaḍāgeṣu teṣu sarveṣu vai namaḥ . . 34
1.32.d:
ये च हेलिमरीचिस्था येऽन्तरे दिवि संस्थिताः ।
ये नदीषु महानागा ये सरस्वतिगामिनः ॥
ये च वापीतडागेषु तेषु सर्वेषु वै नमः ॥ 34
1.32.m: And those that dwell in the rays of the sun, those that dwell in the intermediate realm and heaven, / the great snakes that are in rivers, those that go along the Sarasvatī, / and those that are in wells and tanks—to all of them, indeed, homage!'

1.32.s:
nāgānviprāṃśca sampūjya visṛjya ca yathārthataḥ .
tataḥ paścāttu bhuñjīta saha bhṛtyairnarādhipa . . 35
1.32.d:
नागान्विप्रांश्च सम्पूज्य विसृज्य च यथार्थतः ।
ततः पश्चात्तु भुञ्जीत सह भृत्यैर्नराधिप ॥ 35
1.32.m: Having worshipped the snakes and the brāhmaṇas, and having dismissed them properly, / one should eat afterwards, O lord of men, together with servants.

1.32.s:
pūrvaṃ madhuramaśnīyāttato bhuñjīta kāmataḥ .
evaṃ niyamayuktasya yatphalaṃ tannibodha me . . 36
1.32.d:
पूर्वं मधुरमश्नीयात्ततो भुञ्जीत कामतः ।
एवं नियमयुक्तस्य यत्फलं तन्निबोध मे ॥ 36
1.32.m: One should first eat sweet food, and then eat as desired. / Understand from me the fruit of one who is thus bound by this rule:

1.32.s:
mṛto nāgapuraṃ yāti pūjyamāno'psarogaṇaiḥ .
vimānavaramārūḍho ramate kālamīpsitam . . 37
1.32.d:
मृतो नागपुरं याति पूज्यमानोऽप्सरोगणैः ।
विमानवरमारूढो रमते कालमीप्सितम् ॥ 37
1.32.m: Upon death he goes to the realm of the snakes, worshipped by hosts of apsarases; / mounted on a splendid celestial chariot, he rejoices for the desired time.

1.32.s:
iha cāgatya rājāsāvayutānāṃ1 varo bhavet .
sarvaratnasamṛddhaḥ syādvāhanāḍhyaśca jāyate . . 38
1.32.d:
इह चागत्य राजासावयुतानां1 वरो भवेत् ।
सर्वरत्नसमृद्धः स्याद्वाहनाढ्यश्च जायते ॥ 38
1.32.m: And coming back here, that king becomes the foremost of ten thousand [men]; / he becomes rich in all jewels and is born endowed with mounts.

1.32.s:
pañca janmānyasau rājā dvāpare dvāpare bhavet .
ādhivyādhivinirmuktaḥ patnīputrasahāyavān . .
tasmātpūjyāśca pālyāśca2 ghṛtapāyasaguggulaiḥ . . 39
1.32.d:
पञ्च जन्मान्यसौ राजा द्वापरे द्वापरे भवेत् ।
आधिव्याधिविनिर्मुक्तः पत्नीपुत्रसहायवान् ॥
तस्मात्पूज्याश्च पाल्याश्च2 घृतपायसगुग्गुलैः ॥ 39
1.32.m: For five births this man becomes a king in Dvāpara after Dvāpara, / freed from mental pain and disease, attended by wives and sons. / Therefore [the snakes] should be worshipped and cherished with ghee, rice-milk, and bdellium.

1.32.s:
śatānīka uvāca
daśanti ye naraṃ vipra nāgāḥ krodhasamanvitāḥ .
bhavetkiṃ tasya daṣṭasya vistarād brūhi me dvija . . 1.32.40
1.32.d:
शतानीक उवाच
दशन्ति ये नरं विप्र नागाः क्रोधसमन्विताः ।
भवेत्किं तस्य दष्टस्य विस्तराद् ब्रूहि मे द्विज ॥ 1.32.40
1.32.m:
Śatānīka said:
When snakes filled with anger bite a man, O brāhmaṇa, / what happens to that bitten person? Tell me in detail, O twice-born one.

1.32.s:
sumanturuvāca
nāgadaṣṭo naro rājanprāpya mṛtyuṃ vrajatyadhaḥ .
adho gatyā bhavetsarpo nirviṣo nātra saṃśayaḥ . .4 1
śatānīka uvāca
nāgadaṣṭaḥ pitā yasya bhrātā vā duhitāpi vā .
mātā putro'tha vā bhāryā kiṃ kartavyaṃ vadasva me . . 42
1.32.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
नागदष्टो नरो राजन्प्राप्य मृत्युं व्रजत्यधः ।
अधो गत्या भवेत्सर्पो निर्विषो नात्र संशयः ॥4 1
शतानीक उवाच
नागदष्टः पिता यस्य भ्राता वा दुहितापि वा ।
माता पुत्रोऽथ वा भार्या किं कर्तव्यं वदस्व मे ॥ 42
1.32.m:
Sumantu said:
A man bitten by a snake, O king, having met death, goes downward; / by that downward course he becomes a poisonless snake; of this there is no doubt.
Śatānīka said:
One whose father, or brother, or daughter, / mother, son, or wife is bitten by a snake—tell me, what should be done?

1.32.s:
mokṣāya tasya viprendra dānaṃ vratamupoṣaṇam .
brūhi taddvijaśārdūla yena tadvai karomyaham . . 43
1.32.d:
मोक्षाय तस्य विप्रेन्द्र दानं व्रतमुपोषणम् ।
ब्रूहि तद्द्विजशार्दूल येन तद्वै करोम्यहम् ॥ 43
1.32.m: For the liberation of such a one, O best of brāhmaṇas, tell me of a gift, a votive observance, or a fast, / O tiger among the twice-born, by which I may indeed do that.

1.32.s:
sumanturuvāca
upoṣyā pañcamī rājannāgānāṃ puṣṭivardhinī .
tvamevamekaṃ rājendra vidhānaṃ śṛṇu bhārata . . 44
1.32.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
उपोष्या पञ्चमी राजन्नागानां पुष्टिवर्धिनी ।
त्वमेवमेकं राजेन्द्र विधानं शृणु भारत ॥ 44
1.32.m:
Sumantu said:
The fifth lunar day, which increases the vitality of the snakes, should be fasted, O king. / Hear from me this single procedure in this way, O best of kings, descendant of Bharata.

1.32.s:
māsi bhādrapade yā tu kṛṣṇapakṣe1 mahīpate .
mahāpuṇyā tu sā proktā grāhyāpi ca mahīpate . .45
1.32.d:
मासि भाद्रपदे या तु कृष्णपक्षे1 महीपते ।
महापुण्या तु सा प्रोक्ता ग्राह्यापि च महीपते ॥45
1.32.m: The one that occurs in the dark fortnight in the month of Bhādrapada, O lord of earth, / that is declared to be exceedingly meritorious and should be undertaken, O lord of earth.

1.32.s:
jñeyā dvādaśa ṣañcamyo hāyane bharatarṣabha .
cartuthyāṃ tvekabhaktaṃ tu tasyāṃ naktaṃ prakīrtitam . .4 6
bhuvi citramayānnāgānatha vā kaladhautakān .
kṛtvā dārumayānvāpi atha vā mṛnmayānnṛpa . .47
1.32.d:
ज्ञेया द्वादश षञ्चम्यो हायने भरतर्षभ ।
चर्तुथ्यां त्वेकभक्तं तु तस्यां नक्तं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥4 6
भुवि चित्रमयान्नागानथ वा कलधौतकान् ।
कृत्वा दारुमयान्वापि अथ वा मृन्मयान्नृप ॥47
1.32.m: Twelve fifth [lunar days] are to be known in a year, O bull of the Bharatas; / on the fourth [lunar day] one should eat only one meal, and on that [fifth day] a nocturnal meal is prescribed. / Having made snakes on the ground out of painted images, or out of silver, / or having made them of wood, or out of clay, O king,

1.32.s:
pañcamyāmarcayedbhaktyā nāgānāṃ pañcakaṃ nṛpa .
karavīraiḥ śatapatrairjātīpuṣpaiśca suvrata . . 48
1.32.d:
पञ्चम्यामर्चयेद्भक्त्या नागानां पञ्चकं नृप ।
करवीरैः शतपत्रैर्जातीपुष्पैश्च सुव्रत ॥ 48
1.32.m: on the fifth [lunar day] one should worship with devotion the pentad of snakes, O king, / with oleanders, hundred-petalled lotuses, and jasmine flowers, O observer of vows,

1.32.s:
tathā gandhaiśca dhūpaiśca pūjya pañcakamuttamam3 .
brāhmaṇaṃ bhojayetpaścād ghṛtapāyasamodakaiḥ . .4 9
ananto vāsukiḥ śaṅkhaḥ padmaḥ kambala eva ca .
tathā karkoṭako nāgo nāgo hyaśvataro nṛpa . . 1.32.50
1.32.d:
तथा गन्धैश्च धूपैश्च पूज्य पञ्चकमुत्तमम्3 ।
ब्राह्मणं भोजयेत्पश्चाद् घृतपायसमोदकैः ॥4 9
अनन्तो वासुकिः शङ्खः पद्मः कम्बल एव च ।
तथा कर्कोटको नागो नागो ह्यश्वतरो नृप ॥ 1.32.50
1.32.m: and with scents and incenses. Having worshipped that supreme pentad, / one should afterwards feed a brāhmaṇa with ghee, rice-milk, and sweet cakes: / Ananta, Vāsuki, Śaṅkha, Padma, and Kambala; / likewise the snake Karkoṭaka, and the snake Aśvatara, O king;

1.32.s:
dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ śaṅkhapālaḥ kāliyastakṣakastathā .
piṅgalaśca tathā nāgo māsi māsi prakīrtitāḥ . . 51
1.32.d:
धृतराष्ट्रः शङ्खपालः कालियस्तक्षकस्तथा ।
पिङ्गलश्च तथा नागो मासि मासि प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 51
1.32.m: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Śaṅkhapāla, Kāliya, and Takṣaka, / and likewise the snake Piṅgala are proclaimed month by month.

1.32.s:
vatsarānte pāraṇaṃ syādbrāhmaṇānbhojayedbahūn .
itihāsavide nāgaṃ gairikeṇa kṛtaṃ nṛpa . .
tathārcanā pradātavyā vācakāya mahīpate . . 52
1.32.d:
वत्सरान्ते पारणं स्याद्ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेद्बहून् ।
इतिहासविदे नागं गैरिकेण कृतं नृप ॥
तथार्चना प्रदातव्या वाचकाय महीपते ॥ 52
1.32.m: At the end of the year, there should be the breaking of the fast, and one should feed many brāhmaṇas. / A snake made of red ochre should be given to one who knows the epics, O king, / and worship should likewise be offered to the reciter, O lord of earth.

1.32.s:
eṣa vai nāgapañcamyā5 vidhiḥ proktā budhairnṛpa .
tava pitrā kṛtaścaiva piturmokṣāya bhārata . . 53
1.32.d:
एष वै नागपञ्चम्या5 विधिः प्रोक्ता बुधैर्नृप ।
तव पित्रा कृतश्चैव पितुर्मोक्षाय भारत ॥ 53
1.32.m: This indeed is the procedure of the snake-fifth prescribed by the wise, O king, / and it was performed by your father for the liberation of his father, O descendant of Bharata.

1.32.s:
tvamekamekaṃ vai vīra pañcamyāṃ bharatarṣabha .
suvarṇabhāraniṣpannaṃ nāgaṃ dattvā tathā ca gām . . 54
1.32.d:
त्वमेकमेकं वै वीर पञ्चम्यां भरतर्षभ ।
सुवर्णभारनिष्पन्नं नागं दत्त्वा तथा च गाम् ॥ 54
1.32.m: You, indeed, O hero, bull of the Bharatas, on each fifth [lunar day], / having given a snake made of a bhāra of gold and likewise a cow

1.32.s:
vyāsāya kuruśārdūla piturānṛṇyamāpnuyāḥ .
tava pitrā kṛtā hyevaṃ pañcamyupāsanā nṛpa . . 55
1.32.d:
व्यासाय कुरुशार्दूल पितुरानृण्यमाप्नुयाः ।
तव पित्रा कृता ह्येवं पञ्चम्युपासना नृप ॥ 55
1.32.m: to Vyāsa, O tiger of the Kurus, would attain release from the debt to your father. / For thus was the worship of the fifth [lunar day] performed by your father, O king.

1.32.s:
utsṛjya nāgatāṃ vīra tava pūrvapitāmahaḥ .
puṣpottaraṃ sado gatvā tathā puṣpasado nṛpa . . 56
1.32.d:
उत्सृज्य नागतां वीर तव पूर्वपितामहः ।
पुष्पोत्तरं सदो गत्वा तथा पुष्पसदो नृप ॥ 56
1.32.m: Abandoning snakedom, O hero, your father's grandfather / went to the Puṣpottara assembly, and likewise to the Puṣpa assembly, O king;

1.32.s:
sunāsīrasado gatvā tadā bhargasado gataḥ .
svabhūsadastato gatvā kañjajasya sado gataḥ . . 57
1.32.d:
सुनासीरसदो गत्वा तदा भर्गसदो गतः ।
स्वभूसदस्ततो गत्वा कञ्जजस्य सदो गतः ॥ 57
1.32.m: having gone to the assembly of Sunāsīra, he then went to the assembly of Bharga; / having then gone to the assembly of the Self-born, he went to the assembly of the Lotus-born.

1.32.s:
anye'pi ye kariṣyanti idaṃ vratamanuttamam .
daṣṭako mokṣyate teṣāṃ śubhaṃ sthānamavāpsyati . . 58
1.32.d:
अन्येऽपि ये करिष्यन्ति इदं व्रतमनुत्तमम् ।
दष्टको मोक्ष्यते तेषां शुभं स्थानमवाप्स्यति ॥ 58
1.32.m: Others also who will perform this incomparable votive observance— / their bitten [kinsman] will be liberated and will attain an auspicious state.

1.32.s:
yaścedaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ naraḥ1 śraddhāsamanvitaḥ .
kule tasya na nāgebhyo bhayaṃ bhavati kutracit . . 59
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi pañcamīkalpe
nāgapañcamīvratavarṇanaṃ nāma dvātriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 32 .
sarpabhedam
1.32.d:
यश्चेदं शृणुयान्नित्यं नरः1 श्रद्धासमन्वितः ।
कुले तस्य न नागेभ्यो भयं भवति कुत्रचित् ॥ 59
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि पञ्चमीकल्पे
नागपञ्चमीव्रतवर्णनं नाम द्वात्रिंशोऽध्यायः । 32 ।
सर्पभेदम्
1.32.m:
And whichever person constantly hears this endowed with faith, / in his family there is never any fear from snakes anywhere.
Thus ends the thirty-second chapter, named 'Description of the Snake-Fifth Votive Observance,' in the Section on the Fifth Lunar Day of the Brāhma Book in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa consisting of fifty thousand verses.
Classification of Snakes

1.33.s:
śatānīka uvāca
sarpāṇāṃ kati rūpāṇi ke varṇāḥ kiṃ ca lakṣaṇam .
kā jātistu bhavetteṣāṃ keṣu yonikuleṣu vā . . 1
1.33.d:
शतानीक उवाच
सर्पाणां कति रूपाणि के वर्णाः किं च लक्षणम् ।
का जातिस्तु भवेत्तेषां केषु योनिकुलेषु वा ॥ 1
1.33.m:
Śatānīka said:
How many forms of snakes are there? What are their colors and what are their characteristics? / What is their caste, or in what wombs and lineages are they born?

1.33.s:
sumanturuvāca
purā merau nagavare kaśyapaṃ tapasāṃ nidhim .
praṇamya śirasā bhaktayā gautamo vākyamabravīt . . 2
1.33.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
पुरा मेरौ नगवरे कश्यपं तपसां निधिम् ।
प्रणम्य शिरसा भक्तया गौतमो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ 2
1.33.m:
Sumantu said:
Formerly on Meru, best of mountains, Gautama bowed his head with devotion / before Kaśyapa, treasury of austerities, and spoke these words:

1.33.s:
sarpāṇāṃ kati rūpāṇi kiṃ cihnaṃ kiṃ ca lakṣaṇam .
jātiṃ kulaṃ tadhā varṇānbrūhi sarvaṃ prajāpate . . 3
1.33.d:
सर्पाणां कति रूपाणि किं चिह्नं किं च लक्षणम् ।
जातिं कुलं तधा वर्णान्ब्रूहि सर्वं प्रजापते ॥ 3
1.33.m: "How many forms of snakes are there? What is their mark and what are their characteristics? / Tell me all of their caste, lineage, and colors, O lord of creatures."

1.33.s:
kathaṃ vā jāyate sarpaḥ kadhaṃ muñcedviṣaṃ prabho .
viṣavegāḥ kati proktāḥ katyeva viṣanāḍikāḥ . .4
1.33.d:
कथं वा जायते सर्पः कधं मुञ्चेद्विषं प्रभो ।
विषवेगाः कति प्रोक्ताः कत्येव विषनाडिकाः ॥4
1.33.m: How is a snake born, or how does it discharge its venom, O lord? / How many are the venom-impulses declared to be, and how many are the venom-channels?

1.33.s:
daṃṣṭrāḥ katividhāḥ proktāḥ kiṃ pramāṇaṃ viṣāgame .
gṛhṇīte tu kadā garbhaṃ kathaṃ ceha prasūyate . . 5
1.33.d:
दंष्ट्राः कतिविधाः प्रोक्ताः किं प्रमाणं विषागमे ।
गृह्णीते तु कदा गर्भं कथं चेह प्रसूयते ॥ 5
1.33.m: How many kinds of fangs are taught, and what is their measure at the arrival of venom? / When does [the female] conceive, and how does she give birth here?

1.33.s:
kīdṛśī strī pumāṃścaiva kīdṛśaśca napuṃsakaḥ .
kiṃ nāma daśanaṃ caiva etatkathaya suvrata . . 6
1.33.d:
कीदृशी स्त्री पुमांश्चैव कीदृशश्च नपुंसकः ।
किं नाम दशनं चैव एतत्कथय सुव्रत ॥ 6
1.33.m: What is the female like, what the male, and what the neuter? / What are the names of the teeth? Tell this, O you of noble vows.

1.33.s:
tasya1 tadvacanaṃ śrutvā kaśyapaḥ pratyabhāṣata .
śṛṇu gautama tattvena sarpāṇāmiha lakṣaṇam . .7
1.33.d:
तस्य1 तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा कश्यपः प्रत्यभाषत ।
शृणु गौतम तत्त्वेन सर्पाणामिह लक्षणम् ॥7
1.33.m: Hearing these words of his, Kaśyapa replied: / "Listen, Gautama, to the characteristics of snakes here in truth.

1.33.s:
māsyāṣāḍhe tathā jyeṣṭhe pramādyanti bhujaṅgamāḥ .
tato nāgo'tha nāgī ca maithune samprapadyate . . 8
1.33.d:
मास्याषाढे तथा ज्येष्ठे प्रमाद्यन्ति भुजङ्गमाः ।
ततो नागोऽथ नागी च मैथुने सम्प्रपद्यते ॥ 8
1.33.m: In the months of Āṣāḍha and Jyeṣṭha, serpents become intoxicated with passion; / then the male serpent and the female serpent unite in sexual union.

1.33.s:
caturo vārṣikānmāsānnāgī garbhamadhārayat .
tataḥ kārttikamāse tu aṇḍakāni prasūyate . . 9
1.33.d:
चतुरो वार्षिकान्मासान्नागी गर्भमधारयत् ।
ततः कार्त्तिकमासे तु अण्डकानि प्रसूयते ॥ 9
1.33.m: The female serpent carries the embryos for the four rainy months; / then, in the month of Kārttika, she lays her eggs.

1.33.s:
aṇḍakānāṃ tu vijñeye dveśate dve ca viṃśatī .
tānyeva bhakṣayetsā tu bhogaikaṃ ghṛṇayā tyajet . . 1.33.10
1.33.d:
अण्डकानां तु विज्ञेये द्वेशते द्वे च विंशती ।
तान्येव भक्षयेत्सा तु भोगैकं घृणया त्यजेत् ॥ 1.33.10
1.33.m: The number of eggs is to be known as two hundred and twenty-two. / She eats those very [eggs], but out of pity she spares a single coil.

1.33.s:
svarṇārkavarṇādvai tasmātpumānsañjāyate'ṇḍakāt .
tānyeva khādate sarpa ahorātrāṇi viṃśatim . . 11
1.33.d:
स्वर्णार्कवर्णाद्वै तस्मात्पुमान्सञ्जायतेऽण्डकात् ।
तान्येव खादते सर्प अहोरात्राणि विंशतिम् ॥ 11
1.33.m: From the egg coloured like gold and the sun, a male is born; / the serpent eats them over twenty nights and days.

1.33.s:
svarṇaketakavarṇābhāddīrgharājīvasannibhāt .
tasmādutpadyate strī vai aṇḍādbrāhmaṇasattama . . 12
1.33.d:
स्वर्णकेतकवर्णाभाद्दीर्घराजीवसन्निभात् ।
तस्मादुत्पद्यते स्त्री वै अण्डाद्ब्राह्मणसत्तम ॥ 12
1.33.m: From [an egg] having the radiance and colour of a golden ketaka blossom and resembling a long lotus, / from that egg a female is born, O best of brahmins.

1.33.s:
śirīṣapuṣpavarṇābhādaṇḍakātsyānnapuṃsakaḥ .
tato bhinatti cāṇḍāni ṣaṇmāsena tu gautama . . 13
1.33.d:
शिरीषपुष्पवर्णाभादण्डकात्स्यान्नपुंसकः ।
ततो भिनत्ति चाण्डानि षण्मासेन तु गौतम ॥ 13
1.33.m: From an egg coloured like a śirīṣa flower, a neuter is born; / then she hatches the eggs in six months, O Gautama.

1.33.s:
tataste prītisambandhātsnehaṃ badhnanti bālakāḥ .
tato'sau saptarātreṇa kṛṣṇo bhavati pannagaḥ . . 14
1.33.d:
ततस्ते प्रीतिसम्बन्धात्स्नेहं बध्नन्ति बालकाः ।
ततोऽसौ सप्तरात्रेण कृष्णो भवति पन्नगः ॥ 14
1.33.m: Then, through the bond of affection, the young develop fondness; / then, within seven nights, the snake turns black.

1.33.s:
āyuḥpramāṇaṃ sarpāṇāṃ śataṃ viṃśottaraṃ smṛtam .
mṛtyuścāṣṭavidho jñeyaḥ śṛṇuṣvātra yathākramam . . 15
1.33.d:
आयुःप्रमाणं सर्पाणां शतं विंशोत्तरं स्मृतम् ।
मृत्युश्चाष्टविधो ज्ञेयः शृणुष्वात्र यथाक्रमम् ॥ 15
1.33.m: The lifespan of snakes is handed down as one hundred and twenty [years]. / Their death is to be known as eightfold; listen to it here in due order:

1.33.s:
mayūrānmānuṣādvāpi cakorādgokhurāttathā2 .
biḍālānnakulāccaiva varāhādvṛścikāttathā . .
eteṣāṃ yadi mucyeta jīvedviṃśottaraṃ śatam . . 16
1.33.d:
मयूरान्मानुषाद्वापि चकोराद्गोखुरात्तथा2 ।
बिडालान्नकुलाच्चैव वराहाद्वृश्चिकात्तथा ॥
एतेषां यदि मुच्येत जीवेद्विंशोत्तरं शतम् ॥ 16
1.33.m: from a peacock, or a human, a cakora bird, a cow's hoof, / a cat, a mongoose, a boar, or a scorpion. / If it escapes these, it lives for one hundred and twenty [years].

1.33.s:
saptāhe tu tataḥ pūrṇe daṃṣṭrāṇāṃ cādhirohaṇam .
viṣasyāgamanaṃ tatra nikṣipecca punaḥ punaḥ . . 17
1.33.d:
सप्ताहे तु ततः पूर्णे दंष्ट्राणां चाधिरोहणम् ।
विषस्यागमनं तत्र निक्षिपेच्च पुनः पुनः ॥ 17
1.33.m: When a week is complete, the ascent of fangs occurs; / the arrival of venom is there, and it discharges it again and again.

1.33.s:
evaṃ jñātvā tu tattvena viṣakarmmārabheta vai .
ekaviṃśatirātreṇa viṣadaṃṣṭrā sujāyate . .
nāgīpārśvasamāvartī bālasarpaḥ sa ucyate . . 18
1.33.d:
एवं ज्ञात्वा तु तत्त्वेन विषकर्म्मारभेत वै ।
एकविंशतिरात्रेण विषदंष्ट्रा सुजायते ॥
नागीपार्श्वसमावर्ती बालसर्पः स उच्यते ॥ 18
1.33.m: Knowing thus in truth, one should undertake the treatment of venom; / in twenty-one nights the venom-fang is properly produced. / Staying near the female serpent's side, it is called a young snake.

1.33.s:
pañcaviṃśatirātrastu sadyaḥ prāṇaharo bhavet .
ṣaṇmāsājjātamātrastu kañcukaṃ vai pramuñcati . . 19
1.33.d:
पञ्चविंशतिरात्रस्तु सद्यः प्राणहरो भवेत् ।
षण्मासाज्जातमात्रस्तु कञ्चुकं वै प्रमुञ्चति ॥ 19
1.33.m: At twenty-five nights it can take life instantly; / six months after being born, it casts off its slough.

1.33.s:
pādānāṃ cāpi vijñeye dve śate dve ca viṃśatī .
golomasadṛśāḥ pādāḥ praviśanti kramanti ca . . 1.33.20
1.33.d:
पादानां चापि विज्ञेये द्वे शते द्वे च विंशती ।
गोलोमसदृशाः पादाः प्रविशन्ति क्रमन्ति च ॥ 1.33.20
1.33.m: The feet are also to be known as two hundred and twenty-two; / feet resembling cow's hair enter and move.

1.33.s:
sandhīnāṃ cāsya vijñeye dveśate viṃśatī tathā .
aṃgulyaścāpi vijñeyā dve śate viṃśatī tathā . . 21
1.33.d:
सन्धीनां चास्य विज्ञेये द्वेशते विंशती तथा ।
अंगुल्यश्चापि विज्ञेया द्वे शते विंशती तथा ॥ 21
1.33.m: Its joints are to be known as two hundred and twenty; / its fingers are also to be known as two hundred and twenty.

1.33.s:
akālajātā ye sarpā nirviṣāste prakīrtitāḥ .
pañcasaptativarṣāṇi āyusteṣāṃ prakīrtitam . . 22
1.33.d:
अकालजाता ये सर्पा निर्विषास्ते प्रकीर्तिताः ।
पञ्चसप्ततिवर्षाणि आयुस्तेषां प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 22
1.33.m: Those snakes born out of season are proclaimed venomless; / their lifespan is declared to be seventy-five years.

1.33.s:
raktapītaśukladantā anīlā mandaveginaḥ .
ete alpāyuṣo jñeyo anye ca bhīravaḥ smṛtā . . 23
1.33.d:
रक्तपीतशुक्लदन्ता अनीला मन्दवेगिनः ।
एते अल्पायुषो ज्ञेयो अन्ये च भीरवः स्मृता ॥ 23
1.33.m: Those with red, yellow, and white teeth, not blue, and of slow impulse, / are to be known as short-lived, and others are regarded as timid.

1.33.s:
ekaṃ cāsya bhavedvaktraṃ dve jihve ca prakīrtite .
dvātriṃśaddaśanāḥ proktāḥ pannāgānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ . . 24
1.33.d:
एकं चास्य भवेद्वक्त्रं द्वे जिह्वे च प्रकीर्तिते ।
द्वात्रिंशद्दशनाः प्रोक्ताः पन्नागानां न संशयः ॥ 24
1.33.m: It has one mouth, and two tongues are proclaimed; / thirty-two teeth are taught for snakes, without a doubt.

1.33.s:
teṣāṃ madhye catasrastu daṃṣṭrā yāḥ suviṣāvahāḥ .
makarī karālī kālarātrī yamadūtī tathaiva ca . . 25
1.33.d:
तेषां मध्ये चतस्रस्तु दंष्ट्रा याः सुविषावहाः ।
मकरी कराली कालरात्री यमदूती तथैव च ॥ 25
1.33.m: Among them, four are fangs that convey strong venom: / Makarī, Karālī, Kālarātrī, and likewise Yamadūtī.

1.33.s:
sarvāsāṃ caiva daṃṣṭrāṇāṃ devatāḥ parikīrtitāḥ .
prathamā brahmadevatyā dvitīyā viṣṇudevatā . .
tṛtīyā rudradevatyā caturthī yamadevatā . . 26
1.33.d:
सर्वासां चैव दंष्ट्राणां देवताः परिकीर्तिताः ।
प्रथमा ब्रह्मदेवत्या द्वितीया विष्णुदेवता ॥
तृतीया रुद्रदेवत्या चतुर्थी यमदेवता ॥ 26
1.33.m: Deities are proclaimed for all these fangs: / the first has Brahmā as its deity, the second has Viṣṇu as its deity, / the third has Rudra as its deity, and the fourth has Yama as its deity.

1.33.s:
hīnā pramāṇataḥ sā tu vāmanetraṃ samāśritā .
nāsyāṃ mantrāḥ prayoktavyā nauṣadhaṃ naiva bheṣajam . . 27
1.33.d:
हीना प्रमाणतः सा तु वामनेत्रं समाश्रिता ।
नास्यां मन्त्राः प्रयोक्तव्या नौषधं नैव भेषजम् ॥ 27
1.33.m: Inferior in size, that [fourth one] rests on the left eye; / upon it mantras are not to be employed, nor medicine, nor any remedy.

1.33.s:
vaidyaḥ parāṅmukho yāti mṛtyustasyā vilekhanāt .
cikitsā na budhaiḥ kāryā tadantaṃ tasya jīvitam . . 28
1.33.d:
वैद्यः पराङ्मुखो याति मृत्युस्तस्या विलेखनात् ।
चिकित्सा न बुधैः कार्या तदन्तं तस्य जीवितम् ॥ 28
1.33.m: The physician turns away; death [ensues] from its scratch. / No medical treatment should be done by the wise; his life ends with it.

1.33.s:
makarīṃ māsikāṃ vidyātkarālī ca dvimāsikā .
kālarātrī bhavettrīṇi caturo yamadūtikā . . 29
1.33.d:
मकरीं मासिकां विद्यात्कराली च द्विमासिका ।
कालरात्री भवेत्त्रीणि चतुरो यमदूतिका ॥ 29
1.33.m: One should know Makarī as lasting a month, and Karālī as lasting two months; / Kālarātrī lasts three [months], and Yamadūtikā four.

1.33.s:
makarīṃ guḍaudanaṃ1 dadyātkaṣāyānnaṃ karālikām .
kālarātrīṃ kaṭuyutaṃ dūtīṃ vai sānnipātikam . . 1.33.30
1.33.d:
मकरीं गुडौदनं1 दद्यात्कषायान्नं करालिकाम् ।
कालरात्रीं कटुयुतं दूतीं वै सान्निपातिकम् ॥ 1.33.30
1.33.m: One should give jaggery-rice for Makarī, and astringent food for Karālikā; / for Kālarātrī [food] combined with pungency, and for Dūtī [food countering] all three humours combined.

1.33.s:
makarī śastrakaṃ vidyātkarālī kākapādikā .
karākṛtiḥ kālarātriryāmyā kūrmākṛtiḥ smṛtā . . 31
1.33.d:
मकरी शस्त्रकं विद्यात्कराली काकपादिका ।
कराकृतिः कालरात्रिर्याम्या कूर्माकृतिः स्मृता ॥ 31
1.33.m: One should know Makarī as knife-shaped, and Karālī as crow's-foot-shaped; / Kālarātrī is hand-shaped, and [the fang] sacred to Yama is taught as tortoise-shaped.

1.33.s:
makarī vātulā jñeyā karālī paittikī smṛtā .
kaphātmikā kālarātrī yamadūtī sānnipātakī . . 32
1.33.d:
मकरी वातुला ज्ञेया कराली पैत्तिकी स्मृता ।
कफात्मिका कालरात्री यमदूती सान्निपातकी ॥ 32
1.33.m: Makarī is to be known as windy, Karālī is taught as bilious, / Kālarātrī consists of phlegm, and Yamadūtī is of all three humours combined.

1.33.s:
śuklā tu makarī jñeyā karālī raktasannibhā .
kālarātrī bhavetpītā kṛṣṇā ca yamadūtikā . . 33
1.33.d:
शुक्ला तु मकरी ज्ञेया कराली रक्तसन्निभा ।
कालरात्री भवेत्पीता कृष्णा च यमदूतिका ॥ 33
1.33.m: Makarī is to be known as white, Karālī resembles red, / Kālarātrī is yellow, and Yamadūtikā is black.

1.33.s:
vāmā śuklā ca kṛṣṇā ca raktā pītā ca dakṣiṇā .
samāsena tu vakṣyāmi yathaitā varṇataḥ smṛtāḥ . . 34
1.33.d:
वामा शुक्ला च कृष्णा च रक्ता पीता च दक्षिणा ।
समासेन तु वक्ष्यामि यथैता वर्णतः स्मृताः ॥ 34
1.33.m: The left are white and black, and the right are red and yellow. / In brief, I shall describe how these are remembered according to caste.

1.33.s:
śuklā tu brāhmaṇī jñeyā raktā tu kṣatriyā smṛtā .
vaiśyā tu pītikā jñeyā kṛṣṇā śūdrā tu kathyate . .
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi daṃṣṭrāṇāṃ viṣalakṣaṇam . . 35
1.33.d:
शुक्ला तु ब्राह्मणी ज्ञेया रक्ता तु क्षत्रिया स्मृता ।
वैश्या तु पीतिका ज्ञेया कृष्णा शूद्रा तु कथ्यते ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि दंष्ट्राणां विषलक्षणम् ॥ 35
1.33.m: The white is to be known as a Brāhmaṇī, the red is taught as a Kṣatriyā, / the yellow is to be known as a Vaiśyā, and the black is said to be a Śūdrā. / Hereafter I shall explain the characteristics of the venom of the fangs.

1.33.s:
daṃṣṭrāṇāṃ tu viṣaṃ nāsti nityameva bhujaṅgame .
dakṣiṇaṃ netramāsādya viṣaṃ sarpasya tiṣṭhati . . 36
1.33.d:
दंष्ट्राणां तु विषं नास्ति नित्यमेव भुजङ्गमे ।
दक्षिणं नेत्रमासाद्य विषं सर्पस्य तिष्ठति ॥ 36
1.33.m: There is no constant venom in the fangs of a serpent; / having reached the right eye, the snake's venom resides [there].

1.33.s:
saṅkuddhasyeha sarpasya viṣaṃ gacchati mastake .
mastakāddhamanīṃ yāti tato nāḍīṣu gacchati . . 37
1.33.d:
सङ्कुद्धस्येह सर्पस्य विषं गच्छति मस्तके ।
मस्तकाद्धमनीं याति ततो नाडीषु गच्छति ॥ 37
1.33.m: When the snake is angered, the venom goes into the head; / from the head it goes to the artery, and then it goes into the channels.

1.33.s:
nāḍībhyaḥ padyate daṃṣṭrāṃ viṣaṃ tatra pravartate .
tatsarvaṃ kathayiṣyāmi yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ . . 38
1.33.d:
नाडीभ्यः पद्यते दंष्ट्रां विषं तत्र प्रवर्तते ।
तत्सर्वं कथयिष्यामि यथावदनुपूर्वशः ॥ 38
1.33.m: From the channels it reaches the fang; there the venom acts. / I shall tell all of that properly in due sequence.

1.33.s:
aṣṭabhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ sarpo daśate nātra saṃśayaḥ .
ākrānto daśate pūrvaṃ dvitīyaṃ pūrvavairiṇam . . 39
1.33.d:
अष्टभिः कारणैः सर्पो दशते नात्र संशयः ।
आक्रान्तो दशते पूर्वं द्वितीयं पूर्ववैरिणम् ॥ 39
1.33.m: A snake bites for eight reasons, without a doubt: / first, it bites when stepped upon; second, an ancient enemy.

1.33.s:
tṛtīyaṃ daśate bhītaścaturthaṃ madadarpitaḥ .
pañcamaṃ tu kṣudhāviṣṭaḥ ṣaṣṭhaṃ ceha viṣolbaṇaḥ . .
saptamaṃ purarakṣārthamaṣṭamaṃ kālacoditaḥ . . 1.33.40
1.33.d:
तृतीयं दशते भीतश्चतुर्थं मददर्पितः ।
पञ्चमं तु क्षुधाविष्टः षष्ठं चेह विषोल्बणः ॥
सप्तमं पुररक्षार्थमष्टमं कालचोदितः ॥ 1.33.40
1.33.m: Third, it bites out of fear; fourth, arrogant with rut; / fifth, overcome by hunger; sixth, overflowing with venom; / seventh, to protect its dwelling; eighth, impelled by death.

1.33.s:
yastu sarpo daśitvā3 tu udaraṃ parivartayet .
balabhugnākṛtiṃ daṃṣṭrāmākrāntaṃ taṃ vinirdiśet . .4 1
yasya sarpeṇa daṣṭasya gabhīraṃ dṛśyate vraṇam .
vairadaṣṭaṃ vijānīyātkaśyapasya vaco yathā . .4 2
ekaṃ daṃṣṭrāpadaṃ yasya avyaktaṃ na ca kalpitam .
bhītadaṣṭaṃ vijānīyādyathovāca prajāpatiḥ . . 43
1.33.d:
यस्तु सर्पो दशित्वा3 तु उदरं परिवर्तयेत् ।
बलभुग्नाकृतिं दंष्ट्रामाक्रान्तं तं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥4 1
यस्य सर्पेण दष्टस्य गभीरं दृश्यते व्रणम् ।
वैरदष्टं विजानीयात्कश्यपस्य वचो यथा ॥4 2
एकं दंष्ट्रापदं यस्य अव्यक्तं न च कल्पितम् ।
भीतदष्टं विजानीयाद्यथोवाच प्रजापतिः ॥ 43
1.33.m: A snake which, having bitten, turns its belly over, / with its fang curved by force—one should identify that as bitten when stepped upon. / One bitten by a snake on whom a deep wound is seen / should be known as bitten out of enmity, according to the words of Kaśyapa. / One who has a single fang-mark that is indistinct and faint / should be known as bitten in fear, as the Prajāpati said.

1.33.s:
yasya sarpeṇa daṣṭasya rekhā dantasya jāyate .
madadaṣṭaṃ vijānīyātkaśyapasya vaco yathā . . 44
1.33.d:
यस्य सर्पेण दष्टस्य रेखा दन्तस्य जायते ।
मददष्टं विजानीयात्कश्यपस्य वचो यथा ॥ 44
1.33.m: One bitten by a snake on whom a line of the tooth appears / should be known as bitten in rut, according to the words of Kaśyapa.

1.33.s:
dve ca daṃṣṭrāpade yasya dṛśyante ca mahākṣatam .
kṣudhāviṣṭaṃ vijānīyādyathovāca prajāpatiḥ . . 45
1.33.d:
द्वे च दंष्ट्रापदे यस्य दृश्यन्ते च महाक्षतम् ।
क्षुधाविष्टं विजानीयाद्यथोवाच प्रजापतिः ॥ 45
1.33.m: One on whom two fang-marks are seen and a large wound / should be known as [bitten by one] overcome by hunger, as the Prajāpati said.

1.33.s:
dve daṃṣṭre yasya dṛśyete kvacidrudhirasaṅkule .
viṣolbaṇaṃ vijānīyāddaṃśaṃ taṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 46
1.33.d:
द्वे दंष्ट्रे यस्य दृश्येते क्वचिद्रुधिरसङ्कुले ।
विषोल्बणं विजानीयाद्दंशं तं नात्र संशयः ॥ 46
1.33.m: One on whom two fangs are seen, filled with blood in some places, / should be known as a bite [by one] overflowing with venom; there is no doubt here.

1.33.s:
apatyarakṣaṇārthāya jānīyāttaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .
yattu kākapadākāraṃ tribhirdantaistu lakṣitam . . 47
1.33.d:
अपत्यरक्षणार्थाय जानीयात्तं न संशयः ।
यत्तु काकपदाकारं त्रिभिर्दन्तैस्तु लक्षितम् ॥ 47
1.33.m:
One should know, without doubt, that it was for the protection of its offspring.
However, when [the bite mark] has the shape of a crow’s foot and is marked by three teeth,

1.33.s:
mahānāga iti proktaṃ kāladaṇḍaṃ vinirdiśet .
trividhaṃ daṣṭajātaistu lakṣaṇaṃ samudāhṛtam . .48
1.33.d:
महानाग इति प्रोक्तं कालदण्डं विनिर्दिशेत् ।
त्रिविधं दष्टजातैस्तु लक्षणं समुदाहृतम् ॥48
1.33.m:
it is declared to be [from] a great serpent; one should designate it as the staff of Death.
The characteristic arising from the bitten has been proclaimed to be of three kinds.

1.33.s:
daṣṭānupītaṃ vijñeyaṃ kaśyapasya vaco yathā .
viṣabhāgāttu sarpasya tribhāgastatra saṃkramet . . 49
1.33.d:
दष्टानुपीतं विज्ञेयं कश्यपस्य वचो यथा ।
विषभागात्तु सर्पस्य त्रिभागस्तत्र संक्रमेत् ॥ 49
1.33.m:
The bitten-and-sucked is to be understood according to the words of Kaśyapa:
a third part from the snake's portion of venom would enter there.

1.33.s:
udaraṃ darśayedyastu uddhataṃ taṃ vinirdiśet .
charditaṃ viṣavegena nirviṣaḥ pannago bhavet . . 1.33.50
1.33.d:
उदरं दर्शयेद्यस्तु उद्धतं तं विनिर्दिशेत् ।
छर्दितं विषवेगेन निर्विषः पन्नगो भवेत् ॥ 1.33.50
1.33.m:
One which reveals its belly should be designated as enraged.
Having vomited by the force of the venom, the serpent becomes free of venom.

1.33.s:
asādhyaścāpi vijñeyaścaturdaṃṣṭrābhipīḍitaḥ .
grīvābhaṅgo bhavetkiñcitsandaṣṭo viṣayogataḥ . .
ito daṃśastataḥ śuddho vyantaraḥ parikīrtitaḥ . . 51
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi pañcamīkalpe
sarpadaṃṣṭrāvarṇanaṃ nāma trayastriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 33 .
kālalakṣaṇam
1.33.d:
असाध्यश्चापि विज्ञेयश्चतुर्दंष्ट्राभिपीडितः ।
