ग्रीवाभङ्गो भवेत्किञ्चित्सन्दष्टो विषयोगतः ॥
इतो दंशस्ततः शुद्धो व्यन्तरः परिकीर्तितः ॥ 51
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि पञ्चमीकल्पे
सर्पदंष्ट्रावर्णनं नाम त्रयस्त्रिंशोऽध्यायः । 33 ।
काललक्षणम्
1.33.m:
And one afflicted by four fangs is to be known as incurable.
There may be a slight fracture of the neck when bitten through the application of poison.
Bitten on this side, pure on that side: it is celebrated as intermediate.
Thus ends the thirty-third chapter, named 'Description of Snake Fangs', in the Pañcamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan, in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa consisting of fifty-five thousand verses.
Signs of the Time of Death

1.34.s:
kaśyapa uvāca
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi kāladaṣṭasya lakṣaṇam .
śṛṇu gautama tattvena yādṛśo bhavate naraḥ . . 1
1.34.d:
कश्यप उवाच
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि कालदष्टस्य लक्षणम् ।
शृणु गौतम तत्त्वेन यादृशो भवते नरः ॥ 1
1.34.m:
Kaśyapa said:
Hereafter I shall proclaim the signs of one bitten by Death.
Hear truly, O Gautama, what kind of person he becomes.

1.34.s:
jihrābhaṅgo'tha hṛcchūlaṃ cakṣurbhyāṃ ca na paśyati .
daṃśaṃ ca dagdhasaṃkāśaṃ pakvajambūphalopamam . . 2
1.34.d:
जिह्राभङ्गोऽथ हृच्छूलं चक्षुर्भ्यां च न पश्यति ।
दंशं च दग्धसंकाशं पक्वजम्बूफलोपमम् ॥ 2
1.34.m:
There is paralysis of the tongue, then pain in the heart, and he does not see with both eyes;
and the bite resembles something burnt, like a ripe jambū fruit.

1.34.s:
vaivarṇyaṃ caiva dantānāṃ śyāvo bhavati varṇataḥ .
sarveṣvaṅgeṣu śaithilyaṃ purīṣasya ca bhedanam . . 3
1.34.d:
वैवर्ण्यं चैव दन्तानां श्यावो भवति वर्णतः ।
सर्वेष्वङ्गेषु शैथिल्यं पुरीषस्य च भेदनम् ॥ 3
1.34.m:
There is also discolouration of the teeth, and he becomes dark-grey in complexion;
there is flaccidity in all the limbs, and looseness of the stool.

1.34.s:
bhagnaskandhakaṭigrīva ūrdhvadṛṣṭiradhomukhaḥ .
dahyate vepate caiva svapate ca muhurmuhuḥ . . 4
1.34.d:
भग्नस्कन्धकटिग्रीव ऊर्ध्वदृष्टिरधोमुखः ।
दह्यते वेपते चैव स्वपते च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ 4
1.34.m:
His shoulders, waist, and neck are broken; his gaze is upward, and his face is turned down;
he burns, trembles, and falls asleep again and again.

1.34.s:
śastreṇa cchidyamānasya rudhiraṃ na pravartate .
daṇḍena tāḍyamānasya daṇḍarājī na jāyate . . 5
1.34.d:
शस्त्रेण च्छिद्यमानस्य रुधिरं न प्रवर्तते ।
दण्डेन ताड्यमानस्य दण्डराजी न जायते ॥ 5
1.34.m:
When cut with a weapon, blood does not flow;
when struck with a stick, no mark from the stick appears.

1.34.s:
daṃśe kākapadaṃ sunīlamasakṛjjambūphalābhaṃ ghanamucchūnaṃ rudhirārdrasekabahulaṃ kṛcchrānnirodho bhavet .
hikkāśvāsagalagrahaśca sumahānpāṇḍustvacā dṛśyate śuṣkāṅgaḥ pravadanti śāstranipuṇāstatkāladaṣṭaṃ viduḥ . . 6
1.34.d:
दंशे काकपदं सुनीलमसकृज्जम्बूफलाभं घनमुच्छूनं रुधिरार्द्रसेकबहुलं कृच्छ्रान्निरोधो भवेत् ।
हिक्काश्वासगलग्रहश्च सुमहान्पाण्डुस्त्वचा दृश्यते शुष्काङ्गः प्रवदन्ति शास्त्रनिपुणास्तत्कालदष्टं विदुः ॥ 6
1.34.m:
On the bite is a very dark crow’s foot resembling a dense ripe jambū fruit, repeatedly swollen,
profuse with an effusion of moist blood, and there is difficult obstruction [of breath];
there is hiccough, dyspnoea, and constriction of the throat, very great paleness is seen on the skin,
and his body is dry: those skilled in the treatises declare that they know him to be bitten by Death.

1.34.s:
daṃśe yasyātha śothaḥ pracalitavalitaṃ maṇḍalaṃ vā sunīlaṃ prasvedo gātra bhedaḥ sravati ca rudhiraṃ sānunāsaṃ ca jalpet .
dantoṣṭhābhyāṃ viyogo bhramati ca hṛdayaṃ sannirodhaśca tīvro divyānāmeṣa daṃśaḥ sthalavipulamayo viddhi taṃ kāladaṣṭam . . 7
1.34.d:
दंशे यस्याथ शोथः प्रचलितवलितं मण्डलं वा सुनीलं प्रस्वेदो गात्र भेदः स्रवति च रुधिरं सानुनासं च जल्पेत् ।
दन्तोष्ठाभ्यां वियोगो भ्रमति च हृदयं सन्निरोधश्च तीव्रो दिव्यानामेष दंशः स्थलविपुलमयो विद्धि तं कालदष्टम् ॥ 7
1.34.m:
When there is swelling on his bite, or a shaking, curved, very dark circle,
profuse sweating, splitting of the limbs, blood trickles, and he speaks through his nose;
there is separation of the teeth from the lips, the heart wavers, and there is severe suppression [of breath]:
this is the bite of celestial [serpents], full of broad ground—know him to be bitten by Death.

1.34.s:
dantairdantānspṛśati bahuśo dṛṣṭirāyāsakhinnā sthūlo daṃśaḥ sravati rudhiraṃ kekaraṃ cakṣurekam . .
pratyādiṣṭaḥ śvasiti satataṃ sānunāsaṃ ca bhāṣetpāpaṃ brūte sakalagaditaṃ kāladaṇḍaṃ tamāhuḥ . . 8
1.34.d:
दन्तैर्दन्तान्स्पृशति बहुशो दृष्टिरायासखिन्ना स्थूलो दंशः स्रवति रुधिरं केकरं चक्षुरेकम् ॥
प्रत्यादिष्टः श्वसिति सततं सानुनासं च भाषेत्पापं ब्रूते सकलगदितं कालदण्डं तमाहुः ॥ 8
1.34.m:
He frequently touches teeth to teeth, his gaze is weary from exertion, the bite is thick and bleeds, one eye is squinted;
rejected [by physicians], he constantly pants, speaks nasally, and utters evil: they call all that is declared the staff of Death.

1.34.s:
vepate vedanā tīvrā raktanetraśca jāyate .
grīvābhaṅgaścalā nābhiḥ kāladaṣṭaṃ vinirdiśet . . 9
1.34.d:
वेपते वेदना तीव्रा रक्तनेत्रश्च जायते ।
ग्रीवाभङ्गश्चला नाभिः कालदष्टं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ 9
1.34.m:
He trembles, acute pain arises, and he becomes red-eyed;
there is drooping of the neck and an unsteady navel: one should designate him as bitten by Death.

1.34.s:
darpaṇe salile vāpi ātmacchāyāṃ na paśyati .
mandaraśmiṃ tathā tīvraṃ tejohīnaṃ divākaram1 . . 1.34.10
1.34.d:
दर्पणे सलिले वापि आत्मच्छायां न पश्यति ।
मन्दरश्मिं तथा तीव्रं तेजोहीनं दिवाकरम्1 ॥ 1.34.10
1.34.m:
In a mirror or in water he does not see his own shadow,
and likewise he sees the blazing sun as dim-rayed and devoid of splendour.

1.34.s:
vepate vedanātrasto raktanetraśca jāyate .
sa yāti nidhanaṃ jantuḥ kāladaṇḍaṃ vinirdiśet . . 11
1.34.d:
वेपते वेदनात्रस्तो रक्तनेत्रश्च जायते ।
स याति निधनं जन्तुः कालदण्डं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ 11
1.34.m:
He trembles, terrified by pain, and becomes red-eyed;
that creature goes to destruction: one should designate it as the staff of Death.

1.34.s:
aṣṭamyāṃ ca navamyāṃ ca kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśīm .
nāgapañcamīdaṣṭānāṃ jīvitasya ca saṃśayaḥ . . 12
1.34.d:
अष्टम्यां च नवम्यां च कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दशीम् ।
नागपञ्चमीदष्टानां जीवितस्य च संशयः ॥ 12
1.34.m:
On the eighth and on the ninth, on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight,
and on Nāgapañcamī, there is doubt regarding the life of those who are bitten.

1.34.s:
ārdrāśleṣāmaghābharaṇīkṛttikāsu viśeṣataḥ .
viśākhāṃ triṣu pūrvāsu mūlasvātīśatātmake . .
sarpadaṣṭā na jīvanti viṣaṃ pītaṃ ca yaistathā . . 13
1.34.d:
आर्द्राश्लेषामघाभरणीकृत्तिकासु विशेषतः ।
विशाखां त्रिषु पूर्वासु मूलस्वातीशतात्मके ॥
सर्पदष्टा न जीवन्ति विषं पीतं च यैस्तथा ॥ 13

1.34.s:
śūnyāgāre śmaśāne ca śuṣkavṛkṣe tathaiva ca .
na jīvanti narā daṣṭā nakṣatre tithisaṃyute . . 14
1.34.d:
शून्यागारे श्मशाने च शुष्कवृक्षे तथैव च ।
न जीवन्ति नरा दष्टा नक्षत्रे तिथिसंयुते ॥ 14
1.34.m:
In a deserted house, in a cremation ground, and likewise on a withered tree,
men bitten under [such a] constellation combined with [such a] lunar day do not live.

1.34.s:
aṣṭottaraṃ marma śataṃ prāṇināṃ samudāhṛtam .
teṣāṃ madhye tu marmāṇi daśa dve cāpi kīrtite . . 15
1.34.d:
अष्टोत्तरं मर्म शतं प्राणिनां समुदाहृतम् ।
तेषां मध्ये तु मर्माणि दश द्वे चापि कीर्तिते ॥ 15
1.34.m:
One hundred and eight vital spots of living beings have been declared;
among them, however, twelve vital spots are specifically celebrated:

1.34.s:
śaṅkhe netre bhruvormadhye bastibhyāṃ vṛṣaṇottare .
kakṣe skandhe hadi madhye tāluke cibuke gude . . 16
1.34.d:
शङ्खे नेत्रे भ्रुवोर्मध्ये बस्तिभ्यां वृषणोत्तरे ।
कक्षे स्कन्धे हदि मध्ये तालुके चिबुके गुदे ॥ 16
1.34.m:
the temple, the eyes, the space between the eyebrows, both bladders, above the testicles,
the armpit, the shoulder, the centre of the heart, the palate, the chin, and the anus.

1.34.s:
eṣu dvādaśamarmeṣu2 daṃśaiḥ śastreṇa vā hataḥ .
na jīvati naro loke kāladaṇḍaṃ vinirdiśet . . 17
1.34.d:
एषु द्वादशमर्मेषु2 दंशैः शस्त्रेण वा हतः ।
न जीवति नरो लोके कालदण्डं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ 17
1.34.m:
Stricken in these twelve vital spots by bites or by a weapon,
a man in this world does not live: one should designate it as the staff of Death.

1.34.s:
akacaṭatapayaśāṃ vadanti proktā jīvanti na tatra hi .
gataṃ brūyādyadi skhalati śirastasya samprāptakālaḥ . . 18
1.34.d:
अकचटतपयशां वदन्ति प्रोक्ता जीवन्ति न तत्र हि ।
गतं ब्रूयाद्यदि स्खलति शिरस्तस्य सम्प्राप्तकालः ॥ 18
1.34.m:
They declare of the consonants a, ka, ca, ṭa, ta, pa, ya, and śa: if spoken, they do not live there;
if [the messenger] says he is gone, or if his head stumbles, his time of death has arrived.

1.34.s:
bhavati ca yadi dūto hyuttamasyādhamo vā yadi bhavati ca dūta uttamo vādhamasya .
ādau daṣṭasya nāma yadi vadati kvacidvakti tasyātha paścāttaṃ varṇabhedo yadi bhavati samaḥ prāpta kālasya dūtaḥ . . 19
1.34.d:
भवति च यदि दूतो ह्युत्तमस्याधमो वा यदि भवति च दूत उत्तमो वाधमस्य ।
आदौ दष्टस्य नाम यदि वदति क्वचिद्वक्ति तस्याथ पश्चात्तं वर्णभेदो यदि भवति समः प्राप्त कालस्य दूतः ॥ 19

1.34.s:
dūto vā daṇḍahasto bhavati ca yugalaṃ pāśahastastathā vā raktavastraṃ ca kṛṣṇaṃ mukhaśirasi gatamekavastraśca dūtaḥ . .
tailābhyaktaśca tadvadyadi tvaritagatirmuktakeśaśca yāti yaḥ kuryādghoraśabdaṃ karacaraṇayugaiḥ prāptakālasya dūtaḥ . . 1.34.20
1.34.d:
दूतो वा दण्डहस्तो भवति च युगलं पाशहस्तस्तथा वा रक्तवस्त्रं च कृष्णं मुखशिरसि गतमेकवस्त्रश्च दूतः ॥
तैलाभ्यक्तश्च तद्वद्यदि त्वरितगतिर्मुक्तकेशश्च याति यः कुर्याद्घोरशब्दं करचरणयुगैः प्राप्तकालस्य दूतः ॥ 1.34.20

1.34.s:
nāgodayaṃ pravakṣyāmi īśānena tu bhāṣitam .
brahmaṇā tu purā sṛṣṭā grahā nāgāstvanekaśaḥ . . 21
1.34.d:
नागोदयं प्रवक्ष्यामि ईशानेन तु भाषितम् ।
ब्रह्मणा तु पुरा सृष्टा ग्रहा नागास्त्वनेकशः ॥ 21
1.34.m:
I shall proclaim the rising of the serpents as spoken by Īśāna:
formerly, Brahmā created numerous planets and serpents.

1.34.s:
anantaṃ bhāskaraṃ vidyātsomaṃ vidyāttu vāsukim .
takṣakaṃ bhūmiputraṃ tu karkoṭaṃ ca budhaṃ viduḥ . . 22
1.34.d:
अनन्तं भास्करं विद्यात्सोमं विद्यात्तु वासुकिम् ।
तक्षकं भूमिपुत्रं तु कर्कोटं च बुधं विदुः ॥ 22
1.34.m:
One should know Ananta as the Sun, and one should know Vāsuki as the Moon;
Takṣaka is the son of the Earth (Mars), and Karkoṭa they know as Mercury.

1.34.s:
padmaṃ bṛhaspatiṃ vidyānmahāpadmaṃ ca bhārgavam .
kulikaḥ śaṃkhapālaśca dvāvetau tu śanaiścaraḥ . . 23
1.34.d:
पद्मं बृहस्पतिं विद्यान्महापद्मं च भार्गवम् ।
कुलिकः शंखपालश्च द्वावेतौ तु शनैश्चरः ॥ 23
1.34.m:
One should know Padma as Jupiter, and Mahāpadma as Venus;
Kulika and Śaṅkhapāla, both these two, are Saturn.

1.34.s:
pūrvapādaḥ śaṃkhapālo dvitīyaḥ kulikastathā .
nityaṃ bhāge yathoddiṣṭe dinarātrī tathaiva ca . . 24
1.34.d:
पूर्वपादः शंखपालो द्वितीयः कुलिकस्तथा ।
नित्यं भागे यथोद्दिष्टे दिनरात्री तथैव च ॥ 24
1.34.m:
The first quarter is Śaṅkhapāla, and the second is Kulika;
always in the allotted portion, both day and night likewise.

1.34.s:
śukrasomau ca madhyāhne udaye tu kṣamāsutaḥ .
śaniḥ prāgaṣṭame bhāge divārātre tvihocyate . . 25
1.34.d:
शुक्रसोमौ च मध्याह्ने उदये तु क्षमासुतः ।
शनिः प्रागष्टमे भागे दिवारात्रे त्विहोच्यते ॥ 25
1.34.m:
Venus and the Moon [preside] at midday, and the son of the Earth (Mars) at sunrise;
Saturn is said here to preside over the eighth part of the day and night.

1.34.s:
grahāśca bhuñjate caiva śeṣaṃ bhāgasya lakṣaṇam .
ravivāre sadā jñeyau pādau daśa caturdaśa . . 26
1.34.d:
ग्रहाश्च भुञ्जते चैव शेषं भागस्य लक्षणम् ।
रविवारे सदा ज्ञेयौ पादौ दश चतुर्दश ॥ 26
1.34.m:
The planets enjoy [their periods], and [this is] the characteristic of the remainder of the portion:
on Sunday, the tenth and fourteenth quarters are always to be known [as inauspicious];

1.34.s:
aṣṭa dvādaśa vai candre daśa ṣaṣṭhe kuje tathā .
budhasya navame pāde rāhau ca divasasya ca . . 27
1.34.d:
अष्ट द्वादश वै चन्द्रे दश षष्ठे कुजे तथा ।
बुधस्य नवमे पादे राहौ च दिवसस्य च ॥ 27
1.34.m:
the eighth and twelfth on Monday; likewise the tenth and sixth on Tuesday;
in the ninth quarter of Mercury (Wednesday), and of Rāhu during the day;

1.34.s:
gurordvitīyaḥ ṣaṣṭhaśca ṣoḍaśasya tu varjayet .
bhāskarasya dine prokte caturthe daśameṣṭame . . 28
1.34.d:
गुरोर्द्वितीयः षष्ठश्च षोडशस्य तु वर्जयेत् ।
भास्करस्य दिने प्रोक्ते चतुर्थे दशमेष्टमे ॥ 28
1.34.m:
on Thursday, one should avoid the second, the sixth, and the sixteenth;
on the day proclaimed for the Sun (Sunday), in the fourth, tenth, and eighth;

1.34.s:
śanaiścaradine pādaṃ tyajeccaiva sudāruṇam .
dvitīyaṃ dvādaśaṃ caiva ṣoḍaśasya tu varjayet . . 29
1.34.d:
शनैश्चरदिने पादं त्यजेच्चैव सुदारुणम् ।
द्वितीयं द्वादशं चैव षोडशस्य तु वर्जयेत् ॥ 29
1.34.m:
and on the day of Saturn (Saturday), one should avoid the most terrible quarter:
one should avoid the second, the twelfth, and the sixteenth.

1.34.s:
muhūrtaghaṭikādūrddhvaṃ ghaṭikā caturthaṃ bhāgaṃ viṃśatiśca .
kuhūsutaṃ budbudaṃ nimeṣametatkālasya lakṣaṇam . . 1.34.30
1.34.d:
मुहूर्तघटिकादूर्द्ध्वं घटिका चतुर्थं भागं विंशतिश्च ।
कुहूसुतं बुद्बुदं निमेषमेतत्कालस्य लक्षणम् ॥ 1.34.30
1.34.m:
After a muhūrta and a ghaṭikā, a ghaṭikā, a fourth part, and twenty;
a Kuhūsuta, a bubble, a twinkling of an eye: this is the characteristic of time.

1.34.s:
iti śrī bhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi pañcamīkalpe
daṃśadaṣṭakadūtalakṣaṇaṃ nāma catustriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 34 .
yamadūtīlakṣaṇam
1.34.d:
इति श्री भविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि पञ्चमीकल्पे
दंशदष्टकदूतलक्षणं नाम चतुस्त्रिंशोऽध्यायः । 34 ।
यमदूतीलक्षणम्
1.34.m:
Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter, named 'Characteristics of Bites, the Bitten, and Messengers', in the Pañcamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan, in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa consisting of fifty-five thousand verses.
Characteristics of Yamadūtī

1.35.s:
kaśyapa uvāca
saviṣā daṃṣṭrayormadhye yamadūtī tu vai bhavet .
na cikitsā budhaiḥ kāryā taṃ gatāsuṃ virnidaśet . . 1
1.35.d:
कश्यप उवाच
सविषा दंष्ट्रयोर्मध्ये यमदूती तु वै भवेत् ।
न चिकित्सा बुधैः कार्या तं गतासुं विर्निदशेत् ॥ 1
1.35.m: Kaśyapa said: / Between the two fangs, there is indeed Yamadūtī, full of venom. / The wise should not treat him; one should declare him dead.

1.35.s:
praharārdhaṃ divārātrāvekaikaṃ bhuñjate bahiḥ .
ekasya ca samānaṃ ca dvitīyaṃ ṣoḍaśaṃ tathā . . 2
1.35.d:
प्रहरार्धं दिवारात्रावेकैकं भुञ्जते बहिः ।
एकस्य च समानं च द्वितीयं षोडशं तथा ॥ 2
1.35.m: For half a watch, day and night, they feed outside one by one; / equal for the first, and likewise sixteen for the second.

1.35.s:
nāgodayo yamuddiśya hato viddho vidāritaḥ .
kāladaṣṭaṃ vijānīyātkaśyapasya vaco yathā . . 3
1.35.d:
नागोदयो यमुद्दिश्य हतो विद्धो विदारितः ।
कालदष्टं विजानीयात्कश्यपस्य वचो यथा ॥ 3
1.35.m: He against whom a serpent arises, struck, pierced, torn open— / one should know him to be bitten by Time, according to the word of Kaśyapa.

1.35.s:
yanmātraṃ patate bindurvālāgraṃ saliloddhṛtam .
tanmātraṃ sravate daṃṣṭrā viṣaṃ sarpasya dāruṇam . . 4
1.35.d:
यन्मात्रं पतते बिन्दुर्वालाग्रं सलिलोद्धृतम् ।
तन्मात्रं स्रवते दंष्ट्रा विषं सर्पस्य दारुणम् ॥ 4
1.35.m: Just as much as a drop falling from the tip of a hair drawn up from water, / just that much does the serpent's fang exude of terrible venom.

1.35.s:
nāḍīśate tu sampūrṇe dehe saṅkramate viṣam .
yāvatsaṅkrāmayedbāhuṃ kuñcitaṃ vā prasārayet . . 5
1.35.d:
नाडीशते तु सम्पूर्णे देहे सङ्क्रमते विषम् ।
यावत्सङ्क्रामयेद्बाहुं कुञ्चितं वा प्रसारयेत् ॥ 5
1.35.m: When the hundred channels are filled, the venom spreads in the body, / in as much time as one might bend or stretch an arm.

1.35.s:
anena kṣaṇamātreṇa viṣaṃ gacchati mastake .
vepate viṣavege tu śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ . . 6
1.35.d:
अनेन क्षणमात्रेण विषं गच्छति मस्तके ।
वेपते विषवेगे तु शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥ 6
1.35.m: In merely this moment, the venom travels to the head. / In the surge of venom, he trembles hundreds and thousands of times.

1.35.s:
vardhate raktamāsādya tato vātaiḥ śikhī yathā .
tailabindurjalaṃ prāpya yathā vegena vardhate . . 7
1.35.d:
वर्धते रक्तमासाद्य ततो वातैः शिखी यथा ।
तैलबिन्दुर्जलं प्राप्य यथा वेगेन वर्धते ॥ 7
1.35.m: Having reached the blood, it increases then, like fire with winds, / as a drop of oil spreads swiftly upon reaching water.

1.35.s:
śikhaṇḍī āśrayaṃ prāpya mārutena samīritaḥ .
tataḥ sthānaśataṃ prāpya tvacāsthānaṃ viceṣṭitam . . 8
1.35.d:
शिखण्डी आश्रयं प्राप्य मारुतेन समीरितः ।
ततः स्थानशतं प्राप्य त्वचास्थानं विचेष्टितम् ॥ 8
1.35.m: Like fire finding fuel, driven by the wind, / then, having reached a hundred locations, the location of the skin is agitated.

1.35.s:
tvacāsu dviguṇaṃ vidyācchoṇiteṣu caturguṇam .
pitte tu triguṇaṃ yāti śleṣme vai ṣoḍaśaṃ bhavet . . 9
1.35.d:
त्वचासु द्विगुणं विद्याच्छोणितेषु चतुर्गुणम् ।
पित्ते तु त्रिगुणं याति श्लेष्मे वै षोडशं भवेत् ॥ 9
1.35.m: One should know it doubles in the skin, and quadruples in the blood; / in the bile it triples, and in phlegm it becomes sixteen-fold.

1.35.s:
vāyau triṃśadguṇaṃ caiva majjāṣaṣṭiguṇaṃ tathā .
prāṇe caikārṇavībhūte sarvagātrāṇi sandhayet1 . . 1.35.10
1.35.d:
वायौ त्रिंशद्गुणं चैव मज्जाषष्टिगुणं तथा ।
प्राणे चैकार्णवीभूते सर्वगात्राणि सन्धयेत्1 ॥ 1.35.10
1.35.m: In the wind it is thirty-fold, and in the marrow sixty-fold; / and when the vital breath becomes an undifferentiated flood, it paralyzes all the limbs.

1.35.s:
śrotre nirudhyamāne ca yāti daṣṭastvasādhyatām .
tato'sau mriyate janturniḥśvāsocchvāsavarjitaḥ . . 11
1.35.d:
श्रोत्रे निरुध्यमाने च याति दष्टस्त्वसाध्यताम् ।
ततोऽसौ म्रियते जन्तुर्निःश्वासोच्छ्वासवर्जितः ॥ 11
1.35.m: When hearing is obstructed, the bitten person becomes incurable; / then that living being dies, devoid of inhalation and exhalation.

1.35.s:
niṣkrānte tu tato jīve bhūte pañcatvamāgate .
tāni bhūtāni gacchanti yasya yasya yathātatham . . 12
1.35.d:
निष्क्रान्ते तु ततो जीवे भूते पञ्चत्वमागते ।
तानि भूतानि गच्छन्ति यस्य यस्य यथातथम् ॥ 12
1.35.m: When the soul departs and the being undergoes dissolution into the five elements, / those elements depart, each to its own place as it was.

1.35.s:
pṛthivyāpastathā tejo vāyurākāśameva ca .
ityeṣāmeva saṅghātaḥ śarīramabhidhīyate . . 13
1.35.d:
पृथिव्यापस्तथा तेजो वायुराकाशमेव च ।
इत्येषामेव सङ्घातः शरीरमभिधीयते ॥ 13
1.35.m: Earth, water, fire, wind, and ether— / the collection of these alone is called the body.

1.35.s:
pṛthivī pṛthivīṃ yāti toyaṃ toyeṣu līyate .
tejo gacchati cādityaṃ māruto mārutaṃ vrajet . . 14
1.35.d:
पृथिवी पृथिवीं याति तोयं तोयेषु लीयते ।
तेजो गच्छति चादित्यं मारुतो मारुतं व्रजेत् ॥ 14
1.35.m: Earth goes to earth, water dissolves in waters, / fire goes to the sun, wind goes to wind,

1.35.s:
ākāśaṃ caivamākāśe saha tenaiva gacchati .
svasthānaṃ te prapadyante parasparaniyojitāḥ . . 15
1.35.d:
आकाशं चैवमाकाशे सह तेनैव गच्छति ।
स्वस्थानं ते प्रपद्यन्ते परस्परनियोजिताः ॥ 15
1.35.m: and ether likewise goes together into ether. / Joined to one another, they reach their own places.

1.35.s:
na jīvedāgataḥ kaścidiha janmani suvrata .
viṣārtaṃ na upekṣeta tvaritaṃ tu cikitsayet . . 16
1.35.d:
न जीवेदागतः कश्चिदिह जन्मनि सुव्रत ।
विषार्तं न उपेक्षेत त्वरितं तु चिकित्सयेत् ॥ 16
1.35.m: No one who has arrived in this birth can live forever, O you of noble vows; / one should not neglect a person stricken by venom, but treat him quickly.

1.35.s:
ekamasti viṣaṃ loke dvitīyaṃ copapadyate .
yathā nānāvidhaṃ caiva sthāvaraṃ tu tathaiva ca . . 17
1.35.d:
एकमस्ति विषं लोके द्वितीयं चोपपद्यते ।
यथा नानाविधं चैव स्थावरं तु तथैव च ॥ 17
1.35.m: There is one poison in the world, and another arises, / both varied in nature and likewise immobile [vegetal and mineral].

1.35.s:
prathame viṣavege tu romaharṣo'bhijāyate .
dvitīye viṣavege tu svedo gātreṣu jāyate . . 18
1.35.d:
प्रथमे विषवेगे तु रोमहर्षोऽभिजायते ।
द्वितीये विषवेगे तु स्वेदो गात्रेषु जायते ॥ 18
1.35.m: In the first surge of venom, horripilation arises; / in the second surge of venom, sweat appears on the limbs.

1.35.s:
tṛtīye viṣavege tu kampo gātreṣu jāyate .
caturthe viṣavege tu śrotrāntaranirodhakṛt . . 19
1.35.d:
तृतीये विषवेगे तु कम्पो गात्रेषु जायते ।
चतुर्थे विषवेगे तु श्रोत्रान्तरनिरोधकृत् ॥ 19
1.35.m: In the third surge of venom, trembling arises in the limbs; / in the fourth surge of venom, obstruction within the ears occurs.

1.35.s:
pañcame viṣavege tu hikkā gātreṣu jāyate .
ṣaṣṭhe ca viṣavege tu prāṇebhyo'pi pramucyate . .
saptadhātuvahā hyete vainateyena bhāṣitāḥ . . 1.35.20
1.35.d:
पञ्चमे विषवेगे तु हिक्का गात्रेषु जायते ।
षष्ठे च विषवेगे तु प्राणेभ्योऽपि प्रमुच्यते ॥
सप्तधातुवहा ह्येते वैनतेयेन भाषिताः ॥ 1.35.20
1.35.m: In the fifth surge of venom, hiccup arises in the limbs; / and in the sixth surge of venom, he is released even from his vital breaths. / For these, which carry through the seven bodily elements, were spoken by Garuḍa.

1.35.s:
tvacaḥ sthāne viṣe prāpte tasya rūpāṇi me śṛṇu .
aṅgāni timirāyante tapante ca muhurmuhuḥ . . 21
1.35.d:
त्वचः स्थाने विषे प्राप्ते तस्य रूपाणि मे शृणु ।
अङ्गानि तिमिरायन्ते तपन्ते च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ 21
1.35.m: When venom has reached the site of the skin, hear its symptoms from me: / the limbs darken and burn again and again.

1.35.s:
etāni yasya cihnāni tasya tvaci gataṃ viṣam .
tasyāgadaṃ pravakṣyāmi yena sampadyate sukham . . 22
1.35.d:
एतानि यस्य चिह्नानि तस्य त्वचि गतं विषम् ।
तस्यागदं प्रवक्ष्यामि येन सम्पद्यते सुखम् ॥ 22
1.35.m: He who has these symptoms has venom situated in his skin. / I will declare an antidote for him, by which relief is obtained.

1.35.s:
arkamūlamapāmārgaṃ priyaṅguṃ tagaraṃ2 tathā .
etadāloḍya dātavyaṃ tataḥ sampadyate sukham . . 23
1.35.d:
अर्कमूलमपामार्गं प्रियङ्गुं तगरं2 तथा ।
एतदालोड्य दातव्यं ततः सम्पद्यते सुखम् ॥ 23
1.35.m: Arka root, apāmārga, priyaṅgu, and tagara: / having stirred these together, they must be given; then relief is obtained.

1.35.s:
tatastasmitkṛte vipra na nivarteta cedviṣam .
tvacaḥ sthānaṃ tato bhittvā raktasthānaṃ pradhāvati . . 24
1.35.d:
ततस्तस्मित्कृते विप्र न निवर्तेत चेद्विषम् ।
त्वचः स्थानं ततो भित्त्वा रक्तस्थानं प्रधावति ॥ 24
1.35.m: Then, when that is done, O Brahmin, if the venom does not recede, / then, having pierced the site of the skin, it rushes to the site of the blood.

1.35.s:
viṣe ca raktaṃ saṃprāpte tasya rūpāṇi me śṛṇu .
dahyate muhyate1 caiva śītalaṃ bahu manyate . . 25
1.35.d:
विषे च रक्तं संप्राप्ते तस्य रूपाणि मे शृणु ।
दह्यते मुह्यते1 चैव शीतलं बहु मन्यते ॥ 25
1.35.m: When the venom has reached the blood, hear its symptoms from me: / he burns and is bewildered, and values cold highly.

1.35.s:
etāni yasya rūpāṇi tasya raktagataṃ viṣam .
tatrāgadaṃ pravakṣyāmi yena sampadyate sukham . . 26
1.35.d:
एतानि यस्य रूपाणि तस्य रक्तगतं विषम् ।
तत्रागदं प्रवक्ष्यामि येन सम्पद्यते सुखम् ॥ 26
1.35.m: He who has these symptoms has venom situated in the blood. / There I will declare an antidote by which relief is obtained.

1.35.s:
uśīraṃ candanaṃ kuṣṭhamutpalaṃ tagaraṃ tathā .
mahākālasya mūlāni sinduvāranagasya ca . .
hiṅgulaṃ maricaṃ caiva pūrvavege tu dāpeyat . . 27
1.35.d:
उशीरं चन्दनं कुष्ठमुत्पलं तगरं तथा ।
महाकालस्य मूलानि सिन्दुवारनगस्य च ॥
हिङ्गुलं मरिचं चैव पूर्ववेगे तु दापेयत् ॥ 27
1.35.m: Uśīra, candana, kuṣṭha, utpala, and tagara, / the roots of mahākāla and of the sinduvāra tree, / hiṅgula, and black pepper: one should give these in the earlier surge.

1.35.s:
bṛhatī vṛścikā kālī indra vāruṇimūlakam2 .
saptagandhaghṛtaṃ caiva dvitīye parikīrtitam . . 28
1.35.d:
बृहती वृश्चिका काली इन्द्र वारुणिमूलकम्2 ।
सप्तगन्धघृतं चैव द्वितीये परिकीर्तितम् ॥ 28
1.35.m: Bṛhatī, vṛścikā, kālī, root of indravāruṇī, / and ghee prepared with seven fragrant substances is proclaimed for the second [surge].

1.35.s:
sinduvāraṃ tathā hiṅguṃ tṛtīye kārayedbudhaḥ .
tasya pānaṃ ca kurvīta añjanaṃ lepanaṃ tathā . . 29
1.35.d:
सिन्दुवारं तथा हिङ्गुं तृतीये कारयेद्बुधः ।
तस्य पानं च कुर्वीत अञ्जनं लेपनं तथा ॥ 29
1.35.m: The wise person should prepare sinduvāra and asafoetida for the third; / he should make a drink of it, and a collyrium, and an ointment.

1.35.s:
etenaivopacāreṇa tataḥ sampadyate sukham .
raktasthānaṃ tato gatvā pittasthānaṃ pradhāvati . . 1.35.30
1.35.d:
एतेनैवोपचारेण ततः सम्पद्यते सुखम् ।
रक्तस्थानं ततो गत्वा पित्तस्थानं प्रधावति ॥ 1.35.30
1.35.m: By this very treatment, relief is obtained. / Then, having left the site of the blood, it rushes to the site of the bile.

1.35.s:
pittasthānagate vipra viṣarūpāṇi me śṛṇu .
uttiṣṭhate nipatate dahyate muhyate tathā . . 31
1.35.d:
पित्तस्थानगते विप्र विषरूपाणि मे शृणु ।
उत्तिष्ठते निपतते दह्यते मुह्यते तथा ॥ 31
1.35.m: When it has reached the site of the bile, O Brahmin, hear the symptoms of the venom from me: / he rises up, falls down, burns, and is bewildered;

1.35.s:
gātrataḥ pītakaḥ syādvai diśaḥ paśyati pītikā .
prabalā ca bhavanmūrcchā na cātmānaṃ vijānate . .
viṣakriyāṃ tasya kuryādyathā sampadyate sukham . . 32
1.35.d:
गात्रतः पीतकः स्याद्वै दिशः पश्यति पीतिका ।
प्रबला च भवन्मूर्च्छा न चात्मानं विजानते ॥
विषक्रियां तस्य कुर्याद्यथा सम्पद्यते सुखम् ॥ 32
1.35.m: his body becomes yellow, and he sees the directions yellow; / fainting becomes severe, and he does not recognize himself. / One should perform treatment of the venom for him so that relief is obtained.

1.35.s: pittasthānamatikramya śleṣmasthānaṃ ca gacchati . . 33
1.35.d: पित्तस्थानमतिक्रम्य श्लेष्मस्थानं च गच्छति ॥ 33
1.35.m: Having passed beyond the site of the bile, it goes to the site of phlegm.

1.35.s:
pippalyo madhukaṃ caiva madhu khaṇḍaṃ ghṛtaṃ tathā .
madhusāramalābūṃ ca jātiṃ śaṅkaravālukām . .
indravāruṇikāmūlaṃ gavāṃ mūtreṇa peṣayet . . 34
1.35.d:
पिप्पल्यो मधुकं चैव मधु खण्डं घृतं तथा ।
मधुसारमलाबूं च जातिं शङ्करवालुकाम् ॥
इन्द्रवारुणिकामूलं गवां मूत्रेण पेषयेत् ॥ 34
1.35.m: Long peppers, licorice, honey, sugar, and ghee, / madhusāra, bottle gourd, jasmine, cucumber, / [and] indravāruṇikā root: one should grind them with cow's urine.

1.35.s:
nasyaṃ tasya prayuñjīta pānamālepanāñjanam .
etenaivopacāreṇa tataḥ sampadyate sukham . . 35
1.35.d:
नस्यं तस्य प्रयुञ्जीत पानमालेपनाञ्जनम् ।
एतेनैवोपचारेण ततः सम्पद्यते सुखम् ॥ 35
1.35.m: One should administer a nasal drop of it, a drink, an ointment, [and] a collyrium. / By this very treatment, relief is obtained.

1.35.s:
śleṣmasthānaṃ tataḥ prāpte tasya rūpāṇi me śṛṇu .
gātrāṇi1 tasya rudhyante niḥśvāsaśca na jāyate . .
lālā ca sravate tasya kaṇṭho ghurughurāyate . . 36
1.35.d:
श्लेष्मस्थानं ततः प्राप्ते तस्य रूपाणि मे शृणु ।
गात्राणि1 तस्य रुध्यन्ते निःश्वासश्च न जायते ॥
लाला च स्रवते तस्य कण्ठो घुरुघुरायते ॥ 36
1.35.m: When it has reached the site of phlegm, hear its symptoms from me: / his limbs are obstructed, and no breath is produced; / his saliva dribbles, and his throat rattles.

1.35.s:
etāni yasya rūpāṇi tasya śleṣmagataṃ viṣam .
tasyāgadaṃ pravakṣyāmi yena sampadyate sukham . . 37
1.35.d:
एतानि यस्य रूपाणि तस्य श्लेष्मगतं विषम् ।
तस्यागदं प्रवक्ष्यामि येन सम्पद्यते सुखम् ॥ 37
1.35.m: He who has these symptoms has venom situated in the phlegm. / I will declare an antidote for him, by which relief is obtained.

1.35.s:
trikuṭakī śleṣmātako lodhrañca madhusārakam .
etāni samabhāgāni gavāṃ mūtreṇa peṣayet . . 38
1.35.d:
त्रिकुटकी श्लेष्मातको लोध्रञ्च मधुसारकम् ।
एतानि समभागानि गवां मूत्रेण पेषयेत् ॥ 38
1.35.m: Trikuṭakī, śleṣmātaka, lodhra, and madhusāra: / one should grind equal parts of these with cow's urine.

1.35.s:
tasya pānaṃ ca kurvīta añjanaṃ lepanaṃ tathā .
etenaivopacāreṇa tataḥ sampadyate sukham . . 39
1.35.d:
तस्य पानं च कुर्वीत अञ्जनं लेपनं तथा ।
एतेनैवोपचारेण ततः सम्पद्यते सुखम् ॥ 39
1.35.m: One should make a drink of it, and a collyrium, and an ointment. / By this very treatment, relief is obtained.

1.35.s:
śleṣmasthānamatikramya vāyusthānaṃ ca gacchati .
tatra rūpāṇi vakṣyāmi vāyusthānagate viṣe . . 1.35.40
1.35.d:
श्लेष्मस्थानमतिक्रम्य वायुस्थानं च गच्छति ।
तत्र रूपाणि वक्ष्यामि वायुस्थानगते विषे ॥ 1.35.40
1.35.m: Having passed beyond the site of phlegm, it goes to the site of wind. / I will declare the symptoms there when the venom has reached the site of wind.

1.35.s:
ādhmāyate ca jaṭharaṃ bāndhavāṃśca na paśyati .
īdṛśaṃ kurute rūpaṃ vṛṣṭibhaṅgaśca jāyate . . 41
1.35.d:
आध्मायते च जठरं बान्धवांश्च न पश्यति ।
ईदृशं कुरुते रूपं वृष्टिभङ्गश्च जायते ॥ 41
1.35.m: His belly is bloated, and he does not see his kinsmen; / it produces such an appearance, and failure of vision occurs.

1.35.s:
etāni yasya rūpāṇi tasya vāyugataṃ viṣam .
tasyāgadaṃ prakṣyāmi yena sampadyate sukham . .4 2
śoṇāmūlaṃ priyālaṃ ca raktaṃ ca gajapippalīm .
bhārṅgīṃ vacāṃ pippalīṃ ca devadāruṃ madhūkakam . . 43
1.35.d:
एतानि यस्य रूपाणि तस्य वायुगतं विषम् ।
तस्यागदं प्रक्ष्यामि येन सम्पद्यते सुखम् ॥4 2
शोणामूलं प्रियालं च रक्तं च गजपिप्पलीम् ।
भार्ङ्गीं वचां पिप्पलीं च देवदारुं मधूककम् ॥ 43
1.35.m: He who has these symptoms has venom situated in the wind. / I will declare an antidote for him, by which relief is obtained: / root of śoṇā, priyāla, rakta, and gajapippalī, / bhārṅgī, vacā, pippalī, devadāru, and madhūka.

1.35.s:
madhūkasāraṃ sahasinduvāraṃ hiṅguṃ ca piṣṭā guṭikāṃ ca kuryāt .
dadyācca tasyāñjanalepanādi eṣo'gadaḥ sarpaviṣāṇi hanyāt . . 44
1.35.d:
मधूकसारं सहसिन्दुवारं हिङ्गुं च पिष्टा गुटिकां च कुर्यात् ।
दद्याच्च तस्याञ्जनलेपनादि एषोऽगदः सर्पविषाणि हन्यात् ॥ 44
1.35.m: Pounding madhūka-pith together with sinduvāra and asafoetida, one should make pills; / and one should apply it to him as eye-salve, ointment, and so on; this antidote destroys snake poisons.

1.35.s:
añjanaṃ caiva nasyaṃ ca kṣipraṃ dadyādviṣānvite .
vāyusthānaṃ tato muktvā majjāsthānaṃ pradhāvati . .45
1.35.d:
अञ्जनं चैव नस्यं च क्षिप्रं दद्याद्विषान्विते ।
वायुस्थानं ततो मुक्त्वा मज्जास्थानं प्रधावति ॥45
1.35.m: And one should quickly apply eye-salve and nasal drops to the poison-afflicted person. / Then, leaving the locus of wind, it runs forward to the locus of marrow.

1.35.s:
viṣe majjāgate vipra tasya rūpāṇi me śṛṇu .
dṛṣṭiśca hīyate tasya bhṛśamaṅgāni muñcati . .4 6
etāni yasya rūpāṇi tasya majjāgataṃ viṣam .
tasyāgadaṃ pravakṣyāmi yena sampadyate sukham . . 47
1.35.d:
विषे मज्जागते विप्र तस्य रूपाणि मे शृणु ।
दृष्टिश्च हीयते तस्य भृशमङ्गानि मुञ्चति ॥4 6
एतानि यस्य रूपाणि तस्य मज्जागतं विषम् ।
तस्यागदं प्रवक्ष्यामि येन सम्पद्यते सुखम् ॥ 47
1.35.m: When the poison has entered the marrow, O brahmin, hear from me its symptoms: / his eyesight fails, and he severely loses control of his limbs. / One in whom these symptoms appear has poison entered into the marrow; / I will declare the antidote for it, by which ease is obtained.

1.35.s:
ghṛtamadhuśarkarānvitamuśīraṃ caṃdanaṃ tathā ..
etadāloḍya dātavyaṃ pānaṃ nasyaṃ ca suvrata .. 48 ..
1.35.d:
घृतमधुशर्करान्वितमुशीरं चंदनं तथा ॥
एतदालोड्य दातव्यं पानं नस्यं च सुव्रत ॥ 48 ॥
1.35.m: Uśīra and sandalwood combined with ghee, honey, and sugar— / having stirred this together, one should administer it as a drink and nasal drops, O observant one.

1.35.s:
tataḥ praṇaśyate duḥkhaṃ tataḥ saṃpadyate sukham ..
atha tasminkṛte yoge viṣaṃ tasya nivartate ..49..
1.35.d:
ततः प्रणश्यते दुःखं ततः संपद्यते सुखम् ॥
अथ तस्मिन्कृते योगे विषं तस्य निवर्तते ॥49॥
1.35.m: Then his distress vanishes; then ease is attained. / When this preparation is made, then his poison subsides.

1.35.s:
majjāsthānaṃ tato gatvā marmasthānaṃ pradhāvati..
viṣe tu marma saṃprāpte śṛṇu rūpaṃ yathā bhavet..1.35.50..
1.35.d:
मज्जास्थानं ततो गत्वा मर्मस्थानं प्रधावति॥
विषे तु मर्म संप्राप्ते शृणु रूपं यथा भवेत्॥1.35.50॥
1.35.m: Having then gone to the locus of marrow, it runs forward to the vital points. / Now, when the poison has reached the vital point, hear the symptoms as they appear:

1.35.s:
niśceṣṭaḥ patate bhūmau karṇābhyāṃ badhiro bhavet..
vāriṇā sicyamānasya romaharṣo na jāyate ..51..
1.35.d:
निश्चेष्टः पतते भूमौ कर्णाभ्यां बधिरो भवेत्॥
वारिणा सिच्यमानस्य रोमहर्षो न जायते ॥51॥
1.35.m: Motionless, he falls to the ground; he becomes deaf in both ears; / when sprinkled with water, no horripilation arises.

1.35.s:
daṃḍena hanyamānasya daṃḍarājī na jāyate..
śastreṇa cchidyamānasya rudhiraṃ na pravartate .. 52 ..
1.35.d:
दंडेन हन्यमानस्य दंडराजी न जायते॥
शस्त्रेण च्छिद्यमानस्य रुधिरं न प्रवर्तते ॥ 52 ॥
1.35.m: When struck with a stick, no welts appear; / when cut with a blade, no blood flows.

1.35.s:
keśeṣu lucyamāneṣu naiva keśānpravedate ..
yasya karṇau ca pārśve ca hastapādaṃ ca saṃdhayaḥ ..
śithilāni bhavaṃtīha sa gatāsuriti śrutiḥ .. 53..
1.35.d:
केशेषु लुच्यमानेषु नैव केशान्प्रवेदते ॥
यस्य कर्णौ च पार्श्वे च हस्तपादं च संधयः ॥
शिथिलानि भवंतीह स गतासुरिति श्रुतिः ॥ 53॥
1.35.m: When his hairs are plucked, he does not feel the hairs at all. / He whose ears, flanks, hands, feet, and joints / become loose here—he has lost his life, so says tradition.

1.35.s:
etāni yasya rūpāṇi viparītāni gautama ..
mṛtaṃ tu na vijānīyātkaśyapasya vaco yathā ..54..
1.35.d:
एतानि यस्य रूपाणि विपरीतानि गौतम ॥
मृतं तु न विजानीयात्कश्यपस्य वचो यथा ॥54॥
1.35.m: He in whom these signs are the opposite, O Gautama, / one should not consider dead, according to Kaśyapa's word.

1.35.s:
vaidyāstasya na paśyaṃti ye bhavaṃti kuśikṣitāḥ ..
vicakṣaṇāstu paśyaṃti maṃtrauṣadhisamanvitāḥ ..55..
1.35.d:
वैद्यास्तस्य न पश्यंति ये भवंति कुशिक्षिताः ॥
विचक्षणास्तु पश्यंति मंत्रौषधिसमन्विताः ॥55॥
1.35.m: Physicians who are poorly trained do not see this; / but discerning ones who possess mantras and herbs do see it.

1.35.s:
tasyāgadaṃ pravakṣyāmi svayaṃ rudreṇa bhāṣitam ..
mayūrapittaṃ mārjārapittaṃ gandhanāḍīmūlameva ca .. 56 ..
1.35.d:
तस्यागदं प्रवक्ष्यामि स्वयं रुद्रेण भाषितम् ॥
मयूरपित्तं मार्जारपित्तं गन्धनाडीमूलमेव च ॥ 56 ॥
1.35.m: I will declare its antidote, spoken by Rudra himself: / peacock bile, cat bile, and gandhanāḍī root,

1.35.s:
kuṃkumaṃ tagaraṃ kuṣṭhaṃ kāsamardatvacaṃ tathā..
utpalasya ca kiṃjalkaṃ padmasya kumudasya ca .. 57 ..
1.35.d:
कुंकुमं तगरं कुष्ठं कासमर्दत्वचं तथा॥
उत्पलस्य च किंजल्कं पद्मस्य कुमुदस्य च ॥ 57 ॥
1.35.m: saffron, tagara, kuṣṭha, and kāsamarda bark, / and the filaments of the blue water-lily, lotus, and white water-lily.

1.35.s:
etāni samabhāgāni gomūtreṇa tu peṣayet ..
eṣo'gado yasya haste daṣṭo na mriyate sa vai ..
kālāhināpi daṣṭena kṣipraṃ bhavati nirviṣaḥ ..58..
1.35.d:
एतानि समभागानि गोमूत्रेण तु पेषयेत् ॥
एषोऽगदो यस्य हस्ते दष्टो न म्रियते स वै ॥
कालाहिनापि दष्टेन क्षिप्रं भवति निर्विषः ॥58॥
1.35.m: One should grind these in equal parts with cow's urine. / If this antidote is in someone's hand, one bitten does not die; / even if bitten by the serpent of death, he quickly becomes free of poison.

1.35.s:
kṣiprameva pradā tavyaṃ mṛtasaṃjīvanauṣadham ..
aṃjanaṃ caiva nasyaṃ ca kṣipraṃ dadyādvicakṣaṇaḥ .. 59 ..
1.35.d:
क्षिप्रमेव प्रदा तव्यं मृतसंजीवनौषधम् ॥
अंजनं चैव नस्यं च क्षिप्रं दद्याद्विचक्षणः ॥ 59 ॥
1.35.m: The medicine that restores the dead to life must be given immediately. / The discerning physician should quickly administer eye-salve and nasal drops.

1.36.s:
.. gautama uvāca.. ..
kīdṛśaṃ sarpadaṣṭasya sarpiṇyāḥ kīdṛśaṃ bhavet ..
kumāradaṣṭaḥ kīdṛksyātsūtikādaṃśitasya ca .. 1 ..
1.36.d:
॥ गौतम उवाच॥ ॥
कीदृशं सर्पदष्टस्य सर्पिण्याः कीदृशं भवेत् ॥
कुमारदष्टः कीदृक्स्यात्सूतिकादंशितस्य च ॥ 1 ॥
1.36.m: Gautama said: / What are the symptoms of one bitten by a male snake? What would be the symptoms of one bitten by a female snake? / What would be the symptoms of one bitten by a young male snake, and of one bitten by a female snake that has given birth?

1.36.s:
rūpaṃ napuṃsakeneha vyaṃtareṇa ca kīdṛśam ..
etadākhyāhi me sarvamebhirdaṣṭasya lakṣaṇam .. 2 .. ..
1.36.d:
रूपं नपुंसकेनेह व्यंतरेण च कीदृशम् ॥
एतदाख्याहि मे सर्वमेभिर्दष्टस्य लक्षणम् ॥ 2 ॥ ॥
1.36.m: What is the symptom when bitten here by a neuter snake, and by an intermediate snake? / Tell me all this, the characteristics of one bitten by these.

1.36.s:
.. kaśyapa uvāca .. ..
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi nāgānāṃ rūpalakṣaṇam ..
sarpadaṣṭasya ca tathā samāsāddvijapuṃgava .. 3 ..
1.36.d:
॥ कश्यप उवाच ॥ ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि नागानां रूपलक्षणम् ॥
सर्पदष्टस्य च तथा समासाद्द्विजपुंगव ॥ 3 ॥
1.36.m: Kaśyapa said: / Henceforth I will declare the signs and characteristics of snakes, / and likewise of one bitten by a snake, in brief, O bull among the twice-born.

1.36.s:
atha sarpeṇa daṣṭasya ūrdhva dṛṣṭiḥ prajāyate ..
sarpīdaṣṭasya ca tathā adhodṛṣṭiḥ prajāyate .. 4 ..
1.36.d:
अथ सर्पेण दष्टस्य ऊर्ध्व दृष्टिः प्रजायते ॥
सर्पीदष्टस्य च तथा अधोदृष्टिः प्रजायते ॥ 4 ॥
1.36.m: Now, for one bitten by a male snake, an upward gaze arises; / and for one bitten by a female snake, a downward gaze arises.

1.36.s:
kanyādaṣṭasya vāmā syādṛṣṭirdvijavarottama ..
kumāreṇāpi daṣṭasya dakṣiṇā eva jāyate ..5..
1.36.d:
कन्यादष्टस्य वामा स्यादृष्टिर्द्विजवरोत्तम ॥
कुमारेणापि दष्टस्य दक्षिणा एव जायते ॥5॥
1.36.m: For one bitten by a young female snake, the gaze is to the left, O best of the twice-born; / and for one bitten by a young male snake, it is to the right.

1.36.s:
garbhiṇyā vātha daṣṭasya tathā svedaśca jāyate ..
romāṃcaḥ sūtikāyāstu vepathuścāpi jāyate ..
napuṃsakena daṣṭasya aṃgamardaḥ prajāyate .. ..6..
1.36.d:
गर्भिण्या वाथ दष्टस्य तथा स्वेदश्च जायते ॥
रोमांचः सूतिकायास्तु वेपथुश्चापि जायते ॥
नपुंसकेन दष्टस्य अंगमर्दः प्रजायते ॥ ॥6॥
1.36.m: When bitten by a pregnant female snake, sweating arises; / from one that has given birth, horripilation and trembling arise; / when bitten by a neuter snake, body-ache arises.

1.36.s:
pannagyaḥ prabhavo rātrau divā sarpo viṣādhikaḥ..
napuṃsakastu saṃdhyāyāṃ kaśyapena tu bhāṣitam..7..
1.36.d:
पन्नग्यः प्रभवो रात्रौ दिवा सर्पो विषाधिकः॥
नपुंसकस्तु संध्यायां कश्यपेन तु भाषितम्॥7॥
1.36.m: The power of female snakes is at night; by day, a male snake is more venomous; / a neuter snake is venomous at twilight—so it was stated by Kaśyapa.

1.36.s:
aṃdhakāre tu daṣṭo ya udake gahane vane ..
supto vā cetpramatto vā yadi sarpaṃ na paśyati ..
daṣṭarūpāṇyajānanvai kathaṃ vaidyacikitsitam..8..
1.36.d:
अंधकारे तु दष्टो य उदके गहने वने ॥
सुप्तो वा चेत्प्रमत्तो वा यदि सर्पं न पश्यति ॥
दष्टरूपाण्यजानन्वै कथं वैद्यचिकित्सितम्॥8॥
1.36.m: If one is bitten in the dark, in water, or in a dense forest, / or while asleep or intoxicated, if he does not see the snake, / not knowing the symptoms of the bite, how should the physician treat it?

1.36.s:
caturvidhā iha proktāḥ pannagāstu mahātmanā ..
darvīkarā maṃḍalino rājilā vyaṃtarāstathā .. 9 ..
1.36.d:
चतुर्विधा इह प्रोक्ताः पन्नगास्तु महात्मना ॥
दर्वीकरा मंडलिनो राजिला व्यंतरास्तथा ॥ 9 ॥
1.36.m: Snakes are declared by the great-souled one to be of four kinds here: / hooded, spotted, striped, and intermediate.

1.36.s:
darvīkarā vātaviṣā maṃḍalā paittikāḥ smṛtāḥ ..
śleṣmalā rājilrā jñeyā vyaṃtarāḥ sānnipātikāḥ .. 1.36.10 ..
1.36.d:
दर्वीकरा वातविषा मंडला पैत्तिकाः स्मृताः ॥
श्लेष्मला राजिल्रा ज्ञेया व्यंतराः सान्निपातिकाः ॥ 1.36.10 ॥
1.36.m: Hooded snakes have wind-poison; spotted snakes are considered bilious; / striped snakes are known to be phlegmatic; intermediate snakes are tridoshic.

1.36.s:
raktaṃ parīkṣayedeṣāṃ sarpāṇāṃ tu pṛthakpṛthak ..
kṛṣṇaṃ darvīkarāṇāṃ tu jāyate nālpamulbaṇam .. 11 ..
1.36.d:
रक्तं परीक्षयेदेषां सर्पाणां तु पृथक्पृथक् ॥
कृष्णं दर्वीकराणां तु जायते नाल्पमुल्बणम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.36.m: One should examine the blood of these snakes individually: / in the case of hooded snakes, the blood is black and by no means little or weak.

1.36.s:
raktaṃ ghanaṃ ca bahuśaḥ śoṇitaṃ maṃḍalī kṛtam ..
picchilaṃ rājile svalpaṃ tadvadvyaṃtarake tathā .. 12 ..
1.36.d:
रक्तं घनं च बहुशः शोणितं मंडली कृतम् ॥
पिच्छिलं राजिले स्वल्पं तद्वद्व्यंतरके तथा ॥ 12 ॥
1.36.m: In the case of a spotted snake, the blood is thick and copiously shed; / in a striped snake, it is slimy and scant; likewise so in an intermediate one.

1.36.s:
sarpā jñeyāstu catvāraḥ paṃcamo nopalabhyate ..
brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdra ścaiva caturthakaḥ .. 13 ..
1.36.d:
सर्पा ज्ञेयास्तु चत्वारः पंचमो नोपलभ्यते ॥
ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियो वैश्यः शूद्र श्चैव चतुर्थकः ॥ 13 ॥
1.36.m: Four classes of snakes are to be known; a fifth is not found: / Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, and Śūdra as the fourth.

1.36.s:
brāhmaṇe madhuraṃ dadyāttiktaṃ dadyāttathottare ..
vaiśye karṣaphalaṃ dadyācchūdre tristhūṇameva ca .. 14 ..
1.36.d:
ब्राह्मणे मधुरं दद्यात्तिक्तं दद्यात्तथोत्तरे ॥
वैश्ये कर्षफलं दद्याच्छूद्रे त्रिस्थूणमेव च ॥ 14 ॥
1.36.m: For a Brāhmaṇa snake, one should give sweet; and for the next, one should give bitter; / for a Vaiśya snake, one should give karṣaphala; and for a Śūdra snake, tristhūṇa.

1.36.s:
brāhmaṇena tu daṣṭasya dāho gātreṣu jāyate ..
mūrcchā ca prabalā syādvai nātmānamabhijānate .. 15 ..
1.36.d:
ब्राह्मणेन तु दष्टस्य दाहो गात्रेषु जायते ॥
मूर्च्छा च प्रबला स्याद्वै नात्मानमभिजानते ॥ 15 ॥
1.36.m: In one bitten by a Brāhmaṇa snake, burning sensation arises in the limbs, / and strong fainting occurs; he does not recognise himself.

1.36.s:
śyāmavarṇaṃ mukhaṃ ca syānmajjāstaṃbhaśca jāyate ..
tasya kuryātpratīkāraṃ yena saṃpadyate sukham .. 16 ..
1.36.d:
श्यामवर्णं मुखं च स्यान्मज्जास्तंभश्च जायते ॥
तस्य कुर्यात्प्रतीकारं येन संपद्यते सुखम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.36.m: His face becomes dark-hued, and stiffness of the marrow arises; / one should apply the remedy for it, by which ease is obtained.

1.36.s:
aśvagaṃdhāpyapāmārgaḥ siṃduvāraṃ surāmayam ..
etatsarpiḥ samāyuktaṃ pāne nasye ca dāpayet ..
etenaivopacāreṇa sukhī bhavati mānavaḥ .. 17 ..
1.36.d:
अश्वगंधाप्यपामार्गः सिंदुवारं सुरामयम् ॥
एतत्सर्पिः समायुक्तं पाने नस्ये च दापयेत् ॥
एतेनैवोपचारेण सुखी भवति मानवः ॥ 17 ॥
1.36.m: Aśvagandhā, apāmārga, sinduvāra, and kuṣṭha— / combined with ghee, one should administer this as a drink and nasal drops; / by this very treatment the man becomes comfortable.

1.36.s:
kṣatriyeṇa tu daṣṭasya kaṃpo gātreṣu jāyate ..
mūrchā mohastathā syādvai nātmānamabhivetti saḥ .. 18 ..
1.36.d:
क्षत्रियेण तु दष्टस्य कंपो गात्रेषु जायते ॥
मूर्छा मोहस्तथा स्याद्वै नात्मानमभिवेत्ति सः ॥ 18 ॥
1.36.m: In one bitten by a Kṣatriya snake, trembling arises in the limbs, / and fainting and bewilderment occur; he does not know himself.

1.36.s:
jāyate vedanā tasya ūrdhvaṃ caiva nirīkṣate ..
tasya kuryātpratīkāraṃ yena saṃpadyate sukham .. 19 ..
1.36.d:
जायते वेदना तस्य ऊर्ध्वं चैव निरीक्षते ॥
तस्य कुर्यात्प्रतीकारं येन संपद्यते सुखम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.36.m: Pain arises for him, and he stares upwards; / one should apply the remedy for it, by which ease is obtained.

1.36.s:
arkamūlamapāmārgaṃ priyaṃgumindravāruṇīm ..
etatsarpiḥ samāyuktaṃ pānaṃ nasyaṃ ca dāpayet ..
etenaivopacāreṇa sukhī bhavati mānavaḥ .. 1.36.20 ..
1.36.d:
अर्कमूलमपामार्गं प्रियंगुमिन्द्रवारुणीम् ॥
एतत्सर्पिः समायुक्तं पानं नस्यं च दापयेत् ॥
एतेनैवोपचारेण सुखी भवति मानवः ॥ 1.36.20 ॥
1.36.m: Arka root, apāmārga, priyaṅgu, and indravāruṇī— / combined with ghee, one should administer this as a drink and nasal drops; / by this very treatment the man becomes comfortable.

1.36.s:
vaiśyenāpi hi daṣṭasya śṛṇu rūpāṇi yāni tu ..
śleṣmaprakopo lālā ca na codvahati cetanām .. 21 ..
1.36.d:
वैश्येनापि हि दष्टस्य शृणु रूपाणि यानि तु ॥
श्लेष्मप्रकोपो लाला च न चोद्वहति चेतनाम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.36.m: Hear the symptoms of one bitten by a Vaiśya snake: / aggravation of phlegm, salivation, and he does not maintain consciousness.

1.36.s:
mūrchā ca prabalā yasya ātmānaṃ nābhinaṃdati ..
tasya kuryātpratīkāraṃ yena saṃpadyate sukham .. 22 ..
1.36.d:
मूर्छा च प्रबला यस्य आत्मानं नाभिनंदति ॥
तस्य कुर्यात्प्रतीकारं येन संपद्यते सुखम् ॥ 22 ॥
1.36.m: He who suffers severe fainting does not take joy in himself; / one should apply the remedy for it, by which ease is obtained.

1.36.s:
aśvagaṃdhā sagomūtrā gṛha dhūmaṃ saguggulam ..
śirīṣārkapalāśena śvetā ca girikarṇikā .. 23 ..
1.36.d:
अश्वगंधा सगोमूत्रा गृह धूमं सगुग्गुलम् ॥
शिरीषार्कपलाशेन श्वेता च गिरिकर्णिका ॥ 23 ॥
1.36.m: Aśvagandhā with cow's urine, soot with guggulu, / with śirīṣa, arka, and palāśa, and white girikarṇikā—

1.36.s:
gomūtreṇa samāyuktaṃ pānaṃ nasyaṃ ca dāpayet ..
eṣa vaiśyena daṣṭānāmagadaḥ parikīrttitaḥ .. 24 ..
1.36.d:
गोमूत्रेण समायुक्तं पानं नस्यं च दापयेत् ॥
एष वैश्येन दष्टानामगदः परिकीर्त्तितः ॥ 24 ॥
1.36.m: combined with cow's urine, one should administer it as a drink and nasal drops; / this is proclaimed as the antidote for those bitten by a Vaiśya snake.

1.36.s:
śūdreṇāpi hi daṣṭasya śṛṇu tattvena gautama ..
kuthyate vepate caiva jvaraḥ śītaṃ ca jāyate .. 25 ..
1.36.d:
शूद्रेणापि हि दष्टस्य शृणु तत्त्वेन गौतम ॥
कुथ्यते वेपते चैव ज्वरः शीतं च जायते ॥ 25 ॥
1.36.m: Hear now truly, O Gautama, of one bitten by a Śūdra [snake]: / he is afflicted with putrefaction, he trembles, and fever and chill arise;

1.36.s:
aṃgāni culuculāyaṃte śūdradaṣṭasya lakṣaṇam ..
tatrāgadaṃ pravakṣyāmi yena saṃpadyate sukham .. 26 ..
1.36.d:
अंगानि चुलुचुलायंते शूद्रदष्टस्य लक्षणम् ॥
तत्रागदं प्रवक्ष्यामि येन संपद्यते सुखम् ॥ 26 ॥
1.36.m: his limbs tingle: this is the sign of one bitten by a Śūdra. / Thereupon I shall declare the antidote by which ease is obtained:

1.36.s:
padmaṃ ca lodhrakaṃ caiva kṣaudraṃ padmasya kesaram ..
madhūkasāraṃ madhu ca śvetāṃ ca girikarṇikām .. 27 ..
1.36.d:
पद्मं च लोध्रकं चैव क्षौद्रं पद्मस्य केसरम् ॥
मधूकसारं मधु च श्वेतां च गिरिकर्णिकाम् ॥ 27 ॥
1.36.m: lotus, lodhra, wild honey, lotus filaments, / mahua pith, honey, and white clitoria—

1.36.s:
etāni samabhāgāni peṣayecchītavāriṇā ..
pānalepāṃjanairnasyaiḥ sukhī bhavati mānavaḥ .. 28 ..
1.36.d:
एतानि समभागानि पेषयेच्छीतवारिणा ॥
पानलेपांजनैर्नस्यैः सुखी भवति मानवः ॥ 28 ॥
1.36.m: one should grind equal parts of these with cold water. / Through drinks, salves, collyria, and nasal drops, the man becomes well.

1.36.s:
pūrvāhṇe carate vipro madhyāhne kṣatriyaścaret ..
aparāhne caredvaiśyaḥ śūdraḥ saṃdhyācaro bhavet ..29..
1.36.d:
पूर्वाह्णे चरते विप्रो मध्याह्ने क्षत्रियश्चरेत् ॥
अपराह्ने चरेद्वैश्यः शूद्रः संध्याचरो भवेत् ॥29॥
1.36.m: The Brahmin [snake] roams in the forenoon; the Kṣatriya roams at noon; / the Vaiśya roams in the afternoon; the Śūdra moves at twilight.

1.36.s:
āhāro vāyupuṣpāṇi brāhmaṇānāṃ vidurbudhāḥ ..
mūṣikā kṣatri yāṇāṃ ca āhāro dvijasattama ..
vaiśyā maṃḍūkabhakṣāśca śūdrāḥ sarvāśinastathā ..1.36.30..
1.36.d:
आहारो वायुपुष्पाणि ब्राह्मणानां विदुर्बुधाः ॥
मूषिका क्षत्रि याणां च आहारो द्विजसत्तम ॥
वैश्या मंडूकभक्षाश्च शूद्राः सर्वाशिनस्तथा ॥1.36.30॥
1.36.m: The wise know the food of Brahmins to be air and flowers; / and mice are the food of Kṣatriyas, O best of the twice-born; / Vaiśyas feed on frogs, and Śūdras are omnivorous.

1.36.s:
agrato daśate vipraḥ kṣatriyo dakṣiṇena tu ..
vāmapārśve sadā vaiśyaḥ paścādvai śūdra ādaśet .. 31 ..
1.36.d:
अग्रतो दशते विप्रः क्षत्रियो दक्षिणेन तु ॥
वामपार्श्वे सदा वैश्यः पश्चाद्वै शूद्र आदशेत् ॥ 31 ॥
1.36.m: A Brahmin bites in front, but a Kṣatriya on the right side; / a Vaiśya always bites on the left flank, and indeed a Śūdra bites from behind.

1.36.s:
madakāle tu saṃprāpte pīḍyamānā mahāviṣāḥ ..
avelāyāṃ daśaṃte vai maithunārtā bhujaṃgamāḥ .. 32 ..
1.36.d:
मदकाले तु संप्राप्ते पीड्यमाना महाविषाः ॥
अवेलायां दशंते वै मैथुनार्ता भुजंगमाः ॥ 32 ॥
1.36.m: When the rutting season has arrived, those afflicted serpents of deadly poison, / tormented by sexual desire, bite out of season.

1.36.s:
puṣpagaṃdhāḥ smṛtā viprāḥ kṣatriyāścaṃdanāvahāḥ ..
vaiśyāśca ghṛtagaṃdhā vai śūdrāḥ syurmatsyagaṃdhinaḥ .. 33 ..
1.36.d:
पुष्पगंधाः स्मृता विप्राः क्षत्रियाश्चंदनावहाः ॥
वैश्याश्च घृतगंधा वै शूद्राः स्युर्मत्स्यगंधिनः ॥ 33 ॥
1.36.m: Brahmins are recorded as having the smell of flowers, and Kṣatriyas carry the scent of sandalwood; / Vaiśyas have the smell of ghee, and Śūdras have a fish-like odour.

1.36.s:
vāsaṃ teṣāṃ pravakṣyāmi yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ ..
vāpīkūpataḍāgeṣu giriprasravaṇeṣu ca ..
vasaṃti brāhmaṇāḥ sarpā grāmadvāre catuṣpathe ..34..
1.36.d:
वासं तेषां प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावदनुपूर्वशः ॥
वापीकूपतडागेषु गिरिप्रस्रवणेषु च ॥
वसंति ब्राह्मणाः सर्पा ग्रामद्वारे चतुष्पथे ॥34॥
1.36.m: I shall declare their dwellings properly in order: / in stepwells, wells, and tanks, and at mountain springs, / Brahmin serpents dwell, and at village gates and crossroads.

1.36.s:
ārāmeṣu pavitreṣu śuciṣvāyataneṣu ca ..
vasanti kṣatriyā nityaṃ toraṇeṣu saraḥsu ca ..35..
1.36.d:
आरामेषु पवित्रेषु शुचिष्वायतनेषु च ॥
वसन्ति क्षत्रिया नित्यं तोरणेषु सरःसु च ॥35॥
1.36.m: In groves, in holy places, and in pure shrines, / Kṣatriyas dwell continually, and at archways and lakes.

1.36.s:
śmaśāne bhasmaśālāsu palāleṣu taṭeṣu ca ..
goṣṭheṣu pathi vṛkṣeṣu vipra vaiśyā vasaṃti ca ..36..
1.36.d:
श्मशाने भस्मशालासु पलालेषु तटेषु च ॥
गोष्ठेषु पथि वृक्षेषु विप्र वैश्या वसंति च ॥36॥
1.36.m: In cremation grounds, ash-houses, straw heaps, and banks, / in cowsheds, on paths, and in trees, O Brahmin, dwell the Vaiśyas.

1.36.s:
avivikteṣu sthāneṣu nirjaneṣu vaneṣu ca ..
śūnyāgāre śmaśāne ca śūdrā vipra vasaṃti ca .. 37 ..
1.36.d:
अविविक्तेषु स्थानेषु निर्जनेषु वनेषु च ॥
शून्यागारे श्मशाने च शूद्रा विप्र वसंति च ॥ 37 ॥
1.36.m: In unsociable places, in uninhabited forests, / in deserted houses, and in cremation grounds, O Brahmin, dwell the Śūdras.

1.36.s:
śvetāśca kapilāścaiva ye sarpāstvanalaprabhāḥ ..
manasvinaḥ sāttvikāśca brāhmaṇāste budhaiḥ smṛtāḥ ..38..
1.36.d:
श्वेताश्च कपिलाश्चैव ये सर्पास्त्वनलप्रभाः ॥
मनस्विनः सात्त्विकाश्च ब्राह्मणास्ते बुधैः स्मृताः ॥38॥
1.36.m: Those serpents that are white and tawny, having the splendour of fire, / intelligent and endowed with the quality of goodness, are known by the wise as Brahmins.

1.36.s:
raktavarṇāḥ suvarṇābhāḥ pravālamaṇisaṃnibhāḥ ..
sūryaprabhāstathā vipra kṣatriyāste bhujaṃgamāḥ..39..
1.36.d:
रक्तवर्णाः सुवर्णाभाः प्रवालमणिसंनिभाः ॥
सूर्यप्रभास्तथा विप्र क्षत्रियास्ते भुजंगमाः॥39॥
1.36.m: Serpents red in colour, of golden radiance, resembling corals and gems, / and having the radiance of the sun, O Brahmin, are Kṣatriyas.

1.36.s:
nānāvicitrarājībhiratasīvarṇasannibhāḥ..
bāṇa puṣpasavarṇābhā vaiśyāste vai bhujaṃgamāḥ .. 1.36.40 ..
1.36.d:
नानाविचित्रराजीभिरतसीवर्णसन्निभाः॥
बाण पुष्पसवर्णाभा वैश्यास्ते वै भुजंगमाः ॥ 1.36.40 ॥
1.36.m: Those serpents resembling the colour of flax with varied, manifold stripes, / having the hue of bāṇa flowers, are indeed Vaiśyas.

1.36.s:
kākodaranibhāḥ kecidye ca aṃjanasannibhāḥ ..
kākavarṇā dhūmravarṇāste śūdrāḥ parikīrtitāḥ ..41..
1.36.d:
काकोदरनिभाः केचिद्ये च अंजनसन्निभाः ॥
काकवर्णा धूम्रवर्णास्ते शूद्राः परिकीर्तिताः ॥41॥
1.36.m: Those that resemble a crow's belly, some that look like collyrium, / crow-coloured, and smoke-coloured: these are proclaimed as Śūdras.

1.36.s:
yasya sarpeṇa daṣṭasya daṃśamaṃguṣṭhamaṃtaram ..
bāladaṣṭaṃ vijānīyātkaśyapasya vaco yathā.. 42 ..
1.36.d:
यस्य सर्पेण दष्टस्य दंशमंगुष्ठमंतरम् ॥
बालदष्टं विजानीयात्कश्यपस्य वचो यथा॥ 42 ॥
1.36.m: The bitten person on whom the bite mark is the distance of a thumb / should be known as bitten by a young [snake], according to the word of Kaśyapa.

1.36.s:
yasya sarpeṇa daṣṭasya daṃśaṃ dvyaṃgulamaṃtaram ..
yauvanasthena daṣṭasya etadbhavati lakṣaṇam .. 43 ..
1.36.d:
यस्य सर्पेण दष्टस्य दंशं द्व्यंगुलमंतरम् ॥
यौवनस्थेन दष्टस्य एतद्भवति लक्षणम् ॥ 43 ॥
1.36.m: The bitten person on whom the bite mark is two finger-breadths apart: / this is the sign of one bitten by a [snake] in the prime of youth.

1.36.s:
yasya sarpeṇa daṣṭasya sārdhaṃ dvyaṃgulamaztaram ..
vṛddhadaṣṭaṃ vijānīyātkaśyapasya vaco yathā .. 44 ..
1.36.d:
यस्य सर्पेण दष्टस्य सार्धं द्व्यंगुलमzतरम् ॥
वृद्धदष्टं विजानीयात्कश्यपस्य वचो यथा ॥ 44 ॥
1.36.m: The bitten person on whom the bite mark is two and a half finger-breadths apart / should be known as bitten by an old [snake], according to the word of Kaśyapa.

1.36.s:
anaṃtaḥ prekṣate pūrvaṃ vāmapārśve tu vāsukiḥ ..
takṣako dakṣiṇeneha karkoṭaḥ pṛṣṭhatastathā .. 45 ..
1.36.d:
अनंतः प्रेक्षते पूर्वं वामपार्श्वे तु वासुकिः ॥
तक्षको दक्षिणेनेह कर्कोटः पृष्ठतस्तथा ॥ 45 ॥
1.36.m: Ananta looks to the east, but Vāsuki to the left side; / Takṣaka is on the right here, and Karkoṭa behind.

1.36.s:
calate bhramate padmo mahāpadmo nimajjati ..
visaṃjñastiṣṭhate caiva śaṃkhapālo muhurmuhuḥ .. 46 ..
1.36.d:
चलते भ्रमते पद्मो महापद्मो निमज्जति ॥
विसंज्ञस्तिष्ठते चैव शंखपालो मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ 46 ॥
1.36.m: Padma trembles and roams; Mahāpadma dives; / and Śaṅkhapāla remains unconscious time and again.

1.36.s:
sarveṣāṃ kurute rūpaṃ kulikaḥ pannagottamaḥ ..
anaṃtasya diśā pūrvā vāsukestu hutāśanī ..47..
1.36.d:
सर्वेषां कुरुते रूपं कुलिकः पन्नगोत्तमः ॥
अनंतस्य दिशा पूर्वा वासुकेस्तु हुताशनी ॥47॥
1.36.m: Kulika, the best of serpents, assumes the form of all. / The eastern direction belongs to Ananta, and the fire-direction (south-east) to Vāsuki;

1.36.s:
dakṣiṇā takṣakasyoktā karkoṭasya tu nairṛtī ..
paścimā padmanābhasya mahāpadmasya vāyujā ..
uttarā śaṃkhapālasya aiśānī kaṃbalasya tu..48..
1.36.d:
दक्षिणा तक्षकस्योक्ता कर्कोटस्य तु नैरृती ॥
पश्चिमा पद्मनाभस्य महापद्मस्य वायुजा ॥
उत्तरा शंखपालस्य ऐशानी कंबलस्य तु॥48॥
1.36.m: the southern is declared to be Takṣaka's, but the south-western belongs to Karkoṭa; / the western is Padmanābha's, the wind-direction (north-west) Mahāpadma's, / the northern Śaṅkhapāla's, and the north-eastern belongs to Kambala.

1.36.s:
anaṃtasya bhavetpadmaṃ vāsukeḥ syāttathotpalam ..
svastikaṃ takṣakasyoktaṃ karkoṭasya tu paṃkajam .. 49 ..
1.36.d:
अनंतस्य भवेत्पद्मं वासुकेः स्यात्तथोत्पलम् ॥
स्वस्तिकं तक्षकस्योक्तं कर्कोटस्य तु पंकजम् ॥ 49 ॥
1.36.m: Ananta's [mark] is a lotus, and Vāsuki's a blue lotus; / a svastika is declared for Takṣaka, and a water-lily for Karkoṭa;

1.36.s:
padmasya tu bhavetpadmaṃ śūlaṃ padmetarasya tu ..
śaṃkhapāle bhavecchatraṃ kulikasyārdhacandrakam .. 1.36.50 ..
1.36.d:
पद्मस्य तु भवेत्पद्मं शूलं पद्मेतरस्य तु ॥
शंखपाले भवेच्छत्रं कुलिकस्यार्धचन्द्रकम् ॥ 1.36.50 ॥
1.36.m: Padma's is a lotus, but a trident is the other Padma's; / for Śaṅkhapāla there is a royal parasol, and for Kulika a crescent moon.

1.36.s:
anaṃtakapilau viprau kṣatriyau śaṃkhavāsukī ..
mahāpadmastakṣakaśca vaiśyau vipra prakīrtitau ..
padmakarkoṭakau śūdrau sadā jñeyau manīṣibhiḥ .. 51 ..
1.36.d:
अनंतकपिलौ विप्रौ क्षत्रियौ शंखवासुकी ॥
महापद्मस्तक्षकश्च वैश्यौ विप्र प्रकीर्तितौ ॥
पद्मकर्कोटकौ शूद्रौ सदा ज्ञेयौ मनीषिभिः ॥ 51 ॥
1.36.m: Ananta and Kapila are Brahmins; Śaṅkha and Vāsuki are Kṣatriyas; / Mahāpadma and Takṣaka are declared to be Vaiśyas, O Brahmin; / Padma and Karkoṭaka are always to be known by the wise as Śūdras.

1.36.s:
anaṃtakulikau varṇato brahmasaṃbhavau ..
vāsukiḥ śaṃkhapālaśca raktau hyagnisamudbhavau .. 52 ..
1.36.d:
अनंतकुलिकौ वर्णतो ब्रह्मसंभवौ ॥
वासुकिः शंखपालश्च रक्तौ ह्यग्निसमुद्भवौ ॥ 52 ॥
1.36.m: Ananta and Kulika, by caste, are born from Brahmā; / Vāsuki and Śaṅkhapāla, red in hue, are born from Agni;

1.36.s:
takṣakaśca mahāpadma īṣatpītau babhūvatuḥ ..
padmakarkoṭakau vipra sarpau kṛṣṇau babhūvatuḥ .. 53 ..
1.36.d:
तक्षकश्च महापद्म ईषत्पीतौ बभूवतुः ॥
पद्मकर्कोटकौ विप्र सर्पौ कृष्णौ बभूवतुः ॥ 53 ॥
1.36.m: Takṣaka and Mahāpadma were slightly yellow; / Padma and Karkoṭaka, O Brahmin, were black serpents.

1.36.s:
hayaṃ yānaṃ vṛṣaṃ chatraṃ rājānamatha pāvakam ..
dharaṇīmutpādya dhṛtānetānsiddhikarānviduḥ .. ..54..
1.36.d:
हयं यानं वृषं छत्रं राजानमथ पावकम् ॥
धरणीमुत्पाद्य धृतानेतान्सिद्धिकरान्विदुः ॥ ॥54॥
1.36.m: A horse, a carriage, a bull, a royal parasol, a king, or fire— / these, brought forth and carried, are known to bring success over the earth.

1.36.s:
pūrṇakumbhaḥ patākā ca kāṃcanaṃ maṇayastathā ..
śirīṣaṃ māṇikaṃ kaṇṭhe jīvajīveti suvrata ..
eteṣāṃ darśanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kanyā caikaprasūyikā ..55..
1.36.d:
पूर्णकुम्भः पताका च कांचनं मणयस्तथा ॥
शिरीषं माणिकं कण्ठे जीवजीवेति सुव्रत ॥
एतेषां दर्शनं श्रेष्ठं कन्या चैकप्रसूयिका ॥55॥
1.36.m: A full waterpot, a banner, gold, gems, / a śirīṣa flower, a ruby upon the neck, and the cry 'live, live!', O you of good vows: / the sight of these is auspicious, as is a woman with an only child.

1.36.s:
catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ samākhyātā bhogino ye tu pannagāḥ .
adṛśyāsteṣu ṣaṭtriṃśaddṛśyāstriṃśanmahīcarāḥ .. 56 ..
1.36.d:
चतुःषष्टिः समाख्याता भोगिनो ये तु पन्नगाः ।
अदृश्यास्तेषु षट्त्रिंशद्दृश्यास्त्रिंशन्महीचराः ॥ 56 ॥
1.36.m: Sixty-four are declared to be the hooded serpents: / of those, thirty-six are invisible, and thirty are visible earth-dwellers.

1.36.s:
viṃśacca sragviṇaḥ proktāḥ sapta maṃḍalinastathā .
rājīvanto daśa proktā darvyaḥ ṣoḍaśa paṃca ca .. 57 ..
1.36.d:
विंशच्च स्रग्विणः प्रोक्ताः सप्त मंडलिनस्तथा ।
राजीवन्तो दश प्रोक्ता दर्व्यः षोडश पंच च ॥ 57 ॥
1.36.m: Twenty are called garland-bearing, and seven are coiled; / ten are declared striped, and twenty-one hooded.

1.36.s:
duṃdubho ḍuṃḍubhaścaiva ceṭabhaśceṃdravāhanaḥ ..
nāgapuṣpasavarṇākhyā nirviṣā ye ca pannagāḥ..
evameva tu sarpāṇāṃ śatadvinavati smṛtam ..58..
1.36.d:
दुंदुभो डुंडुभश्चैव चेटभश्चेंद्रवाहनः ॥
नागपुष्पसवर्णाख्या निर्विषा ये च पन्नगाः॥
एवमेव तु सर्पाणां शतद्विनवति स्मृतम् ॥58॥
1.36.m: The dundubha, the ḍuṇḍubha, the ceṭabha, the indravāhana, / and those venomless serpents called after the colour of nāgapuṣpa flowers— / in this manner there are known to be one hundred and ninety-two serpents.

1.36.s:
varāhakarṇīṃ gajapippalīṃ ca gāṃdhārikāṃ pippaladevadāru ..
madhūkasāraṃ sahasiṃduvāraṃ hiṃguṃ ca piṣṭvā guṭikā ca kāryā ..59..
1.36.d:
वराहकर्णीं गजपिप्पलीं च गांधारिकां पिप्पलदेवदारु ॥
मधूकसारं सहसिंदुवारं हिंगुं च पिष्ट्वा गुटिका च कार्या ॥59॥
1.36.m: Varāhakarṇī, gajapippalī, gāndhārikā, pippala, deodar, / mahua pith along with sinduvāra, and asafoetida: having ground [these], a pill is to be made.

1.36.s:
.. sumaṃturuvāca .. ..
ityuktavānpurā vīra gautamasya prajāpatiḥ..
lakṣaṇaṃ sarvaināgānāṃ rūpavarṇau viṣaṃ tathā .. 1.36.60 ..
1.36.d:
॥ सुमंतुरुवाच ॥ ॥
इत्युक्तवान्पुरा वीर गौतमस्य प्रजापतिः॥
लक्षणं सर्वैनागानां रूपवर्णौ विषं तथा ॥ 1.36.60 ॥
1.36.m: Sumantu said: / Thus in ancient times, O hero, did Prajāpati speak to Gautama / concerning the characteristics, appearance, color, and poison of all snakes.

1.36.s:
tasmātsaṃpūjayennāgānsadā bhaktyā samanvitaḥ ..
viśeṣatastu paṃcamyāṃ payasā pāyasena ca ..61..
1.36.d:
तस्मात्संपूजयेन्नागान्सदा भक्त्या समन्वितः ॥
विशेषतस्तु पंचम्यां पयसा पायसेन च ॥61॥
1.36.m: Therefore one should worship the snakes always endowed with devotion, / especially on the fifth [tithi], with milk and milk-rice.

1.36.s:
śrāvaṇe māsi paṃcamyāṃ śuklapakṣe narā dhipa .
dvārasyobhayato lekhyā gomayena viṣolbaṇāḥ .. 62 .
1.36.d:
श्रावणे मासि पंचम्यां शुक्लपक्षे नरा धिप ।
द्वारस्योभयतो लेख्या गोमयेन विषोल्बणाः ॥ 62 ।
1.36.m: In the month of Śrāvaṇa, on the fifth [tithi] of the bright fortnight, O lord of men, / terribly venomous [serpents] are to be drawn on both sides of the door with cow dung.

1.36.s:
pūjayedvidhivaddvāraṃ dadhidūrvākṣataiḥ kuśaiḥ .
gaṃdhapuṣpopahāraiśca brāhmaṇānāṃ ca tarpaṇaiḥ.. 63..
1.36.d:
पूजयेद्विधिवद्द्वारं दधिदूर्वाक्षतैः कुशैः ।
गंधपुष्पोपहारैश्च ब्राह्मणानां च तर्पणैः॥ 63॥
1.36.m: One should worship the doorway according to rule with curds, dūrvā grass, unbroken grains, and kuśa grass, / and with gifts of perfumes and flowers, and through satiating Brahmins.

1.36.s:
ye tvasyāṃ pūjaṃtīha nāgānbhaktipuraḥsarāḥ..
na teṣāṃ sarvapato vīra bhayaṃ bhavati karhicit.64..
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddha sāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi pañcamīkalpe śrāvaṇikanāgapañcamīvratavarṇanaṃnāma ṣaṭtriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 36 .. .. cha ..
1.36.d:
ये त्वस्यां पूजंतीह नागान्भक्तिपुरःसराः॥
न तेषां सर्वपतो वीर भयं भवति कर्हिचित्.64॥
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्ध साहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि पञ्चमीकल्पे श्रावणिकनागपञ्चमीव्रतवर्णनंनाम षट्त्रिंशोऽध्यायः ॥ 36 ॥ ॥ छ ॥
1.36.m:
Those who worship the snakes on this [day] preceded by devotion / have no fear whatsoever of snakes, O hero.
Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter, named 'The Description of the Śrāvaṇika Nāgapañcamī Vrata', in the Pañcamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the Śrī Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa consisting of fifty-thousand verses.

1.37.s:
.. sumaṃturuvāca .. ..
tathā bhādrapade māsi paṃcamyāṃ śraddhayānvitaḥ ..
athālekhya naro nāgānkṛṣṇavarṇādivarṇakaiḥ .. 1 ..
1.37.d:
॥ सुमंतुरुवाच ॥ ॥
तथा भाद्रपदे मासि पंचम्यां श्रद्धयान्वितः ॥
अथालेख्य नरो नागान्कृष्णवर्णादिवर्णकैः ॥ 1 ॥
1.37.m:
Sumaṃtu said:
Likewise, filled with faith, on the fifth day in the month of Bhādrapada,
a man should draw the serpents with black and other colours

1.37.s:
pūjayedgaṃdhapuṣpaiśca sarpiḥ pāyasaguggulaiḥ ..
tasya tuṣṭiṃ samāyāṃti pannagāstakṣakādayaḥ..2..
1.37.d:
पूजयेद्गंधपुष्पैश्च सर्पिः पायसगुग्गुलैः ॥
तस्य तुष्टिं समायांति पन्नगास्तक्षकादयः॥2॥
1.37.m:
and worship them with fragrant perfumes, flowers, ghee, milk-rice, and bdellium.
To him the serpents, Takṣaka and the rest, become pleased.

1.37.s:
āsaptamātkulāttasya na bhayaṃ nāgato bhavet..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena nāgānsaṃpūjayedbudhaḥ..3..
1.37.d:
आसप्तमात्कुलात्तस्य न भयं नागतो भवेत्॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन नागान्संपूजयेद्बुधः॥3॥
1.37.m:
Down to the seventh generation of his family there will be no fear of serpents.
Therefore, with every effort, a wise man should worship the serpents.

1.38.s:
.. .. sumaṃturuvāca .. ..
tathā cāśvayuje māsi pañcamyāṃ kurunaṃdana ..
kṛtvā kuśamayānnāgāngaṃdhāṃdyaiḥ saṃprapūjayet .. 1 ..
1.38.d:
॥ ॥ सुमंतुरुवाच ॥ ॥
तथा चाश्वयुजे मासि पञ्चम्यां कुरुनंदन ॥
कृत्वा कुशमयान्नागान्गंधांद्यैः संप्रपूजयेत् ॥ 1 ॥
1.38.m:
Sumaṃtu said:
Likewise, on the fifth day in the month of Āśvina, O delight of the Kurus,
having fashioned serpents made of kuśa grass, one should worship them with perfumes and the like,

1.38.s:
ghṛtodakābhyāṃ payasā snapayitvā viśāṃpate ..
godhūmaiḥ payasā svinnairbhakṣyaiśca vividhaistathā .. 2 ..
1.38.d:
घृतोदकाभ्यां पयसा स्नपयित्वा विशांपते ॥
गोधूमैः पयसा स्विन्नैर्भक्ष्यैश्च विविधैस्तथा ॥ 2 ॥
1.38.m:
having bathed them with ghee, water, and milk, O lord of the people,
with wheat boiled in milk and various edibles.

1.38.s:
yastvasyāṃ vidhivannāgāñchucirbhaktyā samanvitaḥ ..
pūjayetkuruśārdūla tasya śeṣādayo nṛpa ..3..
1.38.d:
यस्त्वस्यां विधिवन्नागाञ्छुचिर्भक्त्या समन्वितः ॥
पूजयेत्कुरुशार्दूल तस्य शेषादयो नृप ॥3॥
1.38.m:
The pure person who, endowed with devotion, according to the rule,
worships the serpents on this day, O tiger of the Kurus, for him Śeṣa and the other

1.38.s:
nāgāḥ prītā bhavaṃtīha śāṃtimāpnoti vā vibho ..
sa śāṃtilokamāsādya modate śāśvatīḥ samāḥ .. 4 ..
1.38.d:
नागाः प्रीता भवंतीह शांतिमाप्नोति वा विभो ॥
स शांतिलोकमासाद्य मोदते शाश्वतीः समाः ॥ 4 ॥
1.38.m:
serpents become pleased here, or he obtains peace, O lord.
Reaching the realm of peace, he rejoices for eternal years.

1.38.s:
ityeṣa kathito vīra pañcamīkalpa uttamaḥ .
yatrāyamucyate maṃtraḥ sarvasarpaniṣedhakaḥ .. 9..
1.38.d:
इत्येष कथितो वीर पञ्चमीकल्प उत्तमः ।
यत्रायमुच्यते मंत्रः सर्वसर्पनिषेधकः ॥ 9॥
1.38.m:
Thus has this supreme ritual procedure for the fifth day been declared, O hero,
wherein this mantra warding off all serpents is pronounced:

1.38.s:
oṃ kurukulle phaṭ svāhā...
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi paṃcamīkalpe samāptikathanaṃ nāmāṣṭatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..38.. ..cha..
1.38.d:
ओं कुरुकुल्ले फट् स्वाहा॥।
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि पंचमीकल्पे समाप्तिकथनं नामाष्टत्रिंशोऽध्यायः ॥38॥ ॥छ॥
1.38.m:
'Oṃ kurukulle phaṭ svāhā.'
Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter, named 'The Proclamation of the Conclusion', in the Ritual Procedure for the Fifth Day, in the Brāhmaparvan, in the Saṃhitā of fifty thousand verses of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.

1.39.s:
..sumaṃturuvāca.. ..
ṣaṣṭhyāṃ phalāśano rājanviśeṣātkārtike nṛpa ..
rājyacyuto viśeṣeṇa svaṃ rājyaṃ labhate'cirāt..1..
1.39.d:
॥सुमंतुरुवाच॥ ॥
षष्ठ्यां फलाशनो राजन्विशेषात्कार्तिके नृप ॥
राज्यच्युतो विशेषेण स्वं राज्यं लभतेऽचिरात्॥1॥
1.39.m:
Sumaṃtu said:
One who eats only fruit on the sixth day, O king, especially in the month of Kārtika, O ruler,
even if fallen from his kingdom, especially regains his own realm before long.

1.39.s:
ṣaṣṭhī tithirmahārāja sarvadā sarvakāmadā..
upoṣyā tu prayatnena sarvakālaṃ jayārthinā . . 2
1.39.d:
षष्ठी तिथिर्महाराज सर्वदा सर्वकामदा॥
उपोष्या तु प्रयत्नेन सर्वकालं जयार्थिना ॥ 2
1.39.m:
The sixth lunar day, O great king, always grants all desires;
it should be observed with fasting with great effort at all times by one desiring victory.

1.39.s:
kārttikeyasya dayitā eṣā ṣaṣṭhī mahātithiḥ .
devasenādhipatyaṃ hi prāptaṃ tasyāṃ mahātmanā . . 3
1.39.d:
कार्त्तिकेयस्य दयिता एषा षष्ठी महातिथिः ।
देवसेनाधिपत्यं हि प्राप्तं तस्यां महात्मना ॥ 3
1.39.m:
Beloved to Kārttikeya is this great lunar day, the sixth;
for on it command of the army of the gods was obtained by the great-souled one.

1.39.s:
asyāṃ hi śreyasā yukto yasmātskando bhavāgraṇīḥ .
tasmātṣaṣṭhyāṃ naktabhojī prāpnuyādīpsitaṃ sadā . . 4
1.39.d:
अस्यां हि श्रेयसा युक्तो यस्मात्स्कन्दो भवाग्रणीः ।
तस्मात्षष्ठ्यां नक्तभोजी प्राप्नुयादीप्सितं सदा ॥ 4
1.39.m:
Because on this day Skanda was endowed with splendour and became leader of the world,
therefore one who eats a nocturnal meal on the sixth day will always obtain what he desires.

1.39.s:
dattvārghyaṃ kārtikeyāya sthitvā vai dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ .
dadhnā ghṛtodakaiḥ puṣpairmantreṇānena suvrata . . 5
1.39.d:
दत्त्वार्घ्यं कार्तिकेयाय स्थित्वा वै दक्षिणामुखः ।
दध्ना घृतोदकैः पुष्पैर्मन्त्रेणानेन सुव्रत ॥ 5
1.39.m:
Having offered water-oblation to Kārttikeya, standing facing south,
with curds, ghee, water, and flowers, by this mantra, O observer of good vows:

1.39.s:
saptarṣidāraja skanda svāhāpatisamudbhava .
rudrāryamāgnija vibho gaṅgāgarbha namo'stu te . .
prīyatāṃ devasenānīḥ sampādayatu hṛdgatam . . 6
1.39.d:
सप्तर्षिदारज स्कन्द स्वाहापतिसमुद्भव ।
रुद्रार्यमाग्निज विभो गङ्गागर्भ नमोऽस्तु ते ॥
प्रीयतां देवसेनानीः सम्पादयतु हृद्गतम् ॥ 6
1.39.m:
'O Skanda born of the wives of the seven sages, produced from the husband of Svāhā,
born of Rudra, Aryaman, and Fire, O lord, embryo of the Gaṅgā, homage to you!
May the general of the gods' army be pleased, and may he fulfil what is in the heart!'

1.39.s:
dattvā viprāya cātmānnaṃ yaccānyadapi vidyate .
paścādbhuṅkte tvasau rātrau bhūmiṃ kṛtvā tu bhājanam . . 7
1.39.d:
दत्त्वा विप्राय चात्मान्नं यच्चान्यदपि विद्यते ।
पश्चाद्भुङ्क्ते त्वसौ रात्रौ भूमिं कृत्वा तु भाजनम् ॥ 7
1.39.m:
And having given his own food to a brāhmaṇa, and whatever else may exist,
he eats afterwards at night, using the ground as a plate.

1.39.s:
evaṃ ṣaṣṭhyāṃ vrataṃ snehātproktaṃ skandena yatnataḥ .
tannibodha mahārāja procyamānaṃ mayākhilam . . 8
1.39.d:
एवं षष्ठ्यां व्रतं स्नेहात्प्रोक्तं स्कन्देन यत्नतः ।
तन्निबोध महाराज प्रोच्यमानं मयाखिलम् ॥ 8
1.39.m:
Thus, out of affection, the votive observance on the sixth day was proclaimed with care by Skanda.
Learn that in its entirety, O great king, as it is being declared by me.

1.39.s:
ṣaṣṭhyāṃ yastu phalāhāro naktāhāro bhaviṣyati .
śuklākṛṣṇāsu niyato brahmacārī samāhitaḥ . . 9
1.39.d:
षष्ठ्यां यस्तु फलाहारो नक्ताहारो भविष्यति ।
शुक्लाकृष्णासु नियतो ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः ॥ 9
1.39.m:
He who consumes only fruits or takes only nocturnal meals on the sixth day,
during the bright and dark fortnights, restrained, celibate, and collected in mind,

1.39.s:
tasya siddhiṃ dhṛtiṃ tuṣṭiṃ rājyamāyurnirāmayam .
pāratrikaṃ caihikaṃ ca dadyātskando na saṃśayaḥ . . 1.39.10
1.39.d:
तस्य सिद्धिं धृतिं तुष्टिं राज्यमायुर्निरामयम् ।
पारत्रिकं चैहिकं च दद्यात्स्कन्दो न संशयः ॥ 1.39.10
1.39.m:
to him Skanda will grant success, fortitude, contentment, kingship, long life free of disease,
in the other world and in this world, without a doubt.

1.39.s:
yo hi naktopavāsaḥ syātsa naktena vratī bhavet .
iha vāmutra so'tyantaṃ labhate khyātimuttamām . .
svarge ca niyataṃ vāsaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 11
1.39.d:
यो हि नक्तोपवासः स्यात्स नक्तेन व्रती भवेत् ।
इह वामुत्र सोऽत्यन्तं लभते ख्यातिमुत्तमाम् ॥
स्वर्गे च नियतं वासं लभते नात्र संशयः ॥ 11

1.39.s:
iha cāgatya kālānte yathoktaphalabhāgbhavet .
devānāmapi vandyo'sau rājñāṃ rājā bhaviṣyati . . 12
1.39.d:
इह चागत्य कालान्ते यथोक्तफलभाग्भवेत् ।
देवानामपि वन्द्योऽसौ राज्ञां राजा भविष्यति ॥ 12
1.39.m:
And returning here at the end of time, he will share the proclaimed fruit;
he will be venerable even to the gods, and will become a king of kings.

1.39.s:
yaścāpi śṛṇuyātkalpaṃ ṣaṣṭhyāḥ kurukulodvaha .
tasya siddhistathā tuṣṭirdhṛtiḥ syātkhyātisambhavā . . 13
1.39.d:
यश्चापि शृणुयात्कल्पं षष्ठ्याः कुरुकुलोद्वह ।
तस्य सिद्धिस्तथा तुष्टिर्धृतिः स्यात्ख्यातिसम्भवा ॥ 13
1.39.m:
And whoever hears the ritual procedure for the sixth day, O upholder of the Kuru lineage,
for him there will be success, contentment, fortitude, and renown.

1.39.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārdhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi
ṣaṣṭhīkalpavarṇanaṃ nāma ekonacatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 39 .
kārtikeyavarṇanam
1.39.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि
षष्ठीकल्पवर्णनं नाम एकोनचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः । 39 ।
कार्तिकेयवर्णनम्
1.39.m:
Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, named 'The Description of the Ritual Procedure for the Sixth Day', in the Brāhmaparvan, in the Saṃhitā of fifty thousand verses of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
The description of Kārttikeya.

1.40.s:
śatānīka uvāca
aho vrataṃ mahatkaṣṭaṃ saṃśayo hṛdi vartate .
kārtikeyasya māhātmyaṃ śrutvā janma tathā dvija . . 1
1.40.d:
शतानीक उवाच
अहो व्रतं महत्कष्टं संशयो हृदि वर्तते ।
कार्तिकेयस्य माहात्म्यं श्रुत्वा जन्म तथा द्विज ॥ 1
1.40.m:
Śatānīka said:
Ah, this votive observance is very difficult! A doubt remains in my heart
upon hearing the majesty and the birth of Kārttikeya, O twice-born one.

1.40.s:
anekajanitasyeha kārttikeyasya suvrata .
māhātmyaṃ sumahadvipra kathametadvibhāvyate . . 2
1.40.d:
अनेकजनितस्येह कार्त्तिकेयस्य सुव्रत ।
माहात्म्यं सुमहद्विप्र कथमेतद्विभाव्यते ॥ 2
1.40.m:
For Kārttikeya, who was generated by many parents here, O observer of good vows,
how is this very great majesty explained, O brāhmaṇa?

1.40.s:
jātiḥ śreṣṭhā bhavedvīra uta karma bhavedvaram .
saṃśayastu mahānatra dṛṣṭvā me kṛttikāsutam . . 3
1.40.d:
जातिः श्रेष्ठा भवेद्वीर उत कर्म भवेद्वरम् ।
संशयस्तु महानत्र दृष्ट्वा मे कृत्तिकासुतम् ॥ 3
1.40.m:
Is caste superior, O hero, or is action better?
Great indeed is my doubt here on seeing the son of the Kṛttikās.

1.40.s:
etadvada viniścitya na yathā saṃśayo bhavet .
janmataḥ karmaṇaścaiva yajjvāyastad bravīhi me . . 4
1.40.d:
एतद्वद विनिश्चित्य न यथा संशयो भवेत् ।
जन्मतः कर्मणश्चैव यज्ज्वायस्तद् ब्रवीहि मे ॥ 4
1.40.m:
State this with certainty so that there will be no doubt;
tell me which of the two is greater: birth or action?

1.40.s:
sumanturuvāca
imamarthaṃ purā pṛṣṭo brahmā śiṣyairmanīṣibhiḥ .
yaduktaṃ tena teṣāṃ ca tatte vacmi nibodha me . . 5
1.40.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
इममर्थं पुरा पृष्टो ब्रह्मा शिष्यैर्मनीषिभिः ।
यदुक्तं तेन तेषां च तत्ते वच्मि निबोध मे ॥ 5

1.40.s:
surajyeṣṭhaṃ sukhāsīnamabhigamya maharṣayaḥ .
praṇamya ca mahābāho viśvāmitrasya vipratām . . 6
1.40.d:
सुरज्येष्ठं सुखासीनमभिगम्य महर्षयः ।
प्रणम्य च महाबाहो विश्वामित्रस्य विप्रताम् ॥ 6
1.40.m:
Having approached the eldest of gods sitting comfortably, the great sages,
having bowed down, O mighty-armed one, having seen the brāhmaṇa status of Viśvāmitra

1.40.s:
dṛṣṭvā vismayamāgatya kautūhalasamanvitāḥ .
bhaktiṃ śraddhāṃ purodhāya praṇamyānatakandharāḥ . . 7
1.40.d:
दृष्ट्वा विस्मयमागत्य कौतूहलसमन्विताः ।
भक्तिं श्रद्धां पुरोधाय प्रणम्यानतकन्धराः ॥ 7
1.40.m:
and struck with wonder, accompanied by curiosity,
placing devotion and faith foremost, having bowed with bent necks,

1.40.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
bho brahmannādakalpe hi brāhmaṇyaṃ brūhi kiṃ bhavet .
jātyadhyayanadehātmasaṃskārācārakarmaṇām1 . . 8
1.40.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
भो ब्रह्मन्नादकल्पे हि ब्राह्मण्यं ब्रूहि किं भवेत् ।
जात्यध्ययनदेहात्मसंस्काराचारकर्मणाम्1 ॥ 8
1.40.m:
the sages said:
O Brahmā, tell us: in the primal cosmic age, what is brāhmaṇa status?
Among caste, study, the body, the self, the saṃskāras, conduct, and action,

1.40.s:
bāhyābhyantarasāmānyaviśeṣā yadi kṛtrimāḥ .
manovākkarmaśārīrajātidravyaguṇātmakāḥ . . 9
1.40.d:
बाह्याभ्यन्तरसामान्यविशेषा यदि कृत्रिमाः ।
मनोवाक्कर्मशारीरजातिद्रव्यगुणात्मकाः ॥ 9
1.40.m:
if the external and internal, the universal and particular are artificial,
consisting of mind, speech, bodily action, caste, substance, and quality,

1.40.s:
santyaktavyāḥ prasiddhā ye jātibhedavidhāyinaḥ .
vastubhūtāḥ parokṣairvā pramāṇairna viniścitāḥ . . 1.40.10
1.40.d:
सन्त्यक्तव्याः प्रसिद्धा ये जातिभेदविधायिनः ।
वस्तुभूताः परोक्षैर्वा प्रमाणैर्न विनिश्चिताः ॥ 1.40.10
1.40.m:
and if those [distinctions] establishing caste differentiation that are renowned are to be rejected,
whether they are real things or not determined by unobservable instruments of knowledge,

1.40.s:
avyaktāgamasiddhaścejjātibhedavidhirnṛṇām .
vikalpo'yaṃ na puṣṇāti bhavataḥ śemuṣībalam . . 11
1.40.d:
अव्यक्तागमसिद्धश्चेज्जातिभेदविधिर्नृणाम् ।
विकल्पोऽयं न पुष्णाति भवतः शेमुषीबलम् ॥ 11
1.40.m:
and if the rule of caste differentiation among humans is established through an unmanifest tradition,
then this mental construction does not support the strength of your intellect.

1.40.s:
brahmovāca
evametanna sandeho yathā yūyaṃ vadanti1 ha .
śṛṇudhvaṃ yogino vākyaṃ satarkaṃ śiṣyaśreyase . . 12
1.40.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवमेतन्न सन्देहो यथा यूयं वदन्ति1 ह ।
शृणुध्वं योगिनो वाक्यं सतर्कं शिष्यश्रेयसे ॥ 12
1.40.m:
Brahmā said:
It is so, there is no doubt, just as you say.
Hear the statement of the yogin, accompanied by reason, for the welfare of the disciples.

1.40.s:
yogeśvara uvāca
pramāṇe hi prasiddhe tu bhinnārthaviṣaye yataḥ .
spaṣṭayogyārthaviṣayaṃ pratyakṣaṃ tāvadīkṣate . . 13
1.40.d:
योगेश्वर उवाच
प्रमाणे हि प्रसिद्धे तु भिन्नार्थविषये यतः ।
स्पष्टयोग्यार्थविषयं प्रत्यक्षं तावदीक्षते ॥ 13
1.40.m:
The Lord of Yoga said:
Indeed, when two instruments of knowledge are well known, having different objects of reference,
direct perception observes an object that is manifest and suitable.

1.40.s:
samānyātīndriyagrāhī siddhānto'bhyupagamyate .
sa eva bhagavānekaṃ pramāṇamiti cenna tat . . 14
1.40.d:
समान्यातीन्द्रियग्राही सिद्धान्तोऽभ्युपगम्यते ।
स एव भगवानेकं प्रमाणमिति चेन्न तत् ॥ 14
1.40.m:
A doctrine that grasps the universal and the imperceptible is accepted;
if it is said that the Blessed One alone is the sole instrument of knowledge, that is not so.

1.40.s:
yasmādvividhame tatte saṅkaṭaṃ bhadra vartate .
vedasya pauruṣeyatvaṃ nityajātisamarthakam . . 15
1.40.d:
यस्माद्विविधमे तत्ते सङ्कटं भद्र वर्तते ।
वेदस्य पौरुषेयत्वं नित्यजातिसमर्थकम् ॥ 15
1.40.m:
Because this dilemma of yours is diverse, O gentle one:
the human authorship of the Veda would support an eternal caste;

1.40.s:
kāryā viśeṣā vedoktā na yuktamakṛtaṃ vacaḥ .
tālvādikaraṇānāṃ ca vyāpārānantaraṃ śruteḥ . . 16
1.40.d:
कार्या विशेषा वेदोक्ता न युक्तमकृतं वचः ।
ताल्वादिकरणानां च व्यापारानन्तरं श्रुतेः ॥ 16
1.40.m:
the particulars stated in the Veda are effects; it is not proper that the word is unmade,
because hearing occurs immediately after the operation of vocal organs such as the palate,

1.40.s:
vyāpārātparatastasya prāgabhāvaviśeṣataḥ .
tadbhāvānuvidhāyitvamanvayavyatiraketaḥ . . 17
1.40.d:
व्यापारात्परतस्तस्य प्रागभावविशेषतः ।
तद्भावानुविधायित्वमन्वयव्यतिरकेतः ॥ 17
1.40.m:
subsequent to that operation, because of the distinction of prior non-existence,
and because of conforming to its existence through positive and negative concomitance.

1.40.s:
tasmāddhūmāgnivadvārthaphalabhāvo'vatiṣṭhate .
na ca vyāpāravacasoranyathānupapattitaḥ . . 18
1.40.d:
तस्माद्धूमाग्निवद्वार्थफलभावोऽवतिष्ठते ।
न च व्यापारवचसोरन्यथानुपपत्तितः ॥ 18
1.40.m: Therefore, the relation between word, meaning, and result stands established like smoke and fire; / nor is it otherwise, because the activity and the speech cannot be accounted for without it.

1.40.s:
puruṣānugatā jātirbrāhmaṇatvādikāsti cet .
dvivarṇajātibhedena pratyākṣārthopalakṣaṇāt . . 19
1.40.d:
पुरुषानुगता जातिर्ब्राह्मणत्वादिकास्ति चेत् ।
द्विवर्णजातिभेदेन प्रत्याक्षार्थोपलक्षणात् ॥ 19
1.40.m: If a caste such as brahminhood were inherent in a man / through the division of castes and classes, because perceivable things are observed,

1.40.s:
govargamadhyaṃ ca gato yathāśvo nirdhāryate jñaiḥ suvicakṣaṇatvāt .
manuṣyabhāvādaviśiṣyamāṇastadvaddvijaḥ śūdragaṇānna bhinnaḥ . . 1.40.20
1.40.d:
गोवर्गमध्यं च गतो यथाश्वो निर्धार्यते ज्ञैः सुविचक्षणत्वात् ।
मनुष्यभावादविशिष्यमाणस्तद्वद्द्विजः शूद्रगणान्न भिन्नः ॥ 1.40.20
1.40.m: just as a horse entering among a herd of cattle is distinguished by the knowledgeable on account of their great discernment, / in the same way a twice-born man, not being distinguished from the human state, is not different from a company of śūdras.

1.40.s:
manuṣyajāterna paro viśeṣo yaḥ kalpyate sarvanarānuyāyī .
saṃskārayuktā hi kriyāviśiṣṭā dvijanmanāṃ śūdravivekahetuḥ . . 21
1.40.d:
मनुष्यजातेर्न परो विशेषो यः कल्प्यते सर्वनरानुयायी ।
संस्कारयुक्ता हि क्रियाविशिष्टा द्विजन्मनां शूद्रविवेकहेतुः ॥ 21
1.40.m: There is no higher distinction of the human species that is conceived as applying to all men; / for ritual action accompanied by consecrations is the cause of distinguishing the twice-born from a śūdra.

1.40.s:
jīvo'pi brāhmaṇaḥ prokto yairatattvajñamānavaiḥ .
prabhraṣṭabrāhmaṇatvāste jāyante viprasaṅgataḥ . . 22
1.40.d:
जीवोऽपि ब्राह्मणः प्रोक्तो यैरतत्त्वज्ञमानवैः ।
प्रभ्रष्टब्राह्मणत्वास्ते जायन्ते विप्रसङ्गतः ॥ 22
1.40.m: Those ignorant men by whom even the individual soul is declared to be a brahmin / have fallen from brahminhood; they are born merely from association with brahmins.

1.40.s:
jarājanmāntarakleśaduṣṭagrāhakulākulam .
nara tiryagasacchūdra yoniduḥkhormisaṃkaṭam .. 23
1.40.d:
जराजन्मान्तरक्लेशदुष्टग्राहकुलाकुलम् ।
नर तिर्यगसच्छूद्र योनिदुःखोर्मिसंकटम् ॥ 23
1.40.m: Turbulent with a host of vicious sea-monsters—the afflictions of old age and other births—, / distressed by the waves of suffering in the wombs of humans, beasts, and base śūdras,

1.40.s:
dausthityarogaśokārtijanāvartasamanvitam .
śvānuśūkaracāṇḍālakṛmikūrmādikāyakam . . 24
1.40.d:
दौस्थित्यरोगशोकार्तिजनावर्तसमन्वितम् ।
श्वानुशूकरचाण्डालकृमिकूर्मादिकायकम् ॥ 24
1.40.m: filled with the whirlpools of people afflicted by destitution, disease, and sorrow, / possessing bodies such as those of dogs, pigs, caṇḍālas, worms, and turtles,

1.40.s:
saṃsārasāgaraṃ ghoraṃ magnaḥ khalu pariplavan .
bhūripāpabharākrāntaḥ sa jīvo brāhmaṇaḥ katham . . 25
1.40.d:
संसारसागरं घोरं मग्नः खलु परिप्लवन् ।
भूरिपापभराक्रान्तः स जीवो ब्राह्मणः कथम् ॥ 25
1.40.m: submerged and drifting in the terrifying ocean of saṃsāra, / overwhelmed by a heavy burden of sin—how can that soul be a brahmin?

1.40.s:
brahmovāca
saptavyādhakathā viprā manunā parikīrtitāḥ .
taṃ niśamya yaduśreṣṭha nityaṃ jātipadaṃ tyajet . . 26
1.40.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सप्तव्याधकथा विप्रा मनुना परिकीर्तिताः ।
तं निशम्य यदुश्रेष्ठ नित्यं जातिपदं त्यजेत् ॥ 26
1.40.m:
Brahmā said:
The story of the seven hunters was recounted to the brahmins by Manu. / Having heard it, O best of the Yadus, one should constantly renounce the status of caste.

1.40.s:
saptavyādhā daśārṇeṣu1 mṛgāḥ kālañjare girau .
cakravākāḥ sariddvīpe haṃsāḥ sarasi mānase . . 27
1.40.d:
सप्तव्याधा दशार्णेषु1 मृगाः कालञ्जरे गिरौ ।
चक्रवाकाः सरिद्द्वीपे हंसाः सरसि मानसे ॥ 27
1.40.m: Seven hunters in Daśārṇa, deer on Mount Kālañjara, / cakravāka birds on a river island, swans on Lake Mānasa—

1.40.s:
te'pi jātāḥ kurukṣetre brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ.
prasthitā dīrghamadhvānaṃ mṛyaṃ kimavasīdatha . . 28
1.40.d:
तेऽपि जाताः कुरुक्षेत्रे ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः।
प्रस्थिता दीर्घमध्वानं मृयं किमवसीदथ ॥ 28
1.40.m: they too were born in Kurukṣetra as brahmins who had mastered the Vedas. / Having set out on the long road, why do you despair when dying?

1.40.s: tasmānna jīve brāhmaṇyaṃ paśyāmo hi kathañcana . . 29
1.40.d: तस्मान्न जीवे ब्राह्मण्यं पश्यामो हि कथञ्चन ॥ 29
1.40.m: Therefore, we certainly do not see brahminhood in the soul in any way.

1.40.s:
śastrādimadbhārgavajātiyukto gajāśvagojoṣṭrakharādikānām .
śaktyā kṛto hyaṅgajavarṇadharmairbhedaḥ sphuṭaṃ lakṣaṇato'tra yadvat . . 1.40.30
1.40.d:
शस्त्रादिमद्भार्गवजातियुक्तो गजाश्वगोजोष्ट्रखरादिकानाम् ।
शक्त्या कृतो ह्यङ्गजवर्णधर्मैर्भेदः स्फुटं लक्षणतोऽत्र यद्वत् ॥ 1.40.30
1.40.m: Just as the division among elephants, horses, cattle, camels, donkeys, and the like is made by their capacities, / along with the characteristics and traits born of their limbs, and is clearly distinguished by marks here,

1.40.s:
taduttarānnaiva vikartanīyā brāhmaṇyajātinṛṣu nāsti kācit .
nityākṛtirnānupabhedarūpā yathā hi bhedaḥ paramo'tra sidhyet . .
sitādyasādhāraṇatulyarūpāḥ sanātano'ṅgeṣu na varṇabhedaḥ . . 31
1.40.d:
तदुत्तरान्नैव विकर्तनीया ब्राह्मण्यजातिनृषु नास्ति काचित् ।
नित्याकृतिर्नानुपभेदरूपा यथा हि भेदः परमोऽत्र सिध्येत् ॥
सिताद्यसाधारणतुल्यरूपाः सनातनोऽङ्गेषु न वर्णभेदः ॥ 31
1.40.m: hence there is no caste of brahminhood among men to be distinguished. / There is no permanent bodily form that is not subdivided, by which an absolute difference could be established here. / They are of equal form, lacking unique [physical traits] like white or other [complexions]; there is no eternal division of class in their bodies.

1.40.s:
